data.title: Compiler Explorer and the promise of URLs that last forever
data.author: anarazel
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了Compiler Explorer在URL处理上的演变过程及其面临的挑战。最初，整个编译器状态存储在URL中，导致链接过长。2014年引入Google的goo.gl短链接服务解决此问题，但2016年因Stack Overflow禁止短链接，团队改用godbolt.org/g/形式的重定向链接。2018年，URL长度限制问题再次出现，团队开发了自己的存储方案，使用S3和DynamoDB存储状态并生成短链接。由于goo.gl将在2025年关闭，团队正积极抢救旧链接，通过各种渠道收集并存储这些链接及其重定向目标。文章强调了对第三方服务的依赖风险，并指出只有完全掌控技术栈，才能真正实现“永久链接”的承诺。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：URL的持久性及其相关技术和经济问题

不同观点：
• **URL应永久持续的理想 vs. 现实的不可持续性**：
  - [nssnsjsjsjs] 认为URL持久存在需要永远的存储和维护，成本高昂，且不现实。
  - [s17n] 指出99%的URL实际上无法永久存在，建议技术应基于基础设施非永久性的假设进行构建。
  - [swyx] 质疑URL永久存在的可能性，指出域名维持需要成本，并提出URL的"死亡"可能是好事，筛选出有价值的内容。

• **个人应对URL失效的策略**：
  - [kccqzy] 分享了自己从依赖浏览器书签到发现链接失效后转向保存网页为PDF或文本的经历。
  - [creatonez] 讽刺了将链接短址服务当作数据库使用，随后又不得不从互联网角落找回链接的做法。

• **技术与服务的持久性与关闭原因**：
  - [layer8] 对Google关闭只读版本表示惊讶，猜测可能涉及法律风险。
  - [devrandoom] 批评Google过去的承诺不可信，将其与无实际价值的行为相比。
  - [jimmyl02] 强调免费第三方服务在关键基础设施上的风险，指出没有收入来源的项目最终难以维持。

• **具体案例讨论**：
  - [amiga386] 提到Google的Go Links服务关闭，指出即使是大型公司的服务也无法永久存在。
  - [2YwaZHXV] 询问是否可能让Google查询数据库找回短链接。
  - [sedatk] 指出purl.org在互联网档案馆的帮助下，四分之一个世纪后仍然有效。

• **未来展望与技术趋势**：
  - [olalonde] 提到由人类写作但由LLM辅助检查生成链接的文章，认为这是一种新趋势。
  - [wrs] 悲观地认为，除非有强大资金支持，否则技术服务如Compiler Explorer和godbolt.org也无法永久存在，并开玩笑提到未来可能由超级AI模型替代。

补充讨论：
- URL短址服务的弊端（如Goo.gl）及ArchiveTeam的合作项目（[mananaysiempre]）。
- 对"Cool URIs don't change"理念的坚持与实际操作中的困难（[shepmaster]）。
- 关于如何处理技术服务和基础设施非永久性的广泛讨论，涉及经济、法律及技术实现等多个层面。

争议焦点：
- URL是否应永久存在，以及是否有必要为此付出高昂成本。

44117722.article_content:
Compiler Explorer and the Promise of URLs That Last Forever
The history is this: back in the old days (2012), we used to store the entire
Compiler Explorer
state in the URL. That got unwieldy (who would have thought encoding an entire compiler state in a URL might get a bit long?), so we added support for Google’s link shortener
goo.gl
in March 2014. That meant short links were of the form
goo.gl/abc123
. Clicking a goo.gl link would eventually redirect you to the full URL link on our site, and we’d decode the state from the URL.
In 2016,
Stack Overflow
banned link shorteners because of how they cloak the actual destination of links. Abusers could post innocent goo.gl links that directed folks unwittingly to bad content. However, that meant our Compiler Explorer links were also affected. At the time, we had no intention of storing any user data, so we came up with a hack: we still used goo.gl, but we then rewrote the link we handed out to be
godbolt.org/g/abc123
(where the abc123 is the goo.gl unique ID). We then redirected any hits to
/g/abc123
to
goo.gl/abc123
, which then (finally) redirected back to godbolt.org with the appropriate state in the URL. If you’re keeping track, that’s three redirects to show you some assembly code. We were really committed to making things complicated. Later, we used Google’s API to avoid the redirection dance.
By 2018, the limitations of storing state in the URL started to bite. There’s a limit to how long a URL can be (and we’d already started compressing the data in the URL), so we needed a better solution. We finally implemented our own storage solution: we hash the input, save the state as a JSON document on
S3
under the hash, and then give out a shortened form of the hash as a
godbolt.org/z/hashbit
URL. We use
DynamoDB
to store the mapping of shortened hashes to the full paths (accounting for partial collisions, etc.). And, amusingly, we check the short link’s hash for rude words and add deliberate extra information into the document until we no longer get a rude word. Yes, we literally check if your shortened URL contains profanity. Because apparently even random hashes can’t be trusted to keep it clean. This led to
bug #1297
, which remains one of my favourite issues we’ve ever had to fix.
We still support the
godbolt.org/g/abc123
links, but… despite Google
solemnly promising
that “all existing links will continue to redirect to the intended destination,” it went read-only a few years back, and now they’re
finally sunsetting it
in August 2025. Here I was in 2014, thinking I was so clever using Google’s shortener. “It’ll be around forever!” I said. “Google never discontinues products!” I said. Er…
That means we’ll no longer be able to resolve goo.gl-based links! Which is, to use technical terminology, a bit pants. One of my founding principles is that Compiler Explorer links should last forever. I can’t do anything about the
really
legacy actual
goo.gl
links, but I can do something about the
godbolt.org/g/abc123
links!
Over the last few days, I’ve been scraping everywhere I can think of, collating the links I can find out in the wild, and compiling my own database of links
1
– and importantly, the URLs they redirect to. So far, I’ve found 12,000 links from scraping:
Google
(using their web search API)
GitHub
(using their API)
Our own (somewhat limited) web logs
The
archive.org
Stack Overflow data dumps
Archive.org’s own list of archived webpages
12,298 rescued links and counting - not bad for a few days of digital archaeology
We’re now
using the database in preference
to
goo.gl
internally, so I’m also keeping an eye on new “g” links that we don’t yet have.
Thanks to
Peter Cordes
for reminding us about this issue and
bringing it to our attention
2
.
If you have a secret cache of godbolt.org/g/abc123 links you have lying around, now’s the time to visit each of them! That will ensure they’re in my web logs and I’ll add them to the database. Otherwise, sadly, in August 2025 those links will stop working, joining the great digital graveyard alongside Flash games and GeoCities pages.
The Bigger Picture
This whole saga reinforces why I’m skeptical of relying on third-party services for critical infrastructure. Google’s URL shortener was supposed to be permanent. The redirect chains we built were clever workarounds that bought us time, but ultimately, the only way to truly keep a promise of “URLs that last forever” is to own the entire stack.
It’s been a fascinating archaeological dig through the internet, hunting down these legacy links like some sort of digital Indiana Jones, except instead of ancient artifacts I’m rescuing compiler flags and optimization examples. Each one represents someone’s attempt to share knowledge, ask a question, or demonstrate a concept. Preserving them feels like preserving a small piece of programming history.
So if you’ve got old Compiler Explorer links bookmarked somewhere, dust them off and give them a click. You’ll be helping preserve a litt

data.title: LLM codegen go brrr – Parallelization with Git worktrees and tmux
data.author: skeptrune
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过AI代理和并行化任务提高开发效率的可行性和成本效益

不同观点：
• [hboon] 提出使用AI进行开发时，成本较高（每个任务$2），并质疑如何通过$0.10完成任务。他还提到了使用tmux和手动pull代码的方式，同时对git worktrees的实际优势表示疑问。
• [danielbln] 认为这种方法主要提高了零一万物开发功能的机会，但自己在与LLM迭代代码时需要多次交互，难以并行化。视觉UI迭代和TDD可能从中受益，但对多轮迭代感到困扰。
• [gct] 批评这种方法浪费资源，认为同时运行四个AI而忽略其中三个是低效的，并对当前软件开发效率低下表示不满。
• [diogolsq] 强调了代码质量和清理AI生成代码的重要性，认为节省时间的做法可能导致后期需要花费更多时间进行清理和修复，因此对这种方法的实际效率持怀疑态度。
• [dgunay] 倾向于通过优化每个任务的延迟和并行化多个不同任务来提高整体产出，而不是关注单个任务的速度。他强调文档和工具的改进，以使AI更加自给自足，从而减少人类干预。
• [lmeyerov] 认为通过减少注意力消耗和最大化吞吐量是关键，倾向于通过多任务并行来提高效率，并希望有工具能自动化fork/join并行任务。
• [peterkelly] 提出如果AI编码代理足够好，可以直接通过并行执行多次任务来简化流程。
• [sagarpatil] 避免使用自己的API密钥，选择使用远程代理和按消息收费的服务，以避免本地运行模型时的高成本。
• [mrbonner] 认为使用类似Cline的检查点功能进行任务恢复和重试可能更为有效，且能保留之前的上下文。
• [CraigJPerry] 认为当前的单任务单代理模式不够高效，希望通过多个代理协作完成一个任务，并分享了自己使用不同代理角色和工具的经验。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在通过并行化AI任务来提高开发效率的可行性和成本效益上。一方面，有人认为这种方法浪费资源且成本高昂，另一方面，有人认为可以通过合理的任务分配和工具改进实现更高的整体产出。
• 不同开发者对AI生成代码的质量和后期清理的必要性有不同看法，部分人认为这种方法可能导致代码质量下降，增加后期维护成本。
• 一些开发者分享了自己的具体工作流和工具使用经验，如使用tmux、git worktrees、远程代理服务等，提供了实际操作中的具体见解和建议。

总的来说，讨论围绕着如何在开发过程中有效利用AI代理进行任务并行化，以提高效率和产出，同时控制成本和保证代码质量。

• [diogolsq] 强调了代码质量和清理AI生成代码的重要性，认为节省时间的做法可能导致后期需要花费更多时间进行清理和修复，因此对这种方法的实际效率持怀疑态度。
• [dgunay] 倾向于通过优化每个任务的延迟和并行化多个不同任务来提高整体产出，而不是关注单个任务的速度。他强调文档和工具的改进，以使AI更加自给自足，从而减少人类干预。
• [lmeyerov] 认为通过减少注意力消耗和最大化吞吐量是关键，倾向于通过多任务并行来提高效率，并希望有工具能自动化fork/join并行任务。
• [peterkelly] 提出如果AI编码代理足够好，可以直接通过并行执行多次任务来简化流程。
• [sagarpatil] 避免使用自己的API密钥，选择使用远程代理和按消息收费的服务，以避免本地运行模型时的高成本。
• [mrbonner] 认为使用类似Cline的检查点功能进行任务恢复和重试可能更为有效，且能保留之前的上下文。
• [CraigJPerry] 认为当前的单任务单代理模式不够高效，希望通过多个代理协作完成一个任务，并分享了自己使用不同代理角色和工具的经验。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要集中在通过并行化AI任务来提高开发效率的可行性和成本效益上。一方面，有人认为这种方法浪费资源且成本高昂，另一方面，有人认为可以通过合理的任务分配和工具改进实现更高的整体产出。
• 不同开发者对AI生成代码的质量和后期清理的必要性有不同看法，部分人认为这种方法可能导致代码质量下降，增加后期维护成本。
• 一些开发者分享了自己的具体工作流和工具使用经验，如使用tmux、git worktrees、远程代理服务等，提供了实际操作中的具体见解和建议。

总的来说，讨论围绕着如何在开发过程中有效利用AI代理进行任务并行化，以提高效率和产出，同时控制成本和保证代码质量。

data.author: bveiseh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MindFort产品的功能、安全性、使用方式及独特性

不同观点：
• mparis：对产品的发布表示祝贺，并对产品的一次性成功特性表示赞赏。同时提出了两个问题：1) 关于产品如何处理10万页的评估，是否会影响其他用户的使用；2) 如果系统检测到漏洞，是否会因为权限提升而导致危险行为。

• HocusLocus：以幽默的方式表达了对渗透测试工具潜在风险的担忧，可能暗示对AI工具的不可控性有所保留。

• robszumski：询问产品的具体使用方式，例如是否需要将工具指向公开可用的web应用，或者是否可以在本地开发环境中运行。

• sumanyusharma：提出三个技术性问题：1) 代理如何判断疑似问题为有效漏洞，以及相关的误报/漏报率；2) 客户代码和数据在各个阶段如何隔离和加密；3) 代理是否会自动应用补丁，以及如何与CI/CD集成以防止回归。

• handfuloflight：询问产品的定价细节。

• blibble：关注产品的道德使用问题，具体询问如何确保对目标网站的测试是经过同意的。

• gyanchawdhary：将MindFort与其他类似平台（xbow.com, shinobi.security, gecko.security, zeropath.com）进行比较，询问其独特之处。

• lazyninja987：询问代理是否需要访问源代码以生成攻击策略，以及如何处理黑盒测试和已公开的漏洞列表的匹配问题，表明其对LLM和ML技术不太熟悉。

补充讨论：
• 用户对产品的技术细节和安全性表现出较高的关注，包括对漏洞检测后的行为控制、代码和数据的隔离加密、以及自动补丁应用的流程。
• 产品的使用场景和定价也是用户关心的重点，特别是如何在不同环境中使用（公开web应用、本地开发环境）以及具体的收费模式。
• 用户还关注产品的独特性和竞争优势，尤其是与其他类似平台的比较。
• 道德使用问题也被提及，反映出用户对渗透测试工具可能带来的伦理风险的关注。

data.title: Deepseek R1-0528
data.author: error404x
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了DeepSeek-R1-0528模型的基本信息。该模型拥有6850亿参数，支持多种张量类型，包括BF16、F8_E4M3和F32。目前，该模型尚未被任何推理提供商部署，且最近一次更新是在33分钟前。模型相关文件包括1个微调版本和包含该模型的9个项目的集合。用户可以请求提供商支持以部署此模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DeepSeek-R1-0528模型的发布及其性能、可用性、应用场景和技术要求

不同观点：
• [积极评价性能与开源] jacob019和willchen对DeepSeek-R1-0528的发布表示兴奋，尤其是其性能可媲美OpenAI的模型，并且是完全开源的。willchen特别提到这种不经大肆宣传的更新带来了显著的改进。
• [关注推理能力] mickey475778对DeepSeek-R1-0528的推理能力，尤其是代码生成方面的表现感到兴奋，并提到其可能采用了链式思维（CoT）方法。他们还对该模型在处理新颖代码挑战时的表现表示关注。
• [信息不足] acheong08指出关于该模型的信息不足，期待看到基准测试结果。jacob019也提到缺乏模型卡和发布说明等问题。
• [硬件要求] transcriptase和htrp对普通用户如何使用该模型表示关注，尤其是其硬件要求。htrp具体指出需要至少8个h100 80s的硬件支持。
• [本地LLM应用] karencarits询问人们使用本地LLM的实际用例，并表示自己在寻找有用应用方面遇到困难。

data.title: Mathematical Fiction
data.author: the-mitr
data.article_summary: 《数学虚构作品主页》是由亚历克斯·卡斯曼（Alex Kasman）创建并维护的一个数据库，包含超过一千部的涉及数学或数学家的短篇故事、戏剧、小说、电影和漫画书。该网站旨在收集所有与数学相关的虚构作品信息，用户可以按作者、标题或出版日期浏览整个列表，也可根据类型、主题或媒介进行筛选。此外，网站还提供新近添加或修改的条目列表以及站长的个人推荐。用户可以提出意见或建议，还可阅读关于数学虚构作品的文章以获取更多信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数学与 fiction 的结合，包括数学在小说、诗歌等文学作品中的表现形式及其影响力。

不同观点：
• [Syzygies] 认为《美丽心灵》中的数学情节是为了配合剧情需要而虚构的，指出电影中展示的数学与现实不符，且数学家不擅长创作虚构故事，除撰写科研资助提案之外。
• [omoikane] 介绍了一部日本轻小说《浜村渚の計算ノート》（Hamamura Nagisa's Calculation Notes），该小说通过数学解决犯罪谜题，涵盖了从简单分数到费马大定理等各种数学主题，适合喜欢数学的读者。
• [CurtMonash] 提到了Robert Heinlein的《...And He Built a Crooked House》，认为该小说既有趣又包含数学元素，并分享了小说的链接。此外，他还提到了经典科幻小说中的“数学反事实”问题，建议可以考虑数学诗歌作为替代。
• [A_D_E_P_T] 对推荐的书单做出了回应，特别提到Greg Egan和David Zindell的作品，认为后者的小说《Neverness》是极被低估的科幻佳作。
• [jhallenworld] 推荐了Rudy Rucker的作品，尤其是小说《Wetware》中提到的“merge”药物，这种药物能够让用户与宇宙融为一体。
• [throwaway81523] 补充了一些数学相关的小说和作者，如Jeffrey Kegler、Norbert Wiener、Martin Gardner等，并提到《Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality》虽然不完全是数学小说，但包含了统计学和博弈论的元素。
• [kjellsbells] 认为Dante的《神曲》中对超球面的解释值得提及，并分享了一篇相关的研究文章。

补充讨论：
• [pat_springleaf] 表示对推荐列表中的一些作品不熟悉，询问是否有特别推荐的小说。
• [mmooss] 提到Tom Stoppard的戏剧《Leopoldstadt》中有一位数学家角色Ludwig，他通过数学问题测试孩子们是否为天才，并描述了Ludwig的提问方式。
• [zabzonk] 回忆起大约50年前阅读的一部关于数学家在张量空间中驾驶飞船的小说，但记不起书名和作者。
• [BeetleB] 对《Foundation》是否应列入推荐名单提出质疑，认为如果《Foundation》被包括在内，那么还有许多其他作品也应被列入。
• [mjcohen] 提到Clifton Fadiman编辑的两本数学 fiction 选集《Fantasia Mathematica》和《The Mathematical Magpie》，并表示自己喜欢这两本书。

争议焦点：
• 数学 fiction 作品的真实性与虚构性之间的平衡，如《美丽心灵》中的虚构数学情节。
• 哪些作品应被列入数学 fiction 的推荐名单，例如《Foundation》是否合适。

总结：讨论围绕数学与 fiction 的结合展开，参与者分享了各种包含数学元素的小说、戏剧和诗歌，并对某些作品的真实性和推荐价值进行了辩论。

• [throwaway81523] 补充了一些数学相关的小说和作者，如Jeffrey Kegler、Norbert Wiener、Martin Gardner等，并提到《Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality》虽然不完全是数学小说，但包含了统计学和博弈论的元素。
• [kjellsbells] 认为Dante的《神曲》中对超球面的解释值得提及，并分享了一篇相关的研究文章。

补充讨论：
• [pat_springleaf] 表示对推荐列表中的一些作品不熟悉，询问是否有特别推荐的小说。
• [mmooss] 提到Tom Stoppard的戏剧《Leopoldstadt》中有一位数学家角色Ludwig，他通过数学问题测试孩子们是否为天才，并描述了Ludwig的提问方式。
• [zabzonk] 回忆起大约50年前阅读的一部关于数学家在张量空间中驾驶飞船的小说，但记不起书名和作者。
• [BeetleB] 对《Foundation》是否应列入推荐名单提出质疑，认为如果《Foundation》被包括在内，那么还有许多其他作品也应被列入。
• [mjcohen] 提到Clifton Fadiman编辑的两本数学 fiction 选集《Fantasia Mathematica》和《The Mathematical Magpie》，并表示自己喜欢这两本书。

争议焦点：
• 数学 fiction 作品的真实性与虚构性之间的平衡，如《美丽心灵》中的虚构数学情节。
• 哪些作品应被列入数学 fiction 的推荐名单，例如《Foundation》是否合适。

data.title: Japan Post launches 'digital address' system
data.author: jmsflknr
data.article_summary: 日本邮政推出了一套“数字地址”系统，用户可以通过输入由数字和字母组成的七位组合代码，在网购等网站上自动显示其地址。该系统通过日本邮政的Yu ID会员服务进行注册，即使实际地址发生变化，数字地址仍保持不变，只需提交地址变更通知即可更新。乐天等电商企业正考虑采用这一系统，日本邮政计划用十年时间推动其广泛应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于不同国家邮政地址系统和数字化邮政地址的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持数字化地址的观点**：
   - [kazinator] 认为数字化地址可以减少垃圾邮件问题，并建议通过短期、可丢弃的数字地址来增强隐私保护，防止地址被滥用。
   - [brynet] 提到虚拟地址即使在实际地址改变的情况下仍然保持不变，增加了便利性。

• **对数字化地址的隐私和安全担忧**：
   - [politelemon] 担心虚拟地址若不变，可能会影响隐私和安全。
   - [donnachangstein] 提到在日本，数字化交付仍需使用传统的印章签名，质疑其现代化程度。

• **对地址系统长度的看法**：
   - [isk517] 对7位数的地址系统表示担忧，认为可能不够长远，但理解其结合字母和数字的组合方式。
   - [nan60] 认为日本地址复杂且较长，数字化地址系统在日本特别有意义。

• **对现有地址系统的比较**：
   - [KoolKat23] 介绍了爱尔兰的Eircode系统，指出其在日常生活中很常见，但邮政服务并不主要依赖该系统。
   - [halpow] 解释了日本的门牌号系统，强调其复杂性，需要结合地图寻找地址。

• **对技术实现和误操作的讨论**：
   - [PerilousD] 担心数字化地址输入错误会导致邮件误发，并提到自己处理垃圾邮件的经历。

   - [762236] 提到全球广泛使用的Plus码系统，并指出其在多个国家的交付应用。

• 讨论中多次引用和比较了不同国家的地址系统，如爱尔兰和日本，并探讨了数字化地址在实际应用中的优缺点。
• 部分评论涉及到对技术实现细节的探讨，如虚拟地址的持久性和多地址处理问题。

Japan Post launches 'digital address' system
Under the "digital address" system launched by Japan Post, users can input seven-digit combinations of numbers and letters on online shopping and other websites, and their addresses will automatically appear on the sites.

May 27, 2025
Japan Post said Monday that it has launched a "digital address" system that links seven-digit combinations of numbers and letters to physical addresses.
Under the system, users can input these seven-digit codes on online shopping websites, and their addresses will automatically appear on the sites.
People can obtain digital addresses by registering with Japan Post's Yu ID membership service. Their digital addresses will not change even if their physical addresses change. Their new addresses will be linked to the codes if they submit notices of address changes.
With Japan Post opening up a system for obtaining address information using the codes, e-commerce giant Rakuten and others are considering adopting it.
Japan Post plans to spend about a decade to promote broad adoption of the new system.

data.title: Building interactive web pages with Guile Hoot
data.author: e12e
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Guile Hoot（一种Scheme到WebAssembly编译器）创建交互式网页。通过Wasm垃圾回收（Wasm GC），Wasm现在可以调用DOM API，从而实现类似JavaScript的交互功能。文章展示了如何从简单的"Hello, world"示例开始，逐步构建更复杂的类似React的应用程序。Hoot 0.2.0引入了外部函数接口（FFI），允许Scheme直接调用JavaScript函数，从而减少对JavaScript代码的依赖。文中详细说明了如何使用`define-foreign`声明Wasm导入，并通过JavaScript引导Wasm程序。最终，通过Scheme的数据结构实现HTML渲染，无需像React的JSX那样的额外语言。这展示了Scheme在浏览器环境中强大的表现力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Guile Hoot和Scheme语言在WebAssembly（Wasm）领域中的潜力和应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• [neilv] 认为Guile Hoot的潜力需要通过实际项目和经验报告来证明。他提到，低层次的展示可能无法完全体现其复杂性和优势，类似于Svelte的简单示例无法展示其内部复杂性。他还指出，Scheme的吸引力可能需要通过某个杀手级应用来证明，比如利用第一类延续来简化Web表单UI，或者通过Scheme实现丰富的元数据模型，从而比Java更具优势。

• [sshine] 对Hoot表示了浓厚的兴趣，并提到他通过Rust使用了一些Wasm，但DOM操作需要通过web-sys JS shim来处理。他认为Leptos和Dioxus等框架虽然好，但学习曲线陡峭。他强调Hoot的Wasm自宿主能力使其不仅适用于交互式网页，还可以用于构建任意运行时。他还提到Spritely研究所提供的Goblins工具，可以用于构建分布式运行时。

• [thesuperbigfrog] 只是简单地指出帖子的时间是2023年，没有深入讨论技术细节。

• [evanjrowley] 提到通过System Crafters视频了解了Guile Hoot，并表示希望在不久的将来能使用它。

补充讨论：
• [neilv] 提到尽管在理论上JavaScript可以被强制用于大多数任务，但一个优雅的解决方案可能会使Scheme更具吸引力。

• [sshine] 强调了Hoot有可能使Wasm变得更加易于访问，特别是对于那些不以Scheme为主要语言的人，Scheme仍然是构建编译器的优秀语言。他还提到了Spritely研究所的其他工具（如Goblins），这些工具可以用于构建分布式运行时，进一步扩展了Hoot的应用场景。

争议焦点：目前没有明显的争议，但[neilv]对Guile Hoot的实际应用效果持谨慎乐观态度，认为需要实际项目来验证其潜力，而[sshine]则对Hoot的未来充满期待，并提到了其在构建分布式运行时方面的潜力。

Building interactive web pages with Guile Hoot
Dave Thompson â
November 30, 2023
A question we frequently hear in discussions about WebAssembly (Wasm)
is:
"Can Wasm call the DOM (Document Object Model) API?"
The answer is:
Yes, thanks to
Wasm Garbage
Collection
!
In this post, we will use
Guile Hoot
(our Scheme to Wasm
compiler) to demonstrate how a language that compiles to Wasm GC can
be used to implement the kind of interactivity we're used to
implementing with JavaScript.  We'll start very simple and build up to
something that resembles a
React
-like
application.
In our
previous post about running Scheme in the
browser
, we had to use quite
a lot of JavaScript code to call Scheme procedures (functions), render
the user interface, and handle user input. However, today we're
pleased to announce that those days are behind us; Hoot 0.2.0,
released today
, now includes a
foreign function interface (FFI) for calling JavaScript from Scheme.
In other words, the vast majority of code in a Hoot application can
now be written directly in Scheme!
Hello, world!
Let's start with a "Hello, world" application that simply adds a text
node to the document body.

document-body

The
define-foreign
syntax declares a Wasm import with a given
signature that is bound to a Scheme variable.  In this example, we'd
like access to
document.body
,
document.createTextNode
, and
element.appendChild
.
Each import has a two-part name, which correspond to the strings in
the
define-foreign
expressions above.  Imported functions have a
signature specifying the parameter and result types.
WebAssembly follows the
capability security
model
(and
if you know us, you know
we're big fans
).  Wasm modules
act as guests within a host environment â in our case, the host is the
browser.  By default, a Wasm module has no access to functions that
interact with its host.  The Wasm guest must be granted explicit
permission by its host to be able to, for example, add DOM elements to
a web page.
The way capabilities work in Wasm is as follows:
The Wasm module declares a set of imports.
When the Wasm module is
instantiated
,
the host maps the import names to concrete implementations.
So,
define-foreign
merely
declares
the module's need for a
particular function import; it does
not
bind to a particular
function on the host.  The Wasm guest cannot grant capabilities unto
itself.
The host environment in the browser is the JavaScript engine, so we
must use JavaScript to bootstrap our Wasm program.  To do so, we
instantiate the Wasm module and pass along the implementations for the
declared imports.  The import names in JavaScript match up to the
import names in the Wasm module.  For our "Hello, world" example, that
code looks like this:

• [sshine] 强调了Hoot有可能使Wasm变得更加易于访问，特别是对于那些不以Scheme为主要语言的人，Scheme仍然是构建编译器的优秀语言。他还提到了Spritely研究所的其他工具（如Goblins），这些工具可以用于构建分布式运行时，进一步扩展了Hoot的应用场景。

争议焦点：目前没有明显的争议，但[neilv]对Guile Hoot的实际应用效果持谨慎乐观态度，认为需要实际项目来验证其潜力，而[sshine]则对Hoot的未来充满期待，并提到了其在构建分布式运行时方面的潜力。

data.title: Homo erectus from the seabed, new archaeological discoveries in Indonesia
data.author: palmfacehn
data.article_summary: 考古学家在印尼爪哇海岸发现了14万年前直立人（Homo erectus）的化石，为研究其生活环境提供了新视角。这些化石是在马都拉海峡海床中发现的，包括36种脊椎动物的化石，其中有两块直立人头骨碎片。此前认为爪哇岛的直立人长期处于隔离状态，但新发现表明，他们曾在巽他古陆（Sundaland）的低地活动，并通过主要河流扩散。化石显示直立人猎杀健康的牛科动物，并可能与其他亚洲大陆的人类物种有过接触或基因交流。该研究由莱顿大学和多国专家合作完成，成果发表于《第四纪环境与人类》期刊，化石目前保存在印尼万隆地质博物馆。

44093845.article_content:
Archaeological finds off the coast of Java, Indonesia provide insight into the world of Homo erectus, 140,000 years ago. Skull fragments and other fossil remains provide a unique picture of how and where these early humans lived, says Leiden archaeologist Harold Berghuis.
During dredging operations in the Madura Strait, archaeologists found the fossilised remains of 36 vertebrate species. This is the first discovery of fossils from the seabed between the Indonesian islands. This area, called Sundaland, was once a vast lowland. Among the finds are two skull fragments of Homo erectus. Together, the finds provide a unique image of a prehistoric ecosystem and the position of Homo erectus in this ecosystem.
New insights
Fossil remains of Homo erectus have previously been found on the island of Java, the most famous of which are skulls from sites such as Trinil, Sangiran and Ngandong. Until today, researchers thought that Homo erectus had lived for long in isolation on Java. The new finds show that the Javanese Homo erectus dispersed over the surrounding lowlands of Sundaland during periods with lower sea levels. The species probably spread along the major rivers. ‘Here they had water, shellfish, fish, edible plants, seeds and fruit all year round’, says Berghuis. ‘We already knew that Homo erectus collected river shells. Among our new finds are cut marks on the bones of water turtles and large numbers of broken bovid bones, which point to hunting and consumption of bone marrow.’
The area where the fossils were found ('sand extraction area')
The new finds show that the Sundaland Homo erectus actively hunted healthy, strong bovids. ‘We didn’t find this in the earlier Homo erectus population on Java, but do know it from more modern human species of the Asian mainland. Homo erectus may have copied this practice from these populations. This suggests there may have been contact between these hominin groups, or even genetic exchange.’
A broader view of archaeological research
The site has been studied in detail over the past five years. ‘Often, only the most attractive material is published in this type of research, such as hominin fossils. We present the results of our studies in four extensive, richly illustrated articles,  creating a unique window to the drowned Sundaland of 140,000 years ago,’ says Berghuis. The research was carried out by researchers from Leiden University, the Netherlands, in collaboration with a team of specialists from Indonesia, Australia, Germany and Japan. The results were published this week in the journal
Quaternary Environments and Humans
.
The fossil collection is housed in the Geological Museum in Bandung, Indonesia. The museum is planning an exhibition, and  temporary exhibitions may follow at other locations.
What did Sundaland look like?
In prehistoric times, what we know as the Indonesian archipelago was an extensive lowland in periods with lower sea levels, with the current islands as mountain ranges. ‘We call this area Sundaland’, says Berghuis. ‘Homo erectus could disperse from the Asian mainland to Java.’ The vast majority of Sundaland is now a shallow sea, and until now, fossils had never been found in this area.
‘This makes our discoveries truly unique,’ says Berghuis. ‘The fossils come from a drowned river valley, which filled up over time with river sand. We have been able to date the material to approximately 140,000 years ago. That was the penultimate glacial period. Large parts of the northern hemisphere were covered by glaciers, and so much water on Earth was stored in ice caps that the global sea level was 100 metres lower than today.’
Elephants, rhinos, hippos, Komodo dragons and river sharks
At that time, Sundaland resembled today’s African savannah: a fairly dry grassland with narrow strips of forest along the major rivers and a rich fauna including various species of elephants, bovids, rhinos and crocodiles. ‘Most of these species are extinct, whereas others are the ancestors of species that still occur in the region, but whose survival is seriously threatened. The Asian hippo is extinct. Carnivorous Komodo dragons are now restricted to the islands of Komodo and Flores, and river sharks are extremely rare in the major rivers of India and Thailand. But all these animals were thriving in ancient Sundaland. This knowledge is hugely important to our understanding of the biodiversity of the whole of Southeast Asia.’

data.title: A toy RTOS inside Super Mario Bros. using emulator save states
data.author: notorious_pgb
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过在NES版《超级马里奥兄弟》游戏中实现多线程来解释线程的概念。作者将线程比作模拟器的存档状态，并展示了三个同时运行的马里奥游戏实例，每个实例分配不同的颜色调色板。线程调度器每160帧切换一次线程，跳过被杀死、阻塞或睡眠状态的线程。文章还介绍了同步原语，如互斥锁（Mutex）和条件变量（Condition Variables）。例如，当一个马里奥站在起点三个砖块上时，其他马里奥的游戏会暂停，直到他离开。通过这种方式，文章生动地展示了多线程编程中的时间分片、互斥锁和条件变量等概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对线程、并发、实时操作系统（RTOS）以及相关概念（如互斥锁、信号量、协程等）的技术探讨和比喻解释

不同观点：
• Sohcahtoa82将线程、多核处理、互斥锁、信号量等概念用工具箱和工作台等比喻进行解释，强调了多线程和多核的区别，以及同步工具的使用场景。
• Ericson2314对Sohcahtoa82的解释进行了细化，指出线程和进程的区别主要在于通信和同步机制的不同，并提到通过改变模拟器的外部实现可以更接近硬件并发的支持。
• mort96提出了关于实时操作系统的疑问，认为在模拟器中实现实时性增加了复杂性，限制了调度算法和内存分配器的选择。
• Cloudef认为文章中描述的线程概念更像是协程或绿色线程，并指出它们的区别在于协同调度和抢占式调度。

补充讨论：
• noone_youknow对文章和线程比喻表示高度赞赏，认为这种解释方式有助于帮助人们更好地理解底层系统。
• ignormies回忆了大学时学习实时操作系统课程的经历，认为文章中的可视化演示非常酷，并表示希望找到一个小项目来再次探索这一领域。
• gwbas1c提到了一种消除模拟器延迟的方法，通过预计算不同按钮组合的状态，然后根据实际按键切换到预计算的状态，类似于文章中的线程概念。
• 其他评论如liamwire、Refreeze5224等对文章的可视化演示表示赞赏，认为有助于理解复杂的线程和调度概念。
• CGamesPlay建议如果子世界内存可以在保存状态之间共享，将更能体现互斥锁的概念。
• dsfdsfsfew认为文章在定义RTOS上有所扩展，虽然与预期的使用ACE运行并发程序不同，但仍然具有趣味性和信息性。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于对线程和协程的定义和区分，Cloudef认为文章中的概念更接近协程，而Sohcahtoa82的比喻则更侧重于线程和多核的区别。Ericson2314进一步补充了线程和进程在通信和同步机制上的不同。

They're Mario Bros. for the NES, apparently.

This is another post about programming, which I almost never write about.
Click here
to jump straight to trying this thing out for yourself.
In my
previous post
on Threads, I made an offhand comparison
1
:
Threads
2
are just emulator
3
save states
4
, coupled with a condition upon which they will be resumed.
At the  time, I thought this a
pretty
okay
analogy — but I couldn’t stop thinking about it. I’ve been turning it around in my mind for a while. I think it has serious untapped potential as a pedagogical tool.
So I added multithreading to
Super Mario Bros.
for the NES.
The Thing Itself
No buried ledes here.
What It Is
I should explain myself.
What you just watched happens to be a multithreaded NES emulation, with
Super Mario Bros.
as the threads.
There are three “threads” running, each a distinct instance of the game. Every so often, the emulator switches “threads”, swapping to a different instance of the game.
Each “thread” is assigned a different color palette, which we apply when we resume said thread. This is why the colors are constantly changing around in the video.
More Specifically…
When World 1-1 starts, the “multithreading” begins. Specifically, my script creates three
save states
, each representing the current state of the game
5
. Then I create three
threads
6
, and give them their respective save state to hold on to.
Then I start the thread scheduler.
The thread scheduler’s job is simple:
Every 160 frames, switch to a new thread
The next thread ideally, in a rotating fashion (1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, …)
Skip over threads which are
KILLED
,
BLOCKED
(unless they can be unblocked), or
SLEEPING
(unless it’s time to wake them)
To switch to a new thread:
First, update the
current
thread’s save state with the current game state
Then, load in the
new
thread’s save state
Finally, update the
game color palette
to reflect which thread we’re on
This covers what you see for the first bit of the video: each thread starts at the same time (the loading screen for World 1-1), with different “games” being swapped in every so often.
Essentially,
three different games of Mario Bros.
are being played “at the same time”, but only one is actually
active
at any given time.
Beyond Just Time Slicing
This image shows the full World 1-1 map, with color-coded areas indicating various features explained below. I recommend clicking to expand this image.
Time slicing is cool — we’re running three “concurrent” games of Mario! — but that’s far from the only threading concept demonstrated here.
I’ve set up the game world in such a way that certain areas or features activate synchronization primitives (such as a mutex); you can
physically interact with threading boundaries
.
I describe the synchronization primitives I’ve set up below, but the
net effect
is:
If a Mario is standing on the three blocks at the start of the level, no other Mario’s game will run until he leaves (
Disabled Interrupts
)
Only one Mario can be inside the Pipe Sub-level at a time (
Mutex
)
If a Mario enters while another Mario is inside, his game will not resume until the other Mario leaves
Once a Mario touches the flagpole, his game pauses until all the other Marios have touched their flagpoles (
Condition Variables
)
Disabled Interrupts
The red shaded area on the map denotes a section of the world where
interrupts are disabled
, and therefore, the thread scheduler cannot run.
Whenever a Mario enters the red shaded area, his thread won’t lose control until he leaves the area, regardless of what other Marios are doing.
Mutexes
The yellow shaded area (difficult to discern — it’s the fourth pipe from the left; the one you can go down) demonstrates a
mutex
: an area of the game world where only one Mario may exist at a time.
When a Mario goes down the pipe, he tries to acquire the
pipeMutex
. If nothing else owns that mutex (i.e., no other thread is currently in the pipe sub-level), then he immediately gains ownership of the mutex and proceeds without issue.
However, if another Mario owns the mutex (is presently in the pipe sub-level), then the Mario which is presently entering the pipe will be
blocked
until the mutex is released (the other Mario leaves the pipe sub-level).
Marios outside of the pipe sub-level are not blocked, and are still allowed to run.
Condition Variables
The green shaded area (the flagpole at the end of the level) demonstrates a
condition variable
: when a Mario touches the flagpole, he increments
numMariosTouchedFlagpole
— a “condition variable” — by 1, and then blocks until that same condition variable is equal to the number of threads. In other words, he waits until all the other Marios have touched the flagpole before continuing.
Sleep
Whenever a Mario kills

data.title: Prohibition and ice cream in the US Navy
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary:
**总结：**

1914年，美国海军通过《第99号总令》全面禁止舰艇上饮酒。此前，海军已逐步限制酒精，并在1914年彻底禁止在船上的任何地方饮酒。1920年，美国全国进入禁酒期，导致非法酒吧兴起，但意外促进了冰淇淋的流行，许多酿酒厂转为生产冰淇淋。二战期间，美国海军在太平洋战区使用专门的冰淇淋驳船，每天生产大量冰淇淋，以提高士气。冰淇淋成为奖励手段，特别是在救援飞行员时，船员会获得大量冰淇淋作为奖励。禁酒令期间及二战中，冰淇淋在海军中扮演了重要角色，甚至取代了传统的朗姆酒奖励。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于海军中的酒精、冰淇淋及其他替代品的历史和现状

不同观点：
• **冰淇淋作为士气的象征**：
  - [ceejayoz] 提到一个可能未经证实的二战故事，当日军高层看到冰淇淋运送到前线时意识到战争已经失败，因为盟军有足够的资源提供甜点，而日军却在丛林中挨饿。
  - [jdross] 分享了一个真实故事，其叔祖父在二战期间为麦克阿瑟将军工作，负责为前线将士采购冰淇淋。
  
• **酒精在海军中的历史与现状**：
  - [former_navy_843] 指出，尽管官方上美国海军从酒精转向了冰淇淋，但在2000年代，酒精消费仍然非常普遍，尤其是极端的酗酒现象，甚至包括核反应堆操作员和核武器看守人员。
  - [abeppu] 提到二战期间，海军实际上也有大量酒精，但并不鼓励饮用。

44119173.article_content:
General Order 99
One hundred and eleven years ago on July 1, 1914, Secretary of the US Navy Josephus Daniels issued
General Order 99
, banning “the use or introduction for drinking purposes of alcoholic liquors on board any naval vessel, or within any navy yard or station.”
The US Navy had ended the rum ration in 1862 and imposed progressively more stringent restrictions on what alcohol sailors could have on shipboard. General Order 99 ended even the serving of alcohol in the wardroom and the captain’s cabin. An updated repost.
Prohibition and Ice Cream
Six years later, in 1920, the entire country followed the Navy’s example. With the ratification of the 18th Amendment, the United States banned the production, importation, transportation, and sale of alcoholic beverages. The thirteen year period known as
Prohibition
led to the growth of criminal gangs and the proliferation of “speakeasies,” illegal drinking establishments.
Prohibition also had a surprising and unexpected result — the growth in the popularity of ice cream. During Prohibition, many American breweries, including Yuengling and Anheuser-Busch, switched from brewing beer to making soda and ice cream. Ice cream parlors became popular places to socialize for both young and old. By the end of the decade,
Americans were consuming more than a million gallons of ice cream per day
—and, crucially, associating it with the comfort and diversion formerly assigned to alcohol.
World War II and the Navy’s Ice Cream Barge
With the end of Prohibition and the outbreak of World War II, the still dry US Navy was provided with ice cream on almost every ship.  In the Pacific theater of war, the US Navy even operated a large concrete
ice cream barge
. The Navy spent $1 million dollars retrofitting a barge they got from the Army to allow it to produce 10 US gallons of ice cream every seven minutes, or approximately 500 US gal per shift, and could store 2,000 US gallons of the finished product. Smaller barges, known as ice cream ships, were built to distribute the ice cream throughout the Western Pacific.
Ice cream was important for morale. In 1942, the U.S.S. Lexington was slowly sinking from a Japanese torpedo attack, before the crew abandoned ship,
they broke into the freezer and ate all the ice cream
. Survivors
describe
scooping ice cream into their helmets and licking them clean before lowering themselves into the Pacific.
Ice Cream as a Reward
In addition to the daily rum ration, when the captain of a naval sailing vessel wanted to reward the crew when things went exceptionally well, he might order a tot for all hands. The US Navy developed its own reward system. As there was no alcohol to be had, they used ice cream.
Ice cream became a reward for meritorious service. Specifically, on carriers, a reward system was set up for every pilot rescued by destroyers, escorts, submarines, or any other craft that brought a downed pilot back to the ship. During World War II; ten, twenty, or even thirty gallons of ice cream might be the payoff for a rescued pilot.
Tom Kocurko spent World War II
in the Navy and found out about the ice cream tradition while serving on a destroyer escort. “We’d get 10 gallons of ice cream every time we picked up a pilot, which was a real treat. So we started joking, ‘Let’s shoot one down.”‘
Sometimes ice cream may be better than even a tot of rum.

data.author: alex_hirner
data.article_summary: Terres是一只寄居蟹，隶属于Rustacean家族，是Ferris的伙伴及官方吉祥物。作为Rust编程语言社区的象征，Terres与Ferris一起代表该社区的友好和包容精神，旨在通过可爱的形象吸引更多开发者加入并参与Rust编程语言的发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust编程语言及其相关工具的应用和潜力，特别是调试工具和可视化工具。

不同观点：
• **支持Rust工具的潜力**：[leoh]认为Rust体现了“简单的事情应该简单，复杂的事情应该可能”的理念，并预测Rust将在未来几年得到更广泛的应用。[Rust-Trends]也表示了对Rust项目的赞赏，并计划在新闻通讯中进行推荐。

• **工具的实用性质疑**：[forrestthewoods]对该工具在实际程序调试中的有效性表示怀疑，认为玩具例子不能展示其在真实场景中的价值。

• **工具的比较和替代**：[spencerflem]将该工具与Glamorous Toolkit进行比较，表示对这类解释程序运行过程的工具非常感兴趣。[quotemstr]则从调试器的角度指出，Rust在调试方面与其他原生代码语言并无本质区别，认为专门为Rust设计的调试工具并无特别必要。

• **工具的功能和可用性问题**：[waschl]提到该工具无法与其在qemu中运行的Rust OS内核一起使用。[levkk]表示希望使用该工具，但遇到脚本需要sudo权限和不使用VSCode的问题。[dochtman]则关注该工具是否能在macOS上运行，并对移动端浏览体验提出质疑。

• **工具的技术比较**：[Veserv]将该工具与chrome://tracing进行比较，认为其在轨迹可视化和执行时间信息展示方面不如后者密集和有意义。

补充讨论：
• **工具的具体应用场景**：[tonyhart7]表示希望将该工具应用于数据库调试，询问具体工具名称。[orsenthil]则提到该工具让他想起了Pythontutor，并对其用户界面表示赞赏。

争议焦点：
• **工具的实际应用价值**：部分用户如[forrestthewoods]对其在真实程序调试中的有效性持怀疑态度，而其他用户如[leoh]和[Rust-Trends]则对其未来应用前景持乐观态度。

• **工具的比较和选择**：用户对不同调试和可视化工具如Glamorous Toolkit、chrome://tracing等的功能和优劣进行了比较和讨论。

data.title: What does “Undecidable” mean, anyway
data.author: BerislavLopac
data.article_summary:
本文简要解释了“不可判定”（Undecidable）在计算机科学中的含义，特别是针对没有计算机科学背景但有些许好奇的读者。文章首先引用了一本名为《Automata and Computability》的书中的技术定义：一个字符串属性P是可判定的，如果存在一个图灵机能够对具有属性P的输入返回“true”，对不具有的返回“false”。

接着，文章将这一技术概念转化为程序员更容易理解的术语。它解释了在自动机理论中，程序的输入是字符串，输出是“true”或“false”。通过这种模型，可以研究不同计算能力的计算模型，包括有限状态自动机（DFA）和图灵机（TM）。

图灵机是计算能力的上限，如果一个问题图灵机无法解决，那么任何实际编程语言也无法解决。文章还提到，图灵机可以模拟其他图灵机的运行，这使得我们可以研究图灵机行为的相关决策问题，例如某个图灵机是否在十步内完成计算。

最终，文章通过具体例子帮助读者理解“不可判定”的概念，即某些问题是图灵机无法解决的，从而也是任何实际编程语言无法解决的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不可判定性及其相关概念，包括计算理论、复杂性、逻辑独立性等。

不同观点：
• [mreid] 认为理解不可判定性的关键在于，并不是所有的 `f: string -> boolean` 函数都可以通过程序实现。由于程序是可数的无穷多，而函数是不可数的无穷多，因此存在无法通过程序表达的函数。这解释了为什么像 `IS_HALTING` 这样的函数不可判定。
• [Animats] 指出，任何具有有限状态的确定性系统都是可判定的，只有在无限内存的情况下，停机问题才不可判定。他认为文章没有明确区分复杂性和不可判定性，并强调复杂性（如P=NP问题）和不可判定性是不同层次的问题。
• [ummonk] 对“停机检测器可以被用作程序优化器/定理证明器/密码破解器/国际象棋引擎”的观点持怀疑态度，认为即便不通过停机问题，像密码破解和国际象棋等问题已经有相对简单的算法，虽然时间复杂度很高。
• [godelski] 认为要理解不可判定性，需要参考哥德尔不完备定理。他强调任何一致的公理系统都无法证明所有关于自然数的真理，总会有一些真命题是不可证明的。
• [taeric] 提出可以通过“欠指定”的概念来理解不可判定性，即在某些情况下，程序的部分可以被充分约束以回答特定问题，但其他部分可能仍然自由。
• [nialv7] 认为不可判定性与实数不可数性本质上是同一件事，但文章没有深入探讨这一联系。
• [Aziell] 分享了自己从困惑到接受停机问题不可判定性的过程，认为文章很好地解释了这一概念。
• [brap] 提出是否有可能对“智能”进行类似于“计算”的正式模型化，并探讨智能是否可以分类，是否存在某些类别智能无法完成的任务等问题。
• [skydhash] 强调了计算理论和编程语言理论对其软件工程职业的巨大帮助，认为这些理论使得对抽象机制的理解和使用变得更加容易。
• [cubefox] 指出了“不可判定”在计算机科学和形式逻辑中的不同含义。在计算机科学中，不可判定指的是没有算法可以解决所有输入情况；而在形式逻辑中，不可判定指的是某个命题在某个公理系统中既无法证明也无法反驳。
• [aatd86] 认为不可判定性类似于系统方程中存在太多自由变量，导致无法唯一解。
• [kazinator] 详细解释了停机问题的不可判定性，并指出尽管某些输入情况可以被决定，但对于不可判定问题，总会有输入情况导致算法陷入无限循环或返回错误答案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于不可判定性与复杂性的关系，以及如何在实际工程中处理不可判定问题。例如，[Animats] 强调了不可判定性和复杂性之间的区别，而 [ummonk] 则质疑某些任务通过停机问题解决的实际意义。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不可判定性与哥德尔不完备定理的联系，[godelski] 和 [graycat] 都提到了这一点，并提供了相关的背景信息和例子。
• 关于如何在实际工作中处理不可判定性问题，[kazinator] 和 [skydhash] 都分享了具体的经验和策略，如限制输入、调整需求或使用非图灵完备的语言等。

总体而言，讨论围绕不可判定性的理论基础、实际应用以及与其他计算理论概念的联系展开，涵盖了从哲学到工程实践的多个方面。

44119890.article_content:
May 28, 2025
What does "Undecidable" mean, anyway
An explainer for people who don't know computer science and are mildly curious
Systems Distributed
I'll be speaking at
Systems Distributed
next month! The talk is brand new and will aim to showcase some of the formal methods mental models that would be useful in mainstream software development. It has added some extra stress on my schedule, though, so expect the next two monthly releases of
Logic for Programmers
to be mostly minor changes.
What does "Undecidable" mean, anyway
Last week I read
Against Curry-Howard Mysticism
, which is a solid article I recommend reading. But this newsletter is actually about
one comment
:
I like to see posts like this because I often feel like I can’t tell the difference between BS and a point I’m missing. Can we get one for questions like “Isn’t XYZ (Undecidable|NP-Complete|PSPACE-Complete)?”
I've already written one of these for
NP-complete
, so let's do one for "undecidable". Step one is to pull a technical definition from the book
Automata and Computability
:
A property P of strings is said to be decidable if ... there is a total Turing machine that accepts input strings that have property P and rejects those that do not. (pg 220)
Step two is to translate the technical computer science definition into more conventional programmer terms. Warning, because this is a newsletter and not a blog post, I might be a little sloppy with terms.
Machines and Decision Problems
In automata theory, all inputs to a "program" are strings of characters, and all outputs are "true" or "false". A program "accepts" a string if it outputs "true", and "rejects" if it outputs "false". You can think of this as automata studying all pure functions of type
f :: string -> boolean
. Problems solvable by finding such an
f
are called "decision problems".
This covers more than you'd think, because we can bootstrap more powerful functions from these. First, as anyone who's programmed in bash knows, strings can represent any other data. Second, we can fake non-boolean outputs by instead checking if a certain computation gives a certain result. For example, I can reframe the function
add(x, y) = x + y
as a decision problem like this:
IS_SUM(str) {
x, y, z = split(str, "#")
return x + y == z
}
Then because
IS_SUM("2#3#5")
returns true, we know
2 + 3 == 5
, while
IS_SUM("2#3#6")
is false. Since we can bootstrap parameters out of strings, I'll just say it's
IS_SUM(x, y, z)
going forward.
A big part of automata theory is studying different models of computation with different strengths. One of the weakest is called
"DFA"
. I won't go into any details about what DFA actually can do, but the important thing is that it
can't
solve
IS_SUM
. That is, if you give me a DFA that takes inputs of form
x#y#z
, I can always find an input where the DFA returns true when
x + y != z
,
or
an input which returns false when
x + y == z
.
It's really important to keep this model of "solve" in mind: a program solves a problem if it correctly returns true on all true inputs and correctly returns false on all false inputs.
(total) Turing Machines
A Turing Machine (TM) is a particular type of computation model. It's important for two reasons:
By the
Church-Turing thesis
, a Turing Machine is the "upper bound" of how powerful (physically realizable) computational models can get. This means that if an actual real-world programming language can solve a particular decision problem, so can a TM. Conversely, if the TM
can't
solve it, neither can the programming language.
1
It's possible to write a Turing machine that takes
a textual representation of another Turing machine
as input, and then simulates that Turing machine as part of its computations.
Property (1) means that we can move between different computational models of equal strength, proving things about one to learn things about another. That's why I'm able to write
IS_SUM
in a pseudocode instead of writing it in terms of the TM computational model (and why I was able to use
split
for convenience).
Property (2) does several interesting things. First of all, it makes it possible to compose Turing machines. Here's how I can roughly ask if a given number is the sum of two primes, with "just" addition and boolean functions:
IS_SUM_TWO_PRIMES(z):
x := 1
y := 1
loop {
if x > z {return false}
if IS_PRIME(x) {
if IS_PRIME(y) {
if IS_SUM(x, y, z) {
return true;
}
}
}
y := y + 1
if y > x {
x := x + 1
y := 0
}
}
Notice that without the
if x > z {return false}
, the program would loop forever on
z=2
. A TM that always halts for all inputs is called
total
.
Property (2) also makes "Turing machines" a possible input to functions, meaning that we can now make decision problems about the behavior of Turing machines. For example, "does the TM
M
either accept or reject
x
within ten steps?"
2
IS_DONE_IN_TEN_STEPS(M, x) {
for (i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
`simulate M(x) for one step`
if(`M accepted or rejected`) {
return true
}
}
return false
}

44119890.article_summary:
本文简要解释了“不可判定”（Undecidable）在计算机科学中的含义，特别是针对没有计算机科学背景但有些许好奇的读者。文章首先引用了一本名为《Automata and Computability》的书中的技术定义：一个字符串属性P是可判定的，如果存在一个图灵机能够对具有属性P的输入返回“true”，对不具有的返回“false”。

接着，文章将这一技术概念转化为程序员更容易理解的术语。它解释了在自动机理论中，程序的输入是字符串，输出是“true”或“false”。通过这种模型，可以研究不同计算能力的计算模型，包括有限状态自动机（DFA）和图灵机（TM）。

图灵机是计算能力的上限，如果一个问题图灵机无法解决，那么任何实际编程语言也无法解决。文章还提到，图灵机可以模拟其他图灵机的运行，这使得我们可以研究图灵机行为的相关决策问题，例如某个图灵机是否在十步内完成计算。

最终，文章通过具体例子帮助读者理解“不可判定”的概念，即某些问题是图灵机无法解决的，从而也是任何实际编程语言无法解决的。
44119890.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不可判定性及其相关概念，包括计算理论、复杂性、逻辑独立性等。

不同观点：
• [mreid] 认为理解不可判定性的关键在于，并不是所有的 `f: string -> boolean` 函数都可以通过程序实现。由于程序是可数的无穷多，而函数是不可数的无穷多，因此存在无法通过程序表达的函数。这解释了为什么像 `IS_HALTING` 这样的函数不可判定。
• [Animats] 指出，任何具有有限状态的确定性系统都是可判定的，只有在无限内存的情况下，停机问题才不可判定。他认为文章没有明确区分复杂性和不可判定性，并强调复杂性（如P=NP问题）和不可判定性是不同层次的问题。
• [ummonk] 对“停机检测器可以被用作程序优化器/定理证明器/密码破解器/国际象棋引擎”的观点持怀疑态度，认为即便不通过停机问题，像密码破解和国际象棋等问题已经有相对简单的算法，虽然时间复杂度很高。
• [godelski] 认为要理解不可判定性，需要参考哥德尔不完备定理。他强调任何一致的公理系统都无法证明所有关于自然数的真理，总会有一些真命题是不可证明的。
• [taeric] 提出可以通过“欠指定”的概念来理解不可判定性，即在某些情况下，程序的部分可以被充分约束以回答特定问题，但其他部分可能仍然自由。
• [nialv7] 认为不可判定性与实数不可数性本质上是同一件事，但文章没有深入探讨这一联系。
• [Aziell] 分享了自己从困惑到接受停机问题不可判定性的过程，认为文章很好地解释了这一概念。
• [brap] 提出是否有可能对“智能”进行类似于“计算”的正式模型化，并探讨智能是否可以分类，是否存在某些类别智能无法完成的任务等问题。
• [skydhash] 强调了计算理论和编程语言理论对其软件工程职业的巨大帮助，认为这些理论使得对抽象机制的理解和使用变得更加容易。
• [cubefox] 指出了“不可判定”在计算机科学和形式逻辑中的不同含义。在计算机科学中，不可判定指的是没有算法可以解决所有输入情况；而在形式逻辑中，不可判定指的是某个命题在某个公理系统中既无法证明也无法反驳。
• [aatd86] 认为不可判定性类似于系统方程中存在太多自由变量，导致无法唯一解。
• [kazinator] 详细解释了停机问题的不可判定性，并指出尽管某些输入情况可以被决定，但对于不可判定问题，总会有输入情况导致算法陷入无限循环或返回错误答案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于不可判定性与复杂性的关系，以及如何在实际工程中处理不可判定问题。例如，[Animats] 强调了不可判定性和复杂性之间的区别，而 [ummonk] 则质疑某些任务通过停机问题解决的实际意义。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不可判定性与哥德尔不完备定理的联系，[godelski] 和 [graycat] 都提到了这一点，并提供了相关的背景信息和例子。
• 关于如何在实际工作中处理不可判定性问题，[kazinator] 和 [skydhash] 都分享了具体的经验和策略，如限制输入、调整需求或使用非图灵完备的语言等。

总体而言，讨论围绕不可判定性的理论基础、实际应用以及与其他计算理论概念的联系展开，涵盖了从哲学到工程实践的多个方面。

data.title: Collatz's Ant and Similarity of Landscapes
data.author: Fibra
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了Collatz猜想中的“景观”相似性问题，重点分析从$n = 10^{20}$到$n = 10^{20} + 100$的数字轨迹，关注停止时间（$\tau$）、最大欧氏距离（$\alpha$）、达到最大距离的步数（$\beta$）以及最后一步的距离（$\gamma$）。研究发现，停止时间并非决定景观相似性的唯一因素，不同景观可能有相同停止时间。虽然最大距离（$\alpha$）能提供一些线索，但仅靠它不足以区分不同景观，因为放大相同模式会产生类似景观。步数（$\beta$）提供了一定的离散性，可以用于分类，但也有例外，某些不同景观可能拥有相同$\beta$。文章最后提出，景观的形成过程可能需要进一步研究，以解释这些现象。

44086721.article_content:
Collatz's Ant and similarity of landscapes
This is a small development from the
previous post
, which is mostly focused on trying to understand where the similarities between landscapes come from (and what can be taken as proxies for these).
Considering the trajectories respective to the numbers from $n = 10^{20}$ to $n = 10^{20} + 100$, and the corresponding stopping times ($\tau$), maximum euclidean distance hit ($\alpha$) from the origin point $(0, 0)$ where the ant starts, the step at which such maximum distance is hit ($\beta$), and also the distance from the origin at the last step ($\gamma$) (in the third plot it’s normalized by $\alpha$), we have the following:
along with the corresponding landscapes for each trajectory.
The question is: what makes a certain landscape specific? As already seen before in the
previous post
, the answer isn’t the stopping time. In fact, there are vastly different landscapes with the same stopping time. One can also wonder if the maximum distance hit would give a clue. I have no intent of going about labelling each landscape according to which potential category it might belong to, so as to find if there are any discrepancies to be pointed at, but from a first look at such landscapes and also relying trivially on our intuition, we can of course state that $\alpha$ is always going to be minimally associated with different landscapes to the extent that these can be purely differentiated from each other given their dimensions. Beyond this, it’s not useful. In fact, if we think about scaling up the same pattern such that $\alpha$ increases, we’re more or less talking about the same landscape but with vastly different dimensions (such that there’s some type of scale-free similarity). Not that there are any examples of that in these trajectories, as that would also presumably only be noticeable when comparing trajectories with $\tau$’s with different orders of magnitude. But this suffices to make the point: $\alpha$ alone isn’t sufficient to make such discernment between landscapes.
One thing that’s easily noticeable from the start is that of $\beta$ or the step at which the maximum distance is reached. In fact, this provides some type of discreteness to our analysis. Despite very different maximum distances reached ($\alpha$), the step at which such $\alpha$ is reached seems to allow for grouping onto different categories. Or at least, this seems to be the case at a first sight. We have cases where both $\tau$ and $\beta$ coincide, as present in the following example:
Cases where there’s a slight discrepancy in $\beta$, for instance:
And cases where this completely breaks, such that $\beta$ is vastly different, with respect to the same landscape:
But here of course we notice why this breaks. There’s a slight number of steps at the start of the ant’s trajectory which pushes the formation of the landscape away from the origin, such that the maximum distance reached is going to be at earlier steps (i.e. decrease in $\beta$). This was at least my intuition at first, but it doesn’t seem to make the most sense given that $\alpha$ is relative to the distances of that same trajectory. Not relative to others’! So the question still remains: why shouldn’t $\beta$ still be the same even if in the second example there would be an increase of $\alpha$? And if not, why?
This might require seeing how these landscape are forming…
Respectively (and highlighting $\beta$ with red):
we see that those steps in the start which push the landscape up, do end up influecing $\beta$, but only indirectly through changing which part of the landscape is going to be considered maximally distant from the origin. Ok, that’s interesting. But a big coincidence? Now even stranger is when two considerably different landscapes not only have the same $\tau$ but also end up having the same $\beta$, as is the case with the following example:
This is harder to explain. Perhaps there’s nothing to explain here. Perhaps a mere coincidence?
If we check the formation of the corresponding landscapes:
This is far from being the only example.
Examples from $n = 10^{10}$ to $n = 10^{10} + 100$, for which more of this can be verified.

data.title: What If We Had Bigger Brains? Imagining Minds Beyond Ours
data.author: nsoonhui
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了如果人类或人工智能拥有更多神经元，可能会出现哪些新能力。目前人类大脑有约1000亿个神经元，能够使用复杂的语言，而猫仅有约1亿个神经元，无法做到这一点。文章思考了拥有100万亿神经元的大脑可能会带来的新能力，并指出大脑通过大量感官数据做出决策，利用“可计算简化性”来应对世界的复杂性。大脑像是一个“压缩器”，提取重要特征并形成概念和语言。文章还提出，更大的大脑可能能够处理更多概念和词汇，但具体这些新能力是什么仍需进一步探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大脑处理能力、智力扩展及其局限性

不同观点：
• [necovek] 认为大脑实际上是并行处理信息的，尽管我们在学习新技能时会感到困难，但通过训练可以提高并行处理的能力。他还提出，人类可能能够通过训练实现并行思考，但社会习惯限制了这种能力的发展。
• [x86cherry] 提出，人类智力的限制可能不是大脑尺寸，而是缺乏新体验。大多数人从事重复性工作，限制了他们的认知发展。
• [Aziell] 认为，人类大脑的局限性是内嵌的，人们在深度思考时遇到的困难是因为大脑结构的限制，而不是因为他们不够努力。
• [b00ty4breakfast] 质疑对智力的过度追求，认为更聪明不一定总是更好，人类的许多问题正是源于过度的智力活动。他主张在提升智力之前，应先学会负责任地使用现有的智力资源。

What If We Had Bigger Brains? Imagining Minds beyond Ours
May 21, 2025
Cats Don’t Talk
We humans have perhaps 100 billion neurons in our brains. But what if we had many more? Or what if the AIs we built effectively had many more? What kinds of things might then become possible? At 100 billion neurons, we know, for example, that compositional language of the kind we humans use is possible. At the 100 million or so neurons of a cat, it doesn’t seem to be. But what would become possible with 100 trillion neurons? And is it even something we could imagine understanding?
My purpose here is to start exploring such questions, informed by what we’ve seen in recent years in neural nets and LLMs, as well as by what we now know about the
fundamental nature of computation
, and about neuroscience and the operation of actual brains (like the one that’s writing this, imaged here):
One suggestive point is that as artificial neural nets have gotten bigger, they seem to have successively passed a sequence of thresholds in capability:
So what’s next? No doubt there’ll be things like humanoid robotic control that have close analogs in what we humans already do. But what if we go far beyond the ~10
14
connections that our human brains have? What qualitatively new kinds of capabilities might there then be?
If this was about “computation in general” then there wouldn’t really be much to talk about. The
Principle of Computational Equivalence
implies that beyond some low threshold computational systems can generically produce behavior that corresponds to computation that’s as sophisticated as it can ever be. And indeed that’s the kind of thing we see both in lots of abstract settings, and in the natural world.
But the point here is that we’re not dealing with “computation in general”. We’re dealing with the kinds of computations that brains fundamentally do. And the essence of these seems to have to do with taking in large amounts of sensory data and then coming up with what amount to decisions about what to do next.
It’s not obvious that there’d be any reasonable way to do this. The world at large is full of
computational irreducibility
—where the only general way to work out what will happen in a system is just to run the underlying rules for that system step by step and see what comes out:
And, yes, there are plenty of questions and issues for which there’s essentially no choice but to
do this irreducible computation
—just as there are plenty of cases where
LLMs need
to
call on
our
Wolfram Language
computation system to get computations done. But brains, for the things most important to them, somehow seem to routinely manage to “jump ahead” without in effect simulating every detail. And what makes this possible is the fundamental fact that within any system that shows overall computational irreducibility there must inevitably be an infinite number of “pockets of computational reducibility”, in effect associated with “simplifying features” of the behavior of the system.
It’s these “pockets of reducibility” that brains exploit to be able to successfully “navigate” the world for their purposes in spite of its “background” of computational irreducibility. And in these terms things like the progress of science (and technology) can basically be thought of as the identification of progressively more pockets of computational reducibility. And we can then imagine that the capabilities of bigger brains could revolve around being able to “hold in mind” more of these pockets of computational reducibility.
We can think of brains as fundamentally serving to
“compress” the complexity of the world
, and extract from it just certain features—associated with pockets of reducibility—that we care about. And for us a key manifestation of this is the idea of concepts, and of language that uses them. At the level of raw sensory input we might see many detailed images of some category of thing—but language lets us describe them all just in terms of one particular symbolic concept (say “rock”).
In a rough first approximation, we can imagine that there’s a direct correspondence between concepts and words in our language. And it’s then notable that human languages all tend to have perhaps 30,000 common words (or word-like constructs). So is that scale the result of the size of our brains? And could bigger brains perhaps deal with many more words, say millions or more?
“What could all those words be about?” we might ask. After all, our everyday experience makes it seem like our current 30,000 words are quite sufficient to describe the world as it is. But in some sense this is circular: we’ve invented the words we have because they’re what we

data.author: alberto-m
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了国际象棋棋子设计的历史演变。象棋的祖先可以追溯到公元前2500年印度河流域的文明，当时可能使用粘土小雕像作为早期棋子。到公元7世纪，印度出现了一种叫“恰图兰卡”的游戏，具有四种不同的棋子类型，这些类型后来演变为现代象棋的棋子。恰图兰卡传到波斯，发展为“沙特兰兹”，并逐渐演变为现代象棋。在沙特兰兹时期，棋子开始变得抽象，但也有具象的例子。文章还提到象棋在中世纪的传播和演变，包括在不同国家和时期的设计变化。20世纪后，棋子设计继续发展，进入了多样化的现代时期。
data.comments_summary:

v 3.7.web
2025
A visual history of chessmen
When you or I think about chess, what pieces do we picture? What pieces do people in other countries picture? What did people in the past picture?
This is a timeline of chess set designs through history.
Jump to:
Ancient history
Late antiquity
Early middle ages
Late middle ages
16th century
17th century
18th century
19th century
1900-1950
1950s

Ancient history
2,500 BC
Indus Valley
The earliest ancestors of chess may have been played by the Indus Valley civilisation more than four thousand years ago. Clay figurines discovered in
Lothal
may be the earliest "chessmen".
The Lothal "chessmen."
Late antiquity
7th C. CE
Chaturanga, chess ancestor
By the 7th Century CE, people in India were playing
chaturanga
("four divisions"). The name refers to four types of solider that made up the game—infantry, cavalry, elephants, and chariots, commanded by a raja—that were modeled on the armies of the time. It was the innovation of these different piece types, which each moved in different ways, that distinguished
chaturanga
from other war games. The different piece types are the ancestors of the pieces of the modern game, and one of the reasons why we can trace chess back to
chaturanga
.
Chaturagna
spread outwards from India and is thought to be the common ancestor of many similar games. When it reaches Persia in the 8th Century, the game becomes
shatranj
, which would later reach Europe and develop into modern chess.
A map showing the spread of
chaturanga
and its influence on other games around the globe, including
shatranj
, chess,
xiàngqí
(China) and
shogi
(Japan).
If you were transported to ancient India, you would not necessarily recognise the game they were playing as chess. One of the earliest descriptions we have of how
chaturanga
was played comes from the 11th Century Persian scholar Al-Biruni's text,
India
. Like modern chesss,
chaturanga
was played on an eight by eight grid, which had been borrowed from an existing Indian game called
ashtapada
. In the
chaturanga
Al-Biruni describes, however, this board was the battleground for
four
players and four different armies at once. It was also a game of chance (!), where players rolled dice to decide which pieces to move.
Both modern chess players and 11th Century Persian
shatranj
players would find the moves of this game to be different. Al-Biruni descirbes the elephant (the ancient bishop) as able to move only one square diagonally at a time, or one square forward instead. ("They say that these five squares (i.e. the one straight forward and the others at the corners) are the places occupied by the trunk and the four feet of the elephant.")
If
shatranj
to the West and
xiàngqí
to the East, both games for two players, descend from the same game, it would make sense to assume that the common ancestor was also a two player board game. Chess historian
H J R Murray, who wrote the definitive treatise of the origins of chess, thought,
from the way Persian and Arabics writers described
chaturanga
in reference to
shatranj
, that there must have been two-player versions of the game in India at the same time as Al-Biruni witnessed the four-player game. Murray cannot say which, two- or four-player
chaturanga
, he believes came first. However, in is certain that there were two-player Indian chess games in later centuries. These, which have dispensed with dice, were called by some variation of
buddhidyūta
, "intellectual game".
8th C.
Afrasiab
In the Second Persian Empire,
chaturanga
becomes
shatranj
. As
shatranj
, new rules are introduced that cause the game to begin to resemble modern chess, including the rule that the King cannot be captured but must be rendered helpless: shah mat, the King is helpless, gives us the word checkmate.
The earliest
shatranj
pieces were figural (depicting recognisble forms from life), like those discovered in
Afrasiab
, modern Uzbekistan, made from ivory and dating from the 700s. They feature soldiers on foot, horseback or riding chariots or elephants.
The Afrasiab chessmen are normally considered the oldest definitive chessmen. While there followed a shift in favour of abstract pieces, they must not have been completely replaced, as later examples of Islamic figurative pieces have been found.
Seven figurative chessmen were excavated in
Afrasiab
, northern Samarkland.
Early figural chessmen
, Left: a bishop (elephant), date given as 7th (!?) to 8th C. Right: rook (chariot) 11th to 12th C.
8th C.
Abstract Persian
The shift to abstract chessmen has traditionally been attributed to religious an-iconism: the prohibition of figurative objects to prevent idolatry. However, not only have later figural pieces been found, but per the Met, abstract Persian chessmen are now thought to predate the Islamic conquest. Perhaps the adoption of symbolic chessmen were to make them easier to distinguish in games, or cheaper to manufacture?

data.title: Implementing complex numbers and FFT with just datatypes (2023)
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何仅使用代数数据类型（ADT）实现复数和FFT（快速傅里叶变换），而不使用浮点数。作者首先解释了为何要用ADT实现数字，特别是在证明辅助工具（如Coq）中形式化实数时，以及在HVM上实现最优算法时遇到的困难。传统上，自然数可以用 bitstring 表示，例如用 `O` 表示0位，`I` 表示1位，`E` 表示结束。通过递归操作，如增量和加法，可以实现数值操作。

然而，简单的实现（如重复递增）在Haskell上可能表现不佳，但在HVM上由于函数融合机制可以更高效。作者进一步探讨了如何通过优化数据类型实现数值算法，以期在实际中超越现有算法。

文章还分析了教科书上的FFT实现如何容易破坏函数融合，导致指数级性能下降。作者旨在展示一种纯函数式、仅用ADT实现的FFT，以避免传统浮点运算的弊端，并探索最优算法的新可能性。

• LegionMammal978认为平衡三进制在表示有符号整数时不如二补数整数有效。他指出，二补数整数可以通过从0和-1的基本形式开始构建2x和2x+1，同样能够很好地处理有符号整数。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到平衡三进制的选择是否必要，以及二补数系统的优势。LegionMammal978 implied that the choice of balanced ternary may be more complex or less efficient compared to the widely used two's-complement system, especially when constructing integers in a computational context.
• 评论中没有直接的争议焦点，但隐含的讨论在于技术实现的简便性和效率，特别是在构造和处理有符号整数时，二补数系统可能更为直观和普遍。

总结：
该评论提出了对平衡三进制用于有符号整数表示的质疑，并通过二补数系统的例子说明其可能的优势。主要争议点在于技术选择上的效率和简便性，但未展开详细的技术对比。

Implementing complex numbers and FFT with just datatypes (no floats)
In this article, I'll explain why implementing numbers with just algebraic
datatypes is desirable. I'll then talk about common implementations of FFT (Fast
Fourier Transform) and why they hide inherent inefficiencies. I'll then show how
to implement integers and complex numbers with just algebraic datatypes, in a
way that is extremely simple and elegant. I'll conclude by deriving a pure
functional implementation of complex FFT with just datatypes, no floats.
Why implement numbers with ADTs?
For most programmers, "real numbers" are a given: they just use floats and call
it a day. But, in some cases, it doesn't work well, and I'm not talking about
precision issues. When trying to prove statements on real numbers in proof
assistants like Coq, we can't use doubles, we must formalize reals using
datatypes, which can be very hard. For me, the real issue arises when I'm trying
to implement optimal algorithms on
HVM
.
To do that, I need functions to fuse, which is a fancy way of saying that
(+ 2) .  (+ 2)
"morphs into"
(+ 4)
during execution - yet, machine floats block
that mechanism. Because of that, I've been trying to come up with an elegant way
to implement numbers with just datatypes. For natural numbers, it is easy: we
can just implement them as bitstrings:

numerical example where fusion makes a big difference, being exponential on

linear on HVM
. But this isn't useful in practice, as we already have
fast addition algorithms like add-carry. The question, then, becomes: is it possible to explore
optimality to implement numeric algorithms that actually beat existing ones in
practice? The idea is that we could implement numbers with datatypes, which are, usually,
much slower than floats, but, if the resulting asymptotics are improved,
then this would easily pay off. One of the most successful numeric algorithms ever is the FFT. How
would an "optimal FFT" look like? Let's find out!

44088392.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何仅使用代数数据类型（ADT）实现复数和FFT（快速傅里叶变换），而不使用浮点数。作者首先解释了为何要用ADT实现数字，特别是在证明辅助工具（如Coq）中形式化实数时，以及在HVM上实现最优算法时遇到的困难。传统上，自然数可以用 bitstring 表示，例如用 `O` 表示0位，`I` 表示1位，`E` 表示结束。通过递归操作，如增量和加法，可以实现数值操作。

然而，简单的实现（如重复递增）在Haskell上可能表现不佳，但在HVM上由于函数融合机制可以更高效。作者进一步探讨了如何通过优化数据类型实现数值算法，以期在实际中超越现有算法。

文章还分析了教科书上的FFT实现如何容易破坏函数融合，导致指数级性能下降。作者旨在展示一种纯函数式、仅用ADT实现的FFT，以避免传统浮点运算的弊端，并探索最优算法的新可能性。

data.author: aaaronson
data.article_summary:
《Square Theory》一文描述了在Crosscord这个拥有超过5000名用户的Discord服务器上，拼字爱好者们如何通过一个偶然的观察，发展出一种名为“square theory”的语言游戏现象。故事始于2022年1月，拼字构造者Alex Boisvert在#etuiposting频道发布了一组有趣的词语对：MULTITOOL和MULTIPLIERS，随后引发了更多类似的例子，如PUB QUIZ和BAR EXAM。这种两个词对之间看似无关但能形成有趣组合的现象被称为“double doubles”，并在服务器上掀起了一股热潮，最终创建了专门的讨论线程#double-doubles。

这种现象的吸引力在于其结构——每个double double可以被模型化为一个正方形，四个角是词语，边是词语间的关系。这种正方形结构带来的满足感类似于数学中的范畴论，它研究对象和对象间的关系。这种理论不仅限于词语，还可以应用于各种概念和实体。

拼字谜构造者在设计问题标记线索时，也常经历类似的过程，通过词语联想完成这个“正方形”。这种现象展示了人类对对称和完整结构的天然喜好。

44107942.article_content:
May 27, 2025
Square Theory
The story starts in
Crosscord
, the crossword Discord server. Over 5,000 users strong, the server has emerged as a central hub for the online crossword community, a buzzing, sometimes overwhelming, sometimes delightful town square where total noobs, veteran constructors, and champion solvers alike come together to talk about words that cross each other.
Square roots
We direct our attention toward the #etuiposting channel, Crosscord’s designated space for shitposting (so named because ETUI, a sewing case, is a prototypically shitty piece of crosswordese). There, one afternoon in January 2022, crossword constructor and
Crossword Nexus
warden Alex Boisvert posted what seemed at the time to be an innocuous, mildly interesting observation:
Suffice to say, the Crosscord hivemind had other examples of this.
Will Nediger
replied a few minutes later with the clever MULTITOOL and MULTIPLIERS (words with completely unrelated meanings, despite the fact that PLIERS are a TOOL). Several messages later, Alex chimed back in with the elegant PUB QUIZ and BAR EXAM, a pairing that had been used in some form in crosswords by constructors
Christopher Adams
(2018) and
Robyn Weintraub
(2021).
Something about this concept—two sets of synonyms (PUB and BAR, QUIZ and EXAM), which when paired together, form phrases that themselves are not synonyms (PUB QUIZ and BAR EXAM)—captured the minds of Crosscord. Suddenly, the floodgates were open.
Intermittently over the next
year
, #etuiposting would be flooded with these pairs of pairs. They became too much even for the shitposting channel, and were ultimately confined to a thread called #double-doubles (a name
Bob Weisz
and I both proposed simultaneously). Today, more than three years after Alex’s original prompt, the thread still remains active, a wordplay oasis of over 3,000 posts.
There’s something going on here. Something more than a shitpost or an ephemeral trend. Double doubles have the proverbial juice, and the juice lies in their structure. Each pair of pairs can be modeled as a square, where the corners are words and the sides are relations between those words:
It’s this square structure that makes each double double feel tight, feel satisfying, feel like a real “find”. This is the essence of what I’ve started calling
square theory
, and it applies to much more than just posts in a Discord server.
Just like it’s satisfying when an essay or a news story comes full circle, or mindblowing when you find an unexpected cycle in your network of friends, it’s inherently compelling when things wrap around and complete the square. Let’s break it down.
The theory of everything
Crosscord wasn’t the first to catch onto this kind of formation: Ricki Heicklen has maintained a
huge list
of double doubles (which she calls “Unparalleled Misalignments”—itself a sort of double double) since 2018, and the success of her recent
Twitter thread
about them is another testament to their widespread appeal. Pairs of the same form pop up on a regular basis in the form of crossword clues and Twitter jokes:
However, there’s nothing about the square structure that dictates the edges must represent phrases and synonyms. Each edge of the square can be any relation that connects its vertices (but generally, the stronger the relations, the stronger the square). The vertices don’t even necessarily have to be words—they can be any entity or concept.
It evokes the mathematical field of
category theory
, which very abstractly studies mathematical objects and the relations between them. It’s the topology of the square that makes it satisfying, regardless of what the edges and vertices represent.
Members of the #double-doubles thread have already noticed this, consciously or not, with many of the posts interpreting the original prompt more liberally and swapping out the “synonym” relation for something else:
Sometimes it feels like the #double-doubles thread has devolved into just #question-mark-clues (crossword clues that are trying to trick you, requiring you to reinterpret them beyond their words’ most likely meaning, or “surface sense”). But that’s no coincidence—abstractly, every question mark clue takes the form of a square.
When brainstorming for question mark clues, crossword constructors experience this on a regular basis. You start with the answer at hand, playing word association with it in search of a combination of words that usually means one thing (the surface sense) but can be interpreted differently (the intended interpretation) to point to the answer, thus completing the square:
Take
Will Shortz’s all-time favorite clue
for instance, from a 1995 Martin Ashwood-Smith puzzle: [It turns into a different story] (which deviously didn’t even include the question mark). On the surface, “turns into a different story” typically means something like “develops into another situation.” But the intended interpretation takes the clue’s words to mean “rotates into another floor,” leading to t

data.title: The Decline of Battery Life
data.author: akyuu
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Evercade游戏设备的电池续航问题，相比旧设备如1989年的Game Boy可使用20小时，Evercade仅能支持约四小时。作者指出，现代设备的电池寿命普遍缩短，尽管技术进步，但功耗增加导致续航下降。文章比较了不同任天堂掌机的电池寿命，指出影响电池表现的因素复杂，包括电池类型、设备功耗等。作者怀念如诺基亚3310手机那样长达一周的续航，并以个人经验说明现代设备在长时间使用上的不足，尽管有些设备如M1 MacBook Air表现出色。文章最后质疑，电池寿命的缩短是否真的是技术进步的合理代价。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：设备电池寿命的发展趋势及用户体验变化

不同观点：

• valbaca反驳了电池寿命变短的观点，指出不同设备使用的电池类型不同（如一次性电池和可充电电池），并认为可充电电池是极大的进步，减少了使用成本。

44117911.article_content:
As I was writing
my Evercade gaming device review
, I noticed that the battery life of the new handheld machine wasn’t quite up to par, clocking in at about four hours playtime, fairly independent of the screen brightness settings. Of course I’m heavily biased here, vividly remembering having to lug around four spare AA batteries in case my original Game Boy would die on me. It almost never happened: the 1989 machine lasted for more than 20 hours!
Sure, the Grey Brick is very old. Sure, it was based on what Nintendo’s Gunpei Yokoi—the designer behind the best pocketable machine of all time—called
Lateral Thinking With Withered Technology
. But as a gamer, or even as an end user of any embedded piece of hardware, the trend towards shorter battery lives of devices is definitely visible.
Take a look at the average battery life of Nintendo’s handheld systems over the years:
Average battery life of devices.
Scrambling together these numbers required a lot of guesswork as my own playthroughs and reported numbers from various sources differed quite a bit.
Nerdly Pleasures
explains battery life in the 8-bit Game Boy line more thoroughly.
Wired
and
IGN
also conducted bigger tests.
Comparing battery life is much more involved than simply looking at the average play time. For one, there’s the kilowatt/hour and electric charge/hour rates of the batteries, the composition of the battery (lithium, nickel-metal hybrid, …) Secondly, there’s the required current of the device itself, also based on a slew of different requirements (CPU kind, size, make, RAM, screen technology and intensity, and so forth). Thirdly, it depends on the load of the machine (how the game itself was programmed and the brightness of the screen). I tried adding these to the graph but the resulting mess made me even more confused.
In essence, as an end user of these machines, I do not care about
mAh
,
MHz
,
DDR3
or whatever. I care about the longevity. Will this thing last the long train ride? Can I still make a call after watching these YouTube videos on my smartphone?
Remember the
Nokia 3310 cellphone
from 2000? The battery of that beast lasted a whole week. A week! How many times did you charge your iPhone today? Again, the comparison is far from fair, but in terms of usability, it’s a huge step back. That’s why I’m still clinging onto my
Sony Xperia Z1 Compact
. Its battery lasts three days with mild usage. But I’m
far from a devoted smartphone user
, so again: no fair competition here. It’s not all bad nowadays though, my M1 MacBook Air is a
fantastic
piece of hardware that takes virtually ages to run dry. Even the four hours of my nine year old Air from 2012 is still decent.
Back to that
Evercade
I was fiddling with. It has a
1.2Ghz
Cortex-A7 processor, a
4:3
LCD screen (the same as a PSP), and runs a custom version of Linux (of course it does). That means it’s basically a little computer I just happen to use for retro gaming. 8-bit, 16-bit and even 32-bit handhelds from the original GB to the GBA very simple embedded pieces of hardware. The Game Boy Color didn’t even have another processor: it was still the
Z80
, only running at twice the speed of the original model (
8 MHz
). The GBA “finally” contained a proper CPU, an ARM7TDMI running at
16.78 MHz
. Except that its CPU cycles aren’t clogged with needless Linux daemons or kernel programs: there’s simply no OS! Pop in a cart and you’re ready to go. The Evercade is also cartridge-based, but relies on emulation—hence, a software layer (and more power) is needed.
Twenty years later, the Evercade is almost eighty times faster than the GBA, while its battery life has been divided by three. The first GBA model’s non-backlit screen is not that inferior to the Evercade’s bigger LCD screen. The quality is very bad (see my review), and my modded GBA with backlit fares of much better, without having to give in that much on battery time. The upcoming
Analogue Pocket
—that uses hardware emulation with FPGAs instead of software emulation—reportedly does not perform that much better, with a battery life of six hours as a rough estimation. But that one comes with a high-quality screen. Or so they say.
Power for battery life—a fair trade-off? I’m not so sure.

data.title: Wake Up, Remix
data.author: dimitrisnl
data.article_summary:
2025年5月26日，Remix宣布“复苏”！Michael Jackson和Ryan Florence共同回顾了Remix的发展历程。在去年的React Conf上，他们宣布Remix将与React Router更紧密结合，将Remix v2的大部分功能整合进React Router v7的“框架模式”中，并支持RSC（React Server Components）。React Router v7现已成为一个非常强大且广泛应用的项目，支撑着包括Shopify、GitHub等众多应用。

在此基础上，Remix团队决定探索新的方向，开发Remix v3。这个新版本将不再依赖React，而是基于Preact，追求更简单、快速、贴近web本身的发展路径。新框架将注重模型驱动开发、基于Web API构建、避免不必要依赖以及强调组合性。虽然尚未发布预览，但这些原则将指导Remix v3的开发，旨在提供更轻量、高效的开发体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：React Router和Remix项目的未来方向及其影响

不同观点：
• [kelnos] 对React Router (RR) v7项目的未来维护状况表示担忧，担心其可能无法得到良好维护。
• [tefkah] 认为React Router的新版本代表了新的方向，速度更快、更简单，并且更贴近web本身。同时讽刺一些人直接发布ChatGPT生成的内容。
• [dimitrisnl] 指出标题从"Wake up, Remix!"改为"Come on now Remix.."后语气变得更弱，影响了原有的表达意图。
• [insin] 提到自己使用Preact + htm进行无构建开发，并对React Router作者Ryan和Michael的新项目表示期待。
• [nadis] 对选择基于Preact分叉的决策表示不解，希望有更详细的解释，认为仅给出一句话的说明不够充分。
• [medhir] 表示曾考虑将Next项目重写为Remix，但发现Remix与React Router v7的演变趋同，且不断变化的方向让人对投入时间学习这些解决方案失去信心。
• [zIndex9999] 强烈批评Remix v3的“全 reboot”策略，认为这是对过去所依赖的React生态系统的背离，且动机不明。同时质疑Remix团队在维护两个项目的情况下，会导致两者进度都放缓。

补充讨论：
• Remix从与React Router合并获得用户和信誉，到现在宣布独立并抛弃React，引发对其背后动机的质疑。有人认为这是为了迎合大额收购后的投资预期，也有人认为这是创始人希望全栈控制和长期锁定用户。
• 有人指出Remix的新方向是一种“独立宣言”，但这种激进的变化可能让用户失去信任，尤其是在开发工具领域，信任很容易因为不稳定的方向而失去。
• 对比其他在现有技术栈上解决未来问题的项目，Remix的策略显得更内向和自我定义，而非与现有生态合作进化。

44116341.article_content:
May 26, 2025
Wake up, Remix!
Michael Jackson
Co-Founder
Ryan Florence
Co-Founder
At React Conf last summer we announced that Remix was going to "take a nap".
Remix v2 had become such a thin wrapper around React Router that an artificial separation developed between the two projects. We simplified the projects by moving the bundler and server runtime code from Remix directly into React Router v7, merging everything that made Remix great into React Router v7 “framework mode”. We also announced we'd be adding limited support for RSC in React Router.
We finished that work, releasing v7 last November and previewing RSC support last week. This provides a stable platform with long-term support for anyone who built on Remix v1 and v2, or any previous version of React Router.
It's time to go wake up Remix!
React Router is Really Good
When we set out to evolve Remix, we expected it to become a full-stack, RSC-first React framework — a fresh take on the full-stack React architecture.
But something unexpected happened along the way: React Router v7 became really, really good.
Thanks to the work on RSC support in React Router, we now have a smooth, incremental adoption path that supports returning server components directly from loaders and actions. We even built a first-class story for server-only routes — something we originally imagined as part of Remix's next chapter.
If all your routes are server routes, React Router v7 already feels a lot like where Remix was headed. The differences are subtle, not structural.
And it's not just technically solid — it's battle-tested. React Router now powers apps at Shopify, X.com, GitHub, ChatGPT, Linear, T3Chat, and countless others, including nearly 11 million GitHub projects. It's just one minor release away from fully supporting the complete React architecture. It has a dedicated team, long-term backing, and an
open governance model
to keep it growing for years to come.
So what does that mean for Remix?
It means we're free to go build what comes next.
A New Path
Over the past few years, the web platform has made remarkable progress — and so have the tools we use to build on it. But as much as we've gained, we've also seen complexity grow in ways that feel… heavy. At times, modern web development can feel more like navigating a toolchain than building for the web.
We've had ideas that felt too disruptive to pursue in the past. But with Remix no longer tied to a specific paradigm, we have the freedom to explore them.
Remix v3 is a reimagining of what a web framework can be — a fresh foundation shaped by decades of experience building for the web. Our focus is on simplicity, clarity, and performance, without giving up the power developers need.
It's a modular toolkit that works well together but can also stand on its own — from first-class database drivers to a built-in component library (time to wake up Reach UI too!).
This isn't just a new version — it's a new direction. One that's faster, simpler, and closer to the web itself.
To do that, we need to own the full stack — without leaning on layers of abstraction we don't control. That means no critical dependencies, not even React. We're starting with a fork of Preact, a mature virtual DOM library already used heavily at Shopify, Google, and countless others.
If you've ever wished for a development experience that feels lighter, faster, and more aligned with how the web works, Remix v3 is being built for you.
Principles
While we aren't ready with a preview release, we do have the following principles guiding our development:
Model-First Development.
AI fundamentally shifts the human-computer interaction model for both user experience and developer workflows. Optimize the source code, documentation, tooling, and abstractions for LLMs. Additionally, develop abstractions for applications to use models in the product itself, not just as a tool to develop it.
Build on Web APIs.
Sharing abstractions across the stack greatly reduces the amount of context switching, both for humans and machines. Build on the foundation of Web APIs and JavaScript because it is the only full stack ecosystem.
Religiously Runtime.
Designing for bundlers/compilers/typegen (and any pre-runtime static analysis) leads to poor API design that eventually pollutes the entire system. All packages must be designed with no expectation of static analysis and all tests must run without bundling. Because browsers are involved,
--import
loaders for simple transformations like TypeScript and JSX are permissible.
Avoid Dependencies.
Dependencies lock you into somebody else's roadmap. Choose them wisely, wrap them completely, and expect to replace most of them with our own package eventually. The goal is zero.
Demand Composition.
Abstractions should be single-purpose and replaceable. A composable abstraction is
easy to add and remove from an existing program
. Every package must be useful and documented independent of any other context. New features should first be attempte

data.title: The Art of Fugue – Contrapunctus I (2021)
data.author: xeonmc
data.article_summary: 《赋格的艺术》是巴赫生前最后一套作品，因复杂的复调音乐在当时已不再流行，出版后销量不佳，直至1922年才首次完整演出。这套作品旨在教学，而非单纯欣赏，通过各声部的主题反复变奏，如倒置、反向、加速等。首篇《 Contrapunctus I 》相对简单，缺乏复杂的对位技巧，更像即兴创作。巴赫使用开放式谱写，每个声部独立成行，后来常被改编为四重奏等形式演奏。音乐分析显示，该作品主题流畅，和声变化少，强力度终止被避免，某些段落引入不协和音，增加张力。总体上，虽然技术复杂，但听感自由流畅。
