data.title: Nobel Laureate Daron Acemoglu: Don't Believe the AI Hype
data.author: hannofcart
data.article_summary: 文章对当前有关人工智能（AI）将带来巨大生产力提升的乐观预测提出质疑。作者Daron Acemoglu指出，尽管科技行业和媒体普遍认为AI将彻底改变世界经济，但经济理论和数据并不完全支持这些预测。根据现有研究，AI在自动化某些任务和提升部分工人的生产力方面可能产生影响，但总体效果有限。例如，ChatGPT等工具在简单写作任务上能节省约27%的劳动成本，而总体成本节省为14.4%。考虑到AI影响的任务比例（约4.6%），预估AI将在十年内使总要素生产率（TFP）提升0.66%，即每年0.06%。这远低于高盛和麦肯锡预测的数字。除非AI在科学发现或新产品创造上取得重大突破，否则其经济影响将较为有限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对社会、经济和各个行业的长短期影响及其预测的难度

不同观点：
• Nevermark认为，AI等技术的价值影响非常难以预测，尤其是能力进步与价值门槛之间的关系。他指出，技术进步可能不会立刻显现出其全部价值，且价值链的多层次性使得预测更加复杂。上游的突破可能会在下游遇到瓶颈，而下游的小突破可能会释放巨大的价值。

• jqpabc123以制造业为例，指出自动化已经在没有AI的情况下深入发展，比如现代汽车装配线的自动化程度非常高，人力成本在汽车制造中占比很小。他认为AI在制造业的进一步影响可能有限，因为自动化已经高度实现。

• mistercow认为，虽然长期预测AI的影响非常困难，但我们仍可以对未来三年的情况做出一些合理的预测。他强调，近期的经济影响主要涉及现有技术的改进，而对于更远的未来则充满不确定性。

• bko引用1998年诺贝尔奖得主保罗·克鲁格曼的话，指出互联网的影响在初期也曾被低估，并认为AI等新工具对社会和个人生产力的影响可能会逐渐显现。他表示，虽然有些人可能尚未充分利用这些工具，但他个人从中受益匪浅，并对未来持乐观态度。

• r721仅提及当前年份（2024），未展开具体讨论。

• jonstewart质疑某位经济学家的可信度，指出他之前曾为一份虚假AI论文站台，暗示对该专家关于AI影响的预测持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是对AI未来影响的预测可信度。Nevermark和mistercow强调预测的困难，而jonstewart则对某些专家的预测持怀疑态度。
- jqpabc123通过具体数据和实例（如汽车装配线）说明AI在某些领域的影响可能有限。
- bko通过历史类比（互联网的发展）指出，新技术的长期影响可能被低估，并强调个人经验中的积极影响。

Don’t Believe the AI Hype
May 21, 2024
Daron Acemoglu
If you listen to tech industry leaders, business-sector forecasters, and much of the media, you may believe that recent advances in generative AI will soon bring extraordinary productivity benefits, revolutionizing life as we know it. Yet neither economic theory nor the data support such exuberant forecasts.
BOSTON – According to tech leaders and many pundits and academics, artificial intelligence is poised to transform the world as we know it through unprecedented productivity gains. While some believe that machines soon will do
everything
humans can do, ushering in a new age of boundless prosperity, other predictions are at least more grounded. For example, Goldman Sachs
predicts
that generative AI will boost global GDP by 7% over the next decade, and the McKinsey Global Institute
anticipates
that the annual GDP growth rate could increase by 3-4 percentage points between now and 2040. For its part,
The Economist
expects that AI will create a
blue-collar bonanza
.
Trump’s Unworkable Trade Formula
Johannes Eisele/AFP/Getty Images
Economics
1
The Tragedy of Emmanuel Macron
Yves Herman/POOL/AFP via Getty Images
Longer Reads
3
US Fiscal Irresponsibility Is Everyone’s Problem
Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images
Economics
0
Is this realistic? As I note in a
recent paper
, the outlook is far more uncertain than most forecasts and guesstimates suggest. Still, while it is basically impossible to predict with any confidence what AI will do in 20 or 30 years, one can say something about the next decade, because most of these near-term economic effects must involve existing technologies and improvements to them.
It is reasonable to suppose that AI’s biggest impact will come from automating some tasks and making some workers in some occupations more productive. Economic theory provides some guidance for assessing these aggregate effects. According to
Hulten’s theorem
(named for economist Charles Hulten), aggregate “total factor productivity” (TFP) effects are simply the product of the share of tasks that are automated multiplied by the average cost savings.
While average cost savings are difficult to estimate and will vary by activity, there have already been some careful studies of AI’s effects on certain tasks. For example, Shakked Noy and Whitney Zhang have
examined the impact of ChatGPT
on simple writing tasks (such as summarizing documents or writing routine grant proposals or marketing material), while
Erik Brynjolfsson
, Danielle Li, and Lindsey Raymond have
assessed
the use of AI assistants in customer service. Taken together, this research suggests that currently available generative-AI tools yield average labor-cost savings of 27% and overall cost savings of 14.4%.
What about the share of tasks that will be affected by AI and related technologies? Using numbers from
recent studies
, I estimate this to be around 4.6%, implying that AI will increase TFP by only 0.66% over ten years, or by 0.06% annually. Of course, since AI will also drive an investment boom, the increase in GDP growth could be a little larger, perhaps in the 1-1.5% range.
These figures are much smaller than the ones from Goldman Sachs and McKinsey. If you want to get those bigger numbers, you either must boost the productivity gains at the micro level or assume that many more tasks in the economy will be affected. But neither scenario seems plausible. Labor-cost savings far above 27% not only fall out of the range offered by existing studies; they also do not align with the observed effects of other, even more promising technologies. For example, industrial robots have transformed some manufacturing sectors, and they appear to have reduced labor costs by
about 30%
.

It brings together 30 influential individuals from academia, policymaking, civil society, and the private sector — voices challenging conventional wisdom and blazing a new path.

Similarly, we are unlikely to see far more than 4.6% of tasks being taken over, because AI is nowhere close to being able to perform most manual or social tasks (including seemingly simple functions with some social aspects, like accounting). As of 2019, a
survey
of essentially all US businesses found that only about 1.5% of them had any AI investments. Even if such investments have picked up over the past year and a half, we have a long, long way to go before AI becomes widespread.
Of course, AI could have larger effects than my analysis allows if it revolutionizes the process of scientific discovery or creates many new tasks and products. The recent AI-enabled discoveries of new
crystal structure

• mistercow认为，虽然长期预测AI的影响非常困难，但我们仍可以对未来三年的情况做出一些合理的预测。他强调，近期的经济影响主要涉及现有技术的改进，而对于更远的未来则充满不确定性。

• bko引用1998年诺贝尔奖得主保罗·克鲁格曼的话，指出互联网的影响在初期也曾被低估，并认为AI等新工具对社会和个人生产力的影响可能会逐渐显现。他表示，虽然有些人可能尚未充分利用这些工具，但他个人从中受益匪浅，并对未来持乐观态度。

• r721仅提及当前年份（2024），未展开具体讨论。

• jonstewart质疑某位经济学家的可信度，指出他之前曾为一份虚假AI论文站台，暗示对该专家关于AI影响的预测持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点之一是对AI未来影响的预测可信度。Nevermark和mistercow强调预测的困难，而jonstewart则对某些专家的预测持怀疑态度。
- jqpabc123通过具体数据和实例（如汽车装配线）说明AI在某些领域的影响可能有限。
- bko通过历史类比（互联网的发展）指出，新技术的长期影响可能被低估，并强调个人经验中的积极影响。

data.title: RSyncUI – A SwiftUI based macOS GUI for rsync
data.author: mickelsen
data.article_summary: RsyncUI 是一个基于 SwiftUI 的 macOS 应用程序，为命令行工具 rsync 提供图形用户界面（GUI），适用于 macOS Sonoma 及更高版本。它帮助用户组织同步任务和设置 rsync 参数，简化了 rsync 的使用。虽然 GUI 用于任务管理，但实际的同步任务是由 rsync 命令行工具执行的外部任务，RsyncUI 会监控其进度和终止状态，用户可以随时中止任务。RsyncUI 可通过 Homebrew 安装，并且已获得 Apple 的签名和公证。项目文档基于 Hugo 主题 Docsy，并使用 MIT 许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rsync相关工具及其图形界面（GUI）的应用与改进

不同观点：
• [lproven] 对Sonoma系统兼容性表达了担忧，更倾向于使用Monterey系统，并提到了自己使用过的几款rsync相关的工具，如RSyncOSX、ARsync，指出了不同工具的维护状态和兼容性问题。
• [AnonC] 认为Rsync相关的工具非常有用，特别是在重复性任务中，但每次使用需要查阅手册或在线搜索参数。他还建议在文档中加入通过Macports安装rsync的选项，而不仅限于Homebrew。
• [HeckFeck] 对SwiftUI的应用表示赞赏，认为更多的桌面应用程序正在发展，并对此表示欢迎。

data.title: Breaking the Sorting Barrier for Directed Single-Source Shortest Paths
data.author: mahmoudimus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提出了一种确定性的算法，能够在比较加法模型下，以 $O(m\log^{2/3}n)$ 的时间复杂度解决有向图中单源最短路径问题（SSSP），其中 $m$ 是边数，$n$ 是节点数。这是首次打破 Dijkstra 算法在稀疏图中 $O(m + n\log n)$ 时间界限的结果，证明 Dijkstra 算法并非 SSSP 的最优解。文章提供了17页的详细分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新算法是否在实际应用中优于Dijkstra算法

不同观点：
• djoldman认为，如果这个算法在正权重有向图中优于Dijkstra算法，那将是一个惊人的结果。这暗示了Dijkstra算法通常被认为是处理此类问题的最佳选择，因此对新算法的实际效果持怀疑态度。
• djoldman同时也提出了一种怀疑的观点，认为这个新算法可能仅在处理非常小、非常大或奇怪的数据时才有意义，暗示其在常规数据集上的实用性可能有限。

补充讨论：
• 该评论提出了对新算法实际应用价值的质疑，特别是与Dijkstra算法相比的优越性。
• 强调了对新算法在不同数据规模和类型上的表现进行实际验证的重要性。
• 暗示了Dijkstra算法在图算法领域的经典地位，使得任何声称超越它的新算法都需要有强有力的证据支持。

Abstract:
We give a deterministic $O(m\log^{2/3}n)$-time algorithm for single-source shortest paths (SSSP) on directed graphs with real non-negative edge weights in the comparison-addition model. This is the first result to break the $O(m+n\log n)$ time bound of Dijkstra's algorithm on sparse graphs, showing that Dijkstra's algorithm is not optimal for SSSP.

data.title: Zero-overhead checks with fake stack overflows
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了虚拟机如何在多线程环境中实现零开销检查，特别是通过伪栈溢出机制。为避免频繁锁定内存分配器、垃圾收集器和编译器等共享资源，VM实现者通常为每个线程分配独立资源片。当需要所有线程停止时，传统方法是通过定期检查标志，但这会引入显著开销。为此，Skybison等虚拟机将同步检查与栈溢出检查结合，在栈推入时进行检查。如果主线程需要同步其他线程，可通过缩小其他线程的最大栈大小触发溢出检查，进入慢速路径后再进行其他标志检查。类似技术也被用于处理热循环中的线程同步检查，如CPython、PyPy和Ruby的YARV。PyPy还将其应用于采样剖析中，检查托儿所耗尽情况以决定是否采样。本文最后提到未来可能讨论防护页相关内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过页面故障机制处理循环和中断的实现方法

不同观点：
• Vardump描述了一种通过页面故障（page fault）机制处理循环和中断的实现方法。具体做法是让循环从特定页面加载数据，当需要中断时，将该页面标记为不可读，从而触发页面故障以实现中断处理。

• 这种方法的论据和例子：Vardump通过实际操作演示了如何利用内存管理中的页面故障机制来处理中断，提供了页面标记不可读的具体技术细节，并指出了页面故障在循环处理中的作用。

补充讨论：
• 这种方法的核心在于利用操作系统或硬件的内存管理机制（页面故障）来实现程序控制流的切换，可能在一些需要高效处理中断的场景中具有优势。

• 争议焦点：虽然这种方法在技术上具有创新性，但其复杂性和对系统底层机制的依赖可能会引发关于其实际应用中的稳定性和可维护性的讨论。例如，其他开发者可能会质疑这种方法在不同硬件平台或操作系统上的兼容性和可靠性。

• 进一步讨论的可能方向包括该方法在不同系统架构下的适用性、与其他中断处理机制的比较，以及实际应用中的性能表现等。

Zero-overhead checks with fake stack overflows
May 28, 2025
Imagine you have a virtual machine for a dynamic language. It supports starting
multiple threads from within the guest language via some API. This is
immediately challenging right out the gate because it requires keeping some key
runtime-internal state in sync:
memory allocator / garbage collector
compiler
other bookkeeping
Instead of locking these components so that only one thread can use those
shared resources at a time, runtime implementors tend to shard them: each
thread gets its own slice to work with privately.
This means that each thread might have a separate mini-heap that it can use
privately until exhaustion, and only then request a stop-the-world event. But
how do we indicate that all threads should stop?
We could do something like check for a flag every N instructions, but this
introduces significant overhead in the interpreter and does not play well with
a compiler. Instead, ideally, there would be no overhead in the fast and normal
case.
VM implementors have decided to solve this by folding the synchronization check
into an existing check.
Skybison
, for example, folds this check into the
stack overflow check.
On frame push, we have to check for a stack overflow anyway, so we can re-use
the slow path. If the main thread wants to synchronize the other
threads—because the programmer hit Control-C in the REPL, for example,
causing an interrupt—it can artificially shrink the maximum stack size of the
other threads. Then, the next time the other threads call a function, they will
hit this overflow check and go to the slow path. In the slow path, they can
disambiguate by checking another flag somewhere else.

nullptr
;
}
Frame
*
result
=
pushNativeFrameImpl
(
locals_offset
);
handleInterruptWithFrame
();
return
result
;
}

something very similar in Maglev
on function entry.
But not all applications involve regular function calls. Sometimes it’s
possible to have a hot loop in which no frames are pushed to the call stack. In
this case, it might make sense to check for interrupts (or do other thread
synchronization checks) in loop back-edges. CPython
does this
. PyPy
does too. Ruby’s YARV does this too.
/* set PC to (PC + dst). */
DEFINE_INSN
jump
(
OFFSET
dst
)
()
()
/* Same discussion as leave. */
// attr bool leaf = leafness_of_check_ints; /* has rb_threadptr_execute_interrupts() */
{
RUBY_VM_CHECK_INTS
(
ec
);
JUMP
(
dst
);
}
I’m writing this post because PyPy
published a post
about a new feature
that uses a similar technique! For sampling profiling, they put their check
(whether or not to sample) behind a check for exhaustion of the nursery (small
heap).

RBS…

CF Bolz-Tereick
for feedback on this post!

44122601.article_summary: 本文讨论了虚拟机如何在多线程环境中实现零开销检查，特别是通过伪栈溢出机制。为避免频繁锁定内存分配器、垃圾收集器和编译器等共享资源，VM实现者通常为每个线程分配独立资源片。当需要所有线程停止时，传统方法是通过定期检查标志，但这会引入显著开销。为此，Skybison等虚拟机将同步检查与栈溢出检查结合，在栈推入时进行检查。如果主线程需要同步其他线程，可通过缩小其他线程的最大栈大小触发溢出检查，进入慢速路径后再进行其他标志检查。类似技术也被用于处理热循环中的线程同步检查，如CPython、PyPy和Ruby的YARV。PyPy还将其应用于采样剖析中，检查托儿所耗尽情况以决定是否采样。本文最后提到未来可能讨论防护页相关内容。

data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 在2025年Computex上，英特尔发布了Pro B系列GPU，包括B50和B60型号。这些显卡基于当前的Battlemage架构，拥有更大的内存和专门的驱动程序，特别适合人工智能（AI）应用。B50拥有16GB内存，B60则有24GB内存，能够有效提升AI性能。英特尔还展示了双B60卡配置，达到接近48GB的内存，价格较Nvidia和AMD的类似产品更低。此外，英特尔推出了"Battlematrix"项目，通过在Xeon处理器中插入四张双B60卡，构建高效能系统。英特尔的AI辅助视频调试功能也在展示中，通过自主发现和修复代码错误，大幅提升生产力。总体而言，B50和B60在中期市场表现出色，具有竞争优势。

44123757.article_content:
Intel Shows Off Professional Battlemage Cards
Computex 2025: Interesting choice for some use cases
May 27, 2025
by
Charlie Demerjian
Tweet
Last week at Computex, Intel released their Pro B-Series GPUs, the B50 and B60. On the surface it doesn’t seem like much but SemiAccurate thinks there is a lot of good here.
<rant>Lets start out with the elephant in the room, the Intel GPU roadmap. With the Battlemage/B GPUs, Intel finally has a hit on their hands. Sure it isn’t perfect but it is solid, has a great reputation, and demand is outstripping supply. This bodes well for the C-Series cards, right? Well talking with partners at the show, it seems like the C-Series has yet to get the green light for production. This may be due to management changes, market outlooks, or something SemiAccurate is not privy to. Our advice is to get the ball moving, Intel’s systemic inability to build on success of late needs to be put to rest once and for all. This is a golden opportunity to do so.</rant>
Baby, Mama, and Papa Battlemages
Back to the release of the pro-B GPUs which are basically the current Battlemage GPUs with a new driver and more memory, plus a few twists. The twists are a very large memory complement and a dual GPU card, both really useful for the intended purpose of the GPUs, basically AI. Yes you can say the pro drivers are useful for the traditional CAD and simulation software market, but lets face it, if you don’t lead with AI, no one cares any more. Yes this is sad but it is the reality of the market.
Two new Pro series Battlemage GPUs
` If you have been following the Intel GPU story to date you know that the current cards are firmly in the middle segment of the market, blame the long delays to market on that. This isn’t a slight, they are priced right, perform really well, have stable drivers, and are affordable. With AMD and Nvidia essentially cutting volume for enthusiast parts to near zero, Intel has a golden opportunity here (Authors note: *HINT*). Now in the pro/AI segment, they are repeating the same playbook.
Booth staff show off cards to Computex attendees
So if you have a reasonably priced card that outperforms it’s price by a noticeable amount, why should you buy it over an established player? Drivers and outsized memory specs. The B50 has 16GB and the B60 comes with 24GB, and since memory space is what determines a lot of AI performance, Battlemage has a lot going for it. Sure you can get an Nvidia card with larger memory space now but it also comes with an added bonus in the form of extra zeroes on the price and allocation time. Pick your poison.
Intel’s answer to having a mid-range device in a market where the high end dominates the headlines and price seems to be ignored is to show scaling. This is done in two ways, first the
dual B60 card from Maxsun
is touted as a 48GB AI device which it is. Sort of. 2x24GB not the same as 48GB of contiguous memory but given how tightly coupled a dual card is, it is about as close as you can get. And the price should still be way below an Nvidia or AMD card of similar performance. But dual cards are just a building block for a system which brings us to…
Put it all together and get a Battlematrix
Project Battlematrix is another in a line of halo products with a cool name slapped on. Take an Intel Xeon with PCIe5 slots and slap in four dual B60 cards. This is not a big trick since most Xeons of late support way more than the needed PCIe5 lane count and the B-Series cards only need x8 slots to perform. Intel has an optimized software stack for this configuration including drivers and a tuned Linux stack. So far so good. The pitch is that you can respond to more requests with lower response times than a single device of comparable performance not to mention price. So far so good and they have a bunch of graphs to prove it.
Intel AI assisted video debugging
One of the cooler use cases that we have seen of late is the video debug process. If you are developing hardware or software and there is an error, finding the error is hard enough but tying it back to a specific bit of code is painful and time consuming. The demo Intel had was to have AI ‘watch’ the video, see an error, hunt down the code that screwed up, and fix it. This is all done autonomously, at least in theory, and should be orders of magnitude faster than having meat sacks doing the same job. Even if the AI can only do some of the functions, it should be a massive benefit to productivity.
You can see a bunch of other use cases for the multi-GPU model, running different AIs with some subordinate to others, each with a specific use case for example. You can do this on a single big card but memory constraints and task switching/parameter reloading eventually bite. This is the long way of saying Intel is pointing out the use cases their cards work for but they are actually real use cases that have actual applicability in the market.
Overall the B50 and B60 look like solid players in the mid-market at a goo

data.title: A thought on JavaScript "proof of work" anti-scraper systems
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文解释了为何某些用户在访问博客"Wandering Thoughts"或其所属的CSpace时会被阻止。原因是为减少高流量爬虫（尤其是为LLM训练收集数据的老旧Chrome爬虫）对网站造成的负担，网站主采取了阻挡疑似旧浏览器的措施。若用户确实在使用新版浏览器却遭遇阻挡，可联系网站主提供所用浏览器的详细信息（如User-Agent字符串）。此外，使用archive.*服务的用户（如archive.today, archive.ph）也可能受影响，因这些服务使用与恶意爬虫类似的方式爬取页面。建议使用行为更规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网页内容的微支付与反爬虫机制（尤其是工作量证明，Proof of Work, PoW）

不同观点：
• **myself248**：认为PoW系统可能实现了多年前的网页微支付概念，用户通过计算工作量来支付内容。
• **ChocolateGod**：批评这种做法，认为这会导致不必要的电力消耗，尤其对预算有限的手机用户不友好，且LLM爬虫可能仍会胜出，导致普通用户体验变差。
• **sznio**：支持PoW系统，认为这对网站爬虫操作影响不大，且相比CAPTCHA更方便，特别是对没有RSS或API的网站。
• **benregenspan**：指出已有先例，一些分析供应商使用类似技术来检测和利用客户端资源进行API请求。
• **DaSHacka**：建议将PoW系统用于反爬虫，并通过让爬虫进行无用的哈希计算来获利。
• **avastel**：认为PoW对简单爬虫或DDoS攻击有效，但对专业爬虫效果有限，并指出已有技术可以绕过复杂的PoW系统，同时提到这会增加普通用户的负担。
• **persnickety**：质疑PoW系统的必要性，认为威胁用户使用恶意代码是不合理的，建议标准化一种无风险的PoW算法。
• **dannyw**：不同意persnickety的观点，认为主要的LLM爬虫已经能执行JavaScript，且通过限制运行时间可以控制问题。
• **dxuh**：支持JavaScript挖矿作为广告的替代 monetization 方式，认为只要不过分，用户是可以接受的。
• **bob1029**：认为反爬虫的战斗无法通过这种方式获胜，因为LLM爬虫不需要实时同步整个互联网内容。
• **kbenson**：支持PoW系统，认为可以让LLM等爬虫为其使用的资源付费，并建议Cloudflare等服务提供类似选项。
• **berkes**：怀疑任何反爬虫系统的有效性，担心浏览器厂商可能利用安装基础进行数据抓取。
• **forty**：建议开发有实际用途的PoW算法，如寻找大素数，以避免资源浪费。
• **hardwaresofton**：支持PoW反爬虫工具，但认为最终解决方案可能是对所有网页进行登录限制，并讨论了知识经济价值的问题。
• **keepamovin**：分享了通过Python脚本监控资源使用，并杀死过度消耗资源的进程的经验。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于PoW系统对普通用户和专业爬虫的有效性及其对用户体验的影响。
• 有人建议开发更有意义的计算任务以替代纯粹的资源消耗。
• 讨论中还涉及了反爬虫技术的可行性及其实际应用中的复杂性，包括可能带来的经济利益和用户负担。

44094109.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: Write Terraform policies in natural language instead of Rego / OPA
data.author: igorzij
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Infrabase的规则库，通过GitHub仓库展示了如何使用自然语言编写基础设施即代码（IaC）的安全策略和配置检查。与传统的OPA/Rego/Sentinel相比，Infrabase利用大语言模型（如Gemini）简化了策略编写过程，用户只需用简单的自然语言描述规则，如禁止重复的AWS安全组规则。Infrabase支持多种IaC工具，如Terraform、Pulumi等，且默认启用基本规则，用户仅需在需要时自定义规则。规则需存储在特定文件夹中，并以Markdown格式编写，建议按主题组织规则文件。Infrabase还集成了GitHub高级安全功能，能将检查结果以SARIF格式上传。

不同观点：
• **反对信任LLM生成合规和安全规则**：  
  lowsong认为，不能信任LLM生成合规和安全的规则。他的主要论据是，LLM在这方面的错误输出比没有安全措施更糟糕。因为用户可能会被误导，以为有安全保障，而实际上这些保障并不存在。这种误信可能导致更大的安全隐患。

• **潜在支持LLM在其他领域的应用**：  
 虽然lowsong明确反对在合规和安全领域使用LLM，但没有直接提及是否反对LLM在其他非安全相关领域的应用。这暗示他可能认可LLM在其他不太关键领域的使用，但在合规和安全方面，他的态度非常谨慎。

补充讨论：
• **用户误信的风险**：  
 评论中特别提到，LLM的错误输出可能导致用户误以为有安全措施。这个误信问题是一个关键争议点，因为不仅涉及到技术准确性，还涉及到用户对技术的信任和理解。

• **安全性的特殊性**：  
 评论指出，合规和安全规则具有高度敏感性和特殊性，错误可能带来严重后果。因此，在这些领域使用LLM需要格外谨慎，可能需要额外的验证和监督机制。

总结：评论主要围绕是否可以信任LLM生成合规和安全的规则展开。反对者认为LLM在这方面的错误输出风险极高，可能误导用户，从而造成安全隐患。争议焦点在于用户对LLM输出内容的信任以及安全性本身的特殊要求。

Write policies in natural language
This is an example repository of custom rules for
Infrabase
. It's a GitHub app that detects security issues and other misconfigurations in your IaC pull requests. You can write Infrabase policies in natural language instead of OPA / Rego / Sentinel; this repo contains some examples.
Quick start
Create an account at
dashboard.infrabase.co
Fork this repo (optional; only if you want to use custom rules)
Install the Infrabase GitHub app into the repos you'd like to review and take policies from (including your fork of this repo)
Create a pull request with some infrastructure changes. Shortly Infrabase will report on findings in the comment
Motivation
Policy-as-code is one of those things that everyone knows should be done, but in practice is rarely implemented.
How come? We believe this is caused by the combination of the following 2 factors:
OPA is cumbersome, so writing even a single policy takes a lot of effort
Each policy project needs to start from scratch because policies aren't re-usable
Infrabase checks your infra with an LLM instead of policies directly (
gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06
). You can write your own policies as natural language prompts to customize behaviour - just fork this repo and connect it to Infrabase GitHub app.
See the difference
✅ Infrabase policy - just one line!
No two aws_security_group_rule resources may define an identical ingress rule (same security-group ID, protocol, from/to port, and CIDR block).
❌ Alternative: 61 lines of Rego:
package sg_unique
import future.keywords
# Helper: recursively yield every resource block (root + child modules)
all_resources[r] {
# walk over the input object and pick leaves whose keys are "resources"
some path, idx
walk(input, path, reslist)
last(path) == "resources"
r := reslist[idx]
}
# Flatten each aws_security_group_rule resource into atomic "rule units"
unit_rules[u] {
r := all_resources[_]
r.type == "aws_security_group_rule"
r.mode == "managed"                      # ignore data / config-driven
is_ingress := r.values.type == "ingress"
# explode cidr_blocks list; if empty treat as ["0.0.0.0/0"]
cidr := r.values.cidr_blocks[_]
when := is_ingress                       # only ingress rules in scope
u := {
"addr": r.address,                     # resource address for messaging
"sg":   r.values.security_group_id,
"proto": r.values.protocol,
"from":  r.values.from_port,
"to":    r.values.to_port,
"cidr":  cidr
}
}
# Detect duplicates: identical rule parameters but different resource addresses
dupes[[u1.addr, u2.addr, u1]] {
u1 := unit_rules[_]
u2 := unit_rules[_]
u1.addr < u2.addr                       # deterministic ordering
u1.sg   == u2.sg
u1.proto == u2.proto
u1.from  == u2.from
u1.to    == u2.to
u1.cidr  == u2.cidr
}
# Policy decision
deny[msg] {
pair := dupes[_]
ru   := pair[2]                         # representative rule params
msg := sprintf(
"Duplicate ingress rule (%s %d-%d %s on %s) in %s and %s",
[ru.proto, ru.from, ru.to, ru.cidr, ru.sg, pair[0], pair[1]]
)
}
default allow = count(deny) == 0
Features
Supports Terraform, OpenTofu, Terragrunt, CDK, CDKTF, CloudFormation, Pulumi
Sensible defaults, "on" by default. Only write policies to customise (add new rules or disable existing ones).
Does not require access to state or cloud account
Summary table of findings, ordered by severity. Works well with big PRs and large monorepos.
Integrated with GitHub Advanced Security (GAS) alerts - findings are uploaded as SARIF files
Write policies in natural language (fork this repo)
Structure and conventions
Rules need to be stored in the
policies
folder as markdown files. No other folders or file types are considered.
Each rule file can be structured arbitrarily, but the more explicitly you separate and phrase them the better. General prompt engineering best practices apply. Suggested simple structure that can be a good start: for each rule, write a heading that summarises the key point - e.g. "no public S3 buckets allowed" - followed by a paragraph that adds more detail. For best results use short, definitive sentences. Examples in this repo follow this pattern.
You can have as many files as you want - so it might make sense to group them by topic. For example,
security.md
for security rules and
style.md
for code style rules.
Troubleshooting
Rules are not refreshed after commit: try removing the rules repo from the Infrabase github app installation and then adding again.

data.author: simonpure
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为ScienceBoard的平台，用于评估多模态自主代理在实际科学工作流中的表现。该平台包括两个主要部分：（i）一个多领域、多界面的动态科学工作流环境，代理可以在其中与专业软件互动，自动执行复杂的研究任务；（ii）一个包含169个高质量、经过严格验证的真实世界任务的基准，涵盖生物化学、天文学和地理信息学等领域。尽管一些基于LLM（如GPT-4o和Claude 3.7）的代理展现出潜力，但它们在复杂工作流中的总体成功率仅为15%。文章深入分析了当前代理的局限性，并提出了更有效的设计原则，以推动科学发现的自动化进程。平台的代码和环境已公开。

Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have extended their impact beyond Natural Language Processing, substantially fostering the development of interdisciplinary research. Recently, various LLM-based agents have been developed to assist scientific discovery progress across multiple aspects and domains. Among these, computer-using agents, capable of interacting with operating systems as humans do, are paving the way to automated scientific problem-solving and addressing routines in researchers' workflows. Recognizing the transformative potential of these agents, we introduce ScienceBoard, which encompasses two complementary contributions: (i) a realistic, multi-domain environment featuring dynamic and visually rich scientific workflows with integrated professional software, where agents can autonomously interact via different interfaces to accelerate complex research tasks and experiments; and (ii) a challenging benchmark of 169 high-quality, rigorously validated real-world tasks curated by humans, spanning scientific-discovery workflows in domains such as biochemistry, astronomy, and geoinformatics. Extensive evaluations of agents with state-of-the-art backbones (e.g., GPT-4o, Claude 3.7, UI-TARS) show that, despite some promising results, they still fall short of reliably assisting scientists in complex workflows, achieving only a 15% overall success rate. In-depth analysis further provides valuable insights for addressing current agent limitations and more effective design principles, paving the way to build more capable agents for scientific discovery. Our code, environment, and benchmark are at

.

data.title: Running GPT-2 in WebGL: Rediscovering the Lost Art of GPU Shader Programming
data.author: nathan-barry
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了如何利用WebGL和着色器（shaders）实现GPT-2模型，并探讨了通用GPU（GPGPU）编程的发展和原理。文章首先回顾了GPU编程的起源，指出NVIDIA在2000年代初通过GeForce 3和GeForce FX引入了可编程着色器，使开发者能更灵活地控制渲染管线。研究者发现，某些计算任务（如线性代数）可以通过将它们转化为图形操作来加速。

然而，使用图形API（如OpenGL的GLSL）进行非图形任务较为繁琐。为此，NVIDIA在2006年推出了CUDA，使得开发者可以直接利用GPU的计算能力，而无需通过图形API。CUDA提供了一种更直接的并行计算模型，允许开发者编写C/C++代码，并明确管理GPU内存和并行内核。

文章还比较了图形API和计算API的区别，指出OpenCL和CUDA更适合大规模并行计算任务。最后，文章详细介绍了如何利用WebGL的纹理、帧缓冲对象和其他图形概念来实现GPT-2模型，将图形管线用于通用计算任务。

总结而言，文章探讨了GPGPU编程的历史、技术和实际应用，特别是通过WebGL和着色器实现GPT-2模型的过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WebGL与现代图形计算技术在实现高效渲染和通用计算方面的优缺点，以及向WebGPU等新技术的迁移。

不同观点：
• cmovq：指出使用两个三角形进行渲染会造成碎片重复计算的问题，建议使用一个超出视口的大三角形，通过裁剪来提高效率。
• flakiness：认为CUDA在性能上更优，但传统着色器的纯函数性质概念简单，且具有美学上的吸引力，特别是在不追求极高性能的情况下。
• nathan-barry：分享了使用WebGL和着色器实现GPT-2的经验，并详细介绍了使用纹理和帧缓冲对象进行计算的方法。
• grg0：反对原帖中关于着色器编程过时的观点，认为着色器编程至今仍非常重要，并指出WebGL 2支持计算着色器，建议聚焦于前计算API的局限性。
• rezmason：赞赏nathan-barry的实现，认为如果切换到WebGPU可能会有显著性能提升，同时肯定了WebGL的价值。
• swoorup：提到gpu.js等JavaScript库可以通过传统渲染路径模拟通用计算，提供了一种跨平台的GPU计算方法。
• nickpsecurity：讨论了使用OpenCL进行跨平台GPU计算的可能性，并建议将技术移植到较旧或较便宜的硬件上进行实验。
• 0points：质疑“着色器编程是失落的艺术”的说法，提到现代技术如mega shaders和Vulkan llm等仍很活跃。
• lerp-io：指出现在可以使用WebGPU计算着色器。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于着色器编程是否过时，以及在实现高效渲染和计算时WebGL与WebGPU等新技术的相对优劣。
• 讨论中还涉及了多种技术如CUDA、OpenCL、gpu.js等的比较，以及对旧硬件和跨平台支持的考虑。
• 有人提出WebGPU可能是未来的发展方向，但也肯定了WebGL的成熟和广泛应用。

44109257.article_content:
Running GPT-2 in WebGL: Rediscovering GPGPU Shader Programming
May, 24 2025 •
16 min read •
2440 words
Preface: A few weeks back, I implemented GPT-2 using WebGL and shaders (
Github Repo
) which made the front page of Hacker News (
discussion
). By popular demand, here is a short write-up over the main ideas behind General-Purpose GPU shader programming.
Table Of Contents
The Origins of General-Purpose GPU Programming
In the early 2000s, NVIDIA introduced programmable shaders with the GeForce 3 (2001) and GeForce FX (2003). Instead of being limited to predetermined transformations and effects of earlier GPUs, developers were now given unprecedented control over the rendering pipeline, enabling much more sophisticated visual effects. These programmable shaders laid the foundation for modern GPU computing.
Researchers soon discovered that certain computations (like linear algebra involving matrices and vectors) could be accelerated by casting them as graphics operations on the GPU.
However, using shader languages like OpenGL’s GLSL for no-graphics tasks was cumbersome. By the mid-2000s, the need for a more straightforward, non-graphics interface to GPUs had become clear, and NVIDIA saw a new opportunity.
Inspired by the demand for
general-purpose GPU (GPGPU)
programming, in November 2006, NVIDIA released
CUDA
, the
Compute Unified Device Architecture
. CUDA is a parallel computing platform and programming model that gives developers direct access to the GPU’s computational power without the intermediary of a graphics API. With CUDA, one could write C/C++ code to execute on the CPU using straightforward extensions for parallel kernels and managing GPU memory explicitly. This meant that developers could now ignore graphics-specific concepts and dramatically lowered the barrier for general-purpose GPU computing. Following CUDA came OpenCL which expanded general purpose computing beyond the NVIDIA ecosystem.
Graphics API vs Compute API
Traditional graphics APIs like OpenGL are centered around a fixed-function pipeline tailored for rendering images. The pipeline consists of stages like vertex processing, rasterization, fragment processing, etc. Each stage can be programmable with shaders, but the overall flow is fixed.
Using the OpenGL graphics pipeline to do general-purpose computation required a lot of boilerplate. One had to pack data into texture formats, use off-screen framebuffers to capture the results, and often perform multiple render passes to accomplish multi-stage algorithms.
In contrast, OpenCL and CUDA expose a direct compute model:
Kernels, not shaders
: You write a function and then launch thousands of copies to run in parallel (no notion of vertices or fragments).
Raw buffers
: Allocate arrays of floats or integers, read/write them directly, and move them back and forth between host and device with explicit copy calls.
User-driven pipeline
: You define exactly what happens and when instead of using a predefined fixed sequence of rendering stages.
The result is a far more natural fit for linear algebra, simulations, physics, ML, and any algorithm where you just want to compute independent calculations in bulk.
In OpenGL, the output would ultimately be pixels in a framebuffer or values in a texture; in OpenCL, the output can be data in any form (float arrays, computed lists of numbers, etc.) which you then transfer back to the CPU or use in further computations. This makes OpenCL more suitable for general algorithms where you just want the numerical results.
Implementing GPT-2 with shaders
Below covers textures, framebuffers, vertex and fragment shaders, and other graphics specific concepts I hijacked to get GPT-2 running on a GPU using shaders.
Textures & Framebuffers: The Data Bus
In traditional graphics rendering, a
texture

文章主要介绍了如何利用WebGL和着色器（shaders）实现GPT-2模型，并探讨了通用GPU（GPGPU）编程的发展和原理。文章首先回顾了GPU编程的起源，指出NVIDIA在2000年代初通过GeForce 3和GeForce FX引入了可编程着色器，使开发者能更灵活地控制渲染管线。研究者发现，某些计算任务（如线性代数）可以通过将它们转化为图形操作来加速。

然而，使用图形API（如OpenGL的GLSL）进行非图形任务较为繁琐。为此，NVIDIA在2006年推出了CUDA，使得开发者可以直接利用GPU的计算能力，而无需通过图形API。CUDA提供了一种更直接的并行计算模型，允许开发者编写C/C++代码，并明确管理GPU内存和并行内核。

文章还比较了图形API和计算API的区别，指出OpenCL和CUDA更适合大规模并行计算任务。最后，文章详细介绍了如何利用WebGL的纹理、帧缓冲对象和其他图形概念来实现GPT-2模型，将图形管线用于通用计算任务。

总结而言，文章探讨了GPGPU编程的历史、技术和实际应用，特别是通过WebGL和着色器实现GPT-2模型的过程。

data.title: The Ingredients of a Productive Monorepo
data.author: mifydev
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在工程组织向**单体仓库**（monorepo）迁移时，开发者生产力团队面临的挑战和所需工具。作者基于在大公司和小型初创企业的工作经验，指出并没有一套现成工具能完全解决单体仓库的所有问题，团队可能需要自行开发工具。单体仓库的优势包括**一致性**、**组织连贯性**和**共享工具**，但也会带来新的问题，初期可能出现效率倒退。

关键原则是任何仓库操作必须是**O(change)**，而非**O(repo)**，以确保在大型仓库中保持性能。Git是常见选择，但其设计并非针对单体仓库，当仓库变大时性能可能下降。解决方案包括微软的**修改Git**、Meta的**修改Mercurial**，或谷歌的**自研系统**。团队需明确为何要使用单体仓库，并根据实际情况选择技术路径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： monorepo 与 multirepo 的优劣对比，以及在大型组织中实施 monorepo 的实际挑战和工具支持。

不同观点：
• **支持 monorepo 的观点**：
  - **bob1029**：认为 monorepo 通过原子性提交简化了多开发者的协调工作，即使是团队之间不直接合作，monorepo 也能作为管理和HR工具使用。
  - **bittermandel**：通过 Bazel 建立的 monorepo 帮助小团队高效工作，工具层确保所有人使用相同版本的工具，减少了维护本地环境的负担。
  - **ecoffey**：幽默地表示，唯一比在 monorepo 中工作更糟糕的就是不在 monorepo 中工作。

• **对 monorepo 的批评和挑战**：
  - **lxe**：指出两种 monorepo 类型，尤其提到大型科技公司的 monorepo 需要大量时间和资源来建立，且伴随巨大的痛苦。
  - **AlotOfReading**：提出 monorepo 可能导致组织结构问题，例如在基础设施团队中引发个人英雄主义，且由于潜在的破坏性，任何更改都会变得复杂。
  - **spankalee**：指出在 monorepo 中，团队可能不愿意其他团队依赖他们的代码，从而减少了代码重用，增加了库团队的负担。

• **中立和实际情况**：
  - **rwieruch**：认为 monorepo 像“伪装的 polyrepo”，每个项目可以独立开发和部署，但共享一个代码库，强调工具的重要性。
  - **yc-kraln**：认为 monorepo 和 multirepo 各有优劣，具体选择取决于愿意忍受哪种痛苦，强调了权衡和实际操作中的复杂性。

补充讨论：
• **工具和技术支持**：
  - **Flux159**：提到大规模构建系统需要专门的团队维护，开发通常在开发服务器上进行，而不是本地笔记本。
  - **lihaoyi**：详细讨论了 monorepo 工具的复杂性，指出成功背后往往有其他团队的支持。
  - **chrismatic**：强调使用单一语言工具链的重要性，并介绍了自己简化的构建工具 "Grog"。
  - **cormacrelf**：讨论了不同构建系统与IDE的集成问题，指出需要标准化以支持多种IDE。

• **组织影响和版本控制**：
  - **AlotOfReading**：指出 monorepo 可能通过逆康威定律影响组织结构和问题解决方式。
  - **KaiserPro**：提到 monorepo 默认只提供当前版本，组织需要考虑如何处理版本控制和依赖管理。

争议焦点：
• monorepo 是否真正简化了开发协调，还是引入了新的复杂性和负担。
• 工具链的支持和IDE集成问题在 monorepo 中的实际影响。
• 组织结构和代码重用在 monorepo 环境下的挑战。

总结：讨论围绕 monorepo 的实际应用展开，支持者强调其在协调和统一管理上的优势，批评者则指出其潜在的复杂性和实施难度。工具支持和组织影响也是讨论的重要方面。

44086917.article_content:
So! Suppose you’re an intrepid engineer in a nascent Developer Productivity
team. Your engineering organization has decided that it wants to
move towards a
monorepo
. You’ve heard the stories
told of Google, Meta, Uber - each a large technology company with
developer productivity organizations consisting of hundreds of engineers -
and you want to capture some of their magic in a bottle and give it to your
users. You wonder - what work lies ahead of you?
I’ve worked in a variety of companies, from gigantic titans to small startups
and everything in-between, and I’ve worked in developer infrastructure for
almost all of them. My experience is informed by my own successes and
failures operating within these companies and trying to solve productivity
problems of the developers I served. I’ve observed that a functioning
monorepo environment demands the existence of a number of tools that you,
dear Developer Productivity engineer, will likely need to write yourself for
your company. I have yet to witness a suite of tools that fully solves the
set of problems that you will encounter when setting up a monorepo. In this
blog post I’m going to enumerate these tools and discuss implementation
strategies for them, in the hopes of painting a clear picture of the path
that lies ahead for any organization that walks the monorepo path.
The absolute first question you must ask yourself, though, is:
Why do you want a monorepo?
You and your engineering organization must stare at this question deeply and
answer it using language that is firmly anchored in your organization’s
culture and values. Those blog posts that you read from Google, Facebook, or
Uber engineers about how great their monorepo is, and how effective their
developers are, and how everybody will be a 10x engineer when you’re done?
Purge them from your mind.
You WILL NOT end up with an experience as tight as
google3
1
or
fbsource
2
. You WILL inherit a new set of problems that many-repo
setup did not have. You will take steps backward before you take steps
forward. These blog posts and the wins they promise are not good reasons
to embark on this journey. The
cool
engineering
blogs
from these big companies
are discussing end states that, while very interesting, are far beyond the
capabilities of your company and your small team. You will not have the
same outcomes if you attempt to do what they have done.
Better reasons to embark on this journey are
consistency
,
organizational coherence
, and
shared tooling efforts
. Your developer
productivity gets to focus on improving the experience of working in
a single place and can reach more users in the process. Your engineering leadership gets to define and enforce
engineering conventions. Engineers working in different organizations can
contribute to each other’s codebases with the knowledge that they look and
operate the same way.
You, intrepid Developer Productivity engineer, have the opportunity and
responsibility to pave a path for your colleagues. Let’s get to work.
The Golden Rule
If you can forgive this abuse of
big-O notation
, this principle guides all
engineering for monorepo-related developer tools:
Any operation over your repository that needs to be fast must be O(change) and not O(repo)
.
As you begin to use your normal sets of tools in a large monorepo, you will
find that many tools and processes do not have this property and will cause
you problems as your monorepo grows. We will
repeatedly
come back to this
design principle in every section that this blog post discusses. When you
see a blog post from a big company talking about some engineering that they
did on a developer tool, it is almost always the implementation of this
principle in a space in which an
O(repo)
operation has become a problem.
Source Control
Perhaps the most obvious consequence of storing all of your source code
together in one repository is that, well, all of your source code is stored
together.
git
is the default choice for many software companies today and, despite
git
being designed as decentralized source control system, many
users use
git
through a software forge such as GitHub or GitLab. The reality is that
git
was never designed for the centralized monorepo and
runs into substantial performance problems when your history gets large or
your repo contains many, many files
3
.
Your repo probably isn’t big enough to have problems with
git
. You can push
git
and GitHub pretty far these days. However, git is
(by design) a
O(repo)
system, and operations such as
git status
will
slow down rapidly as the size of the repository grows.
If your monorepo begins to push the limits of git (or GitHub!), you have
several paths available to you, each walked by a company that came before you:
You walk the path of Microsoft and
fork git
.
You walk the path of Meta and
fork Mercurial
.
You walk the path of Google and
write your own
, although Google also managed to get pretty far by running Perforce on the most powerful servers that money could bu

data.title: My website is ugly because I made it
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者对自己个人网站设计的独特追求和演变过程。作者强调，网站是他的个人表达，不同于追求极简和美观的设计，他通过CSS创造了一种混乱但有趣的链接排列方式，并加入互动效果，如鼠标悬停时产生的旋转效果，以及通过合成纹理营造纸张或星空的视觉感受。他的设计灵感来源于“使用过的书店”的感觉，并不断变化以反映他个人的成长和转变。文章传达了个人创作的独特价值，以及每个人在创作中不断变化和探索的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人网站是否应使用手工打造的HTML/CSS以及是否应遵循现代网页设计标准

不同观点：
• [ayaros] 认为手工打造的网站不一定是丑陋的，但随着网站内容增多，可能会变得难以管理，需要重新设计。他强调网站需要在桌面和移动端都有良好的用户界面设计，同时不依赖JavaScript以保证功能性。
• [donatj] 享受手工打造网站的过程，认为这是一种乐趣，类似于维护经典汽车。他不想把这种乐趣交给现成的模板，因为那样会失去对设计和功能的掌控。
• [susam] 也手工打造了自己的网站，并使用Common Lisp程序来自动化一些任务。他认为现成的工具虽然不错，但不符合他的需求，手工打造的网站更简单且完全在他的控制之下。
• [mcdonje] 更倾向于访问没有营销cookies和会员弹窗的网站，即使这些网站看起来"丑陋"。他批评现代网站设计中常见的营销策略。
• [luckyandroid] 怀念过去网页设计多样化的时代，如Geocities和Freewebs，并批评现代网站趋于结构化和雷同，缺乏个性。
• [smjburton] 赞同旧 web 的实验精神，认为那时的网页设计更加混乱但有趣，而现代网页设计则过于公式化，失去了探索的乐趣。
• [nonethewiser] 认为网站从2023年版到当前版本变得更丑陋，并表示这种变化影响了他对网站内容的看法。
• [guywithahat] 对网站改版感到遗憾，希望能看到原来的CSS和非JS版本的网站。
• [AndrewStephens] 强调个人网站应是个人的表达，不应迎合他人。他认为网络世界需要更多的非 conformity。
• [kapitanjakc] 计划手工打造个人网站，使用基本的HTML/CSS/JS和可能的自托管服务，目前还在学习一些技术细节。
• [severusdd] 认为每个手工打造的网站都有其独特的怪异之处，相比千篇一律的现代模板，更喜欢这种独特的风格。
• [jasir] 认为当前的网站设计虽然主观上有些难以阅读，但整体有趣且具有探索性，适合作为个人项目。
• [jbd0] 认为网站被"接受cookies"弹窗遮挡，影响了美观和用户体验。
• [Arisaka1] 回忆过去不因外界评判或就业压力而建网站的时光，认为这种内在的实验精神有助于提升技能和品味。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：手工打造的网站是否丑陋且难以管理。部分人认为手工打造的网站可以很美观且具有个性，而另一些人则认为这些网站可能会变得难以管理且功能不全。
• 关于现代网页设计的批评：许多人怀念过去多样化和个性化的网页设计，批评现代网页设计趋于雷同和公式化。

data.title: Show HN: I made a Zero-config tool to visualize your code
data.author: lezhu
data.article_summary: "Visualize Data Structures & Algorithms in Real Time" 介绍了一款互动工具，帮助学生、教育者和开发者更直观地理解和学习数据结构与算法。该工具允许用户实时可视化代码执行过程，从而加深对复杂概念的掌握。通过可视化演示，用户可以更快速地学习，并更聪明地编写代码，提高编程效率和准确性。这款工具特别适合用于教学和自学，能有效增强学习体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某工具的反馈和功能建议

不同观点：
• [jolmg] 指出滚动时的动画与滚轮步进不匹配，每步填充1.2个孔，导致动画在演示过程中出现暂停。他在Chromium和Firefox上都测试过，鼠标事件是正常的，单步事件对应单一事件。

• [schaefer] 对工具表示赞赏，并询问是否可以在本地运行，比如通过Docker。他还表示愿意捐款支持开发者。

• [federiconafria] 认为工具很适合学习，但建议改进显示返回值，并可视化函数是否尚未返回。他还提到变量和其值的垂直排列有些不习惯。

• [cadamsdotcom] 认为工具很酷，并建议集成LSP（语言服务器协议）以增强对多种语言的兼容性，认为这样可以更好地可视化整个代码库。

• [vishkk] 认为工具简洁，并提到类似的Python Tutor工具，提供了一个参考链接。

• [emushack] 对排序算法示例表示赞赏，认为这是学习数据结构和算法的绝佳工具。

• [chrsw] 提到在Firefox中切换到C/C++语言时，示例代码没有自动更新为C/C++示例。

• [mushufasa] 认为工具对发现性能瓶颈有帮助，但难以整合进其现有的大型代码库，询问其他静态分析工具的推荐。

• [on_the_train] 表示网站为空，箭头按钮无功能。

• [dugmartin] 离题地提到首次注意到网站页脚的ICP许可证链接，并分享了相关维基百科链接。

• [webprofusion] 建议将网站置于Cloudflare后，以获得地理分布的缓存，认为当前网站速度很慢，像是在个人服务器上运行。

补充讨论：
• 功能改进建议集中在返回值显示、语言兼容性和性能分析工具的整合。
• 技术问题包括滚轮步进不匹配和代码示例自动更新失败。
• 部分用户对工具的实用性和学习价值表示赞赏，也有用户遇到网站加载和功能性问题。

data.author: chrisjj
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Easylang（或Tiki）编程语言的评价和其相关特性的讨论

不同观点：
• [abjr] 认为Easylang可能只是Tiki的重新命名，并提到该语言的作者每年都用它来完成Advent of Code（AoC）活动。这表明Easylang在实际编程挑战中具有实用性。
• [7thaccount] 表达了对简化命令驱动语言的需求，特别是与PowerShell的性能和功能比较，强调了对简化GUI操作的需求。
• [layer8] 将Easylang与Comal 80（一种介于Basic和Pascal之间的语言）进行比较，提到其具有老式REPL和类似Logo的图形功能，暗示这是一种复古但有趣的语言。
• [chrisbrandow] 非常赞赏Easylang，认为它比Scratch更有用，特别是其简单的画布和文本/控制台输出功能，适合编程教育。
• [mdaniel] 关注Easylang的许可证问题，指出GPLv3和"All rights reserved"之间的潜在冲突，并对语言尚未自托管表示遗憾。
• [xunil2ycom] 简单地将Easylang比作Logo语言，暗示其创新性不足。
• [bn-l] 质疑Easylang的目标受众，特别是对于儿童而言，认为它并不适合。

补充讨论：
• 许可证问题：[mdaniel] 提到了Easylang在GitHub上的许可证信息及其潜在的法律问题，这是技术社区中经常引起讨论的话题。
• 语言的创新性和适用性：评论中多次将Easylang与其他语言（如Logo、Comal 80、PowerShell）进行比较，讨论了其创新性和适用范围。
• 目标受众的争议：[bn-l] 对Easylang是否适合儿童使用提出了质疑，与其他评论中对其教育价值的肯定形成对比。

争议焦点：
• Easylang是否真正具有创新性及其目标受众的明确性。
• 许可证的合法性问题及其对项目发展的潜在影响。

data.title: Google is using AI to censor independent websites like mine
data.author: rapnie
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google的算法调整及其影响，包括对小网站的流量影响、对开放网络的潜在控制、以及是否应打破像Alphabet这样的大科技公司以促进竞争。

不同观点：
• **对文章语言和夸大描述的批评**：[gorjusborg] 认为文章中关于“审查”和“影子禁令”的描述是夸大和煽动性的。他指出Google只是调整算法，而不应视为 censorship 或 banning。文章的夸张语气降低了其可信度。
  
• **Google的权力与责任**：[blinding-streak] 认为文章虽然提出了一些合理的观点，但充满了一种“ entitled ”（应得权利）的态度。Google为网站带来了大量流量，网站应该自己建立与用户的联系，而不是依赖Google。

• **大科技公司的垄断问题**：[basilgohar] 认为像Alphabet这样的公司拥有过多权力，应该被拆分以促进竞争和用户选择，否则将导致垄断性单一文化，强化现有权力结构。

• **Google对开放网络的控制**：[fidotron] 认为Google正通过AI逐渐控制和取代开放网络，形成一个封闭的生态系统，使开发者不得不遵循Google的规则以获取商业利益。

• **有机流量的权利问题**：[thedevilslawyer] 认为文章错误地将有机流量视为一种固有权利。随着AI提供更好的个性化建议，传统搜索流量可能进一步减少。

• **创新与竞争的必要性**：[redwood] 认为Google的行动是应对竞争压力的必然结果，但担心这会带来群体思维，抑制新想法和创新。

• **信息卡特尔的风险**：[sebstefan] 质疑Google仅从少数几个控制和选择的来源获取信息，可能导致提供更差的结果，并要求提供证据。

• **开放源搜索的设想**：[seaourfreed] 提出了一种开放源搜索引擎的详细构想，通过分散的节点和区块链技术来减少偏见和控制，恢复搜索公平性。

• **政治价值观的影响**：[logicchains] 认为Google的算法调整是政治性行为，旨在压制不符合硅谷叙事的小网站，并优先考虑与自身政治价值观相同的大型网站。

• **适应变化的必要性**：[moresea] 强调必须适应变化，创新或死亡，过去的红利时期已经结束。

• **回归基础**：[Aldipower] 对Google的调整持积极态度，认为这将促使人们通过直接输入URL访问网站，直接营销和口碑传播将再次重要。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于Google是否通过算法调整形成信息垄断，压制小网站和不同政治观点，以及是否应通过拆分大科技公司来促进竞争。
- 一些评论探讨了开放源搜索引擎的可行性及其潜在优势。
- 对文章语气和夸大描述的批评与对Google权力的担忧形成对比，显示出对大科技公司影响的复杂看法。

data.article_summary:
这篇文章探讨了抽象代数中关于域和整环的一些已知结果。文章首先定义了整环，指出它是一个无零因子的交换环，并给出了几个例子，如整数环 $\mathbb{Z}$ 和素数模整数环 $\mathbb{Z}_p$。接着，文章讨论了已知的一些命题，例如在环中任何元素与零的乘积都是零。然后，文章证明了每个域都是整环，因为域中的每个非零元素都有乘法逆元，从而满足无零因子的条件。

文章进一步探讨了有限整环的性质，证明了每个有限整环都是域。这是通过考虑环中的乘法逆元和利用鸽巢原理来实现的。最后，文章总结了所有讨论的结果，重申了域和整环之间的关系，并提出了一个替代证明来加强论述的完整性。

简而言之，文章明确了每个域都是整环，并且每个有限整环必然是域。

From Finite Integral Domains to Finite Fields
By
Susam Pal
on 25 May 2025
In this article, we explore a few well-known results from abstract
algebra pertaining to fields and integral domains.  We ask ourselves
whether every field is an integral domain, and whether every
integral domain is a field.  We begin with the definition of an
integral domain, discuss a few established results, and then proceed
to answer these questions.  Familiarity with algebraic structures
such as rings and fields is assumed.
Contents
Definition of Integral Domain
Examples of Integral Domains
Known Results
On Distinct Identities
Every Field Is an Integral Domain
Infinite Integral Domains
Every Finite Integral Domain Is a Field
Alternate Proof
Conclusion
Definition of Integral Domain
An
integral domain
is a commutative ring, with distinct
additive and multiplicative identities, in which the product of any
two non-zero elements is also non-zero.
Equivalently, an integral domain is a commutative ring, with
distinct additive and multiplicative identities, such that if the
product of two elements is zero, then one of the elements must be
zero.
Using standard notation, we can write that a commutative ring \( R
\) is an integral domain if \( 0 \ne 1 \) and for \( a, b \in R, \)
\[
a \ne 0 \text{ and } b \ne 0 \implies a \cdot b \ne 0
\]
or equivalently,
\[
a \cdot b = 0 \implies a = 0 \text{ or } b = 0.
\]
There are many other alternative ways to define an integral domain
which are all equivalent.  In a ring \( R, \) a
zero
divisor
is a non-zero element \( a \in R \) such that there
exists a non-zero element \( b \in R \) with \( ab = 0.  \)  With
this definition of a zero divisor, we can define an integral domain
to be a unital commutative ring, with \( 0 \ne 1, \) that has no
zero divisors.
Examples of Integral Domains
The ring of integers \( \mathbb{Z} \) is an integral domain since
the product of two non-zero integers is non-zero.  The field of
rational numbers \( \mathbb{Q} \) is also an integral domain.  The
ring of polynomials in the indeterminate \( t \) with coefficients
in an integral domain \( R, \) denoted \( R[t], \) is an integral
domain as well.
The ring of integers modulo 5, denoted \( \mathbb{Z}_5 \) is an
integral domain.  However, the ring of integers modulo 6, denoted \(
\mathbb{Z}_6, \) is not an integral domain since \( 2 \cdot 3 = 0 \)
in \( \mathbb{Z}_6.  \)  In other words, \( \mathbb{Z}_6 \) has zero
divisors, namely \( 2 \) and \( 3, \) so it is not an integral
domain.  In fact, the ring of integers modulo \( n, \) denoted \(
\mathbb{Z}_n \) is an integral domain if and only if \( n \) is
prime.
Known Results
For the sake of brevity, we assume the following known results.
Proposition 1.
Let \( R \) be a ring.  Then, for all \( a \in R, \) we have
\[
a \cdot 0 = 0 \cdot a = 0.
\]
Proposition 2.
Let \( D \) be an integral domain.  Then, for all \( a, b, c \in D \) such
that \( a \ne 0, \) we have
\[
a \cdot b = a \cdot c \implies b = c.
\]
The second result is also known as the
cancellation property of
integral domains
.
On Distinct Identities
We have been mentioning the distinctiveness of the additive and
multiplicative identities as a property of an integral domain.  Some
texts express this more concisely by saying that an integral domain
is a
non-zero
unital commutative ring without zero
divisors, i.e., the zero ring \( \{ 0 \} \) is excluded from the
definition.
This follows directly from
Proposition 1
.  If \( 0 = 1 \in R
, \) then for all \( r \in R, \) we get
\[
r = r \cdot 1 = r \cdot 0 = 0
\]
which means that every element of \( R \) is zero, i.e., \( R = \{ 0
\}.  \)  To summarise
\[ 0 = 1 \in R \implies R = \{ 0 \} \]
or equivalently, for a ring \( R \) with unity,
\[
R \ne \{ 0 \} \implies 0 \ne 1.
\]
Further, if \( 0 \) and \( 1 \) are two distinct elements of \( R
, \) then \( R \) has at least two elements, so for a ring \( R \)
with unity,
\[
0 \ne 1 \implies R \ne \{ 0 \}
\]
Therefore, a ring with unity has distinct additive and
multiplicative identities if and only if it is a non-zero ring.  This
is why an integral domain can also be defined as a non-zero unital
commutative ring without zero divisors.
Every Field Is an Integral Domain
We now show that every field is indeed an integral domain.  Let \( F
\) be a field, and let \( a, b \in F \) such that \( ab = 0.  \)
There are two cases to consider: \( a = 0 \) and \( a \ne 0.  \)  If
\( a = 0, \) then indeed \( ab = 0 \)
by
Proposition 1
.
Now suppose \( a \ne 0.  \)  Then by the properties of fields, there exists a
multiplicative inverse \( a^{-1} \in F \) such that \( a \cdot
a^{-1} = 1.  \)  Then using the properties of fields, we get
\[
b = b \cdot 1 = b \cdot (a \cdot a^{-1}) = (a \cdot b) \cdot
a^{-1} = 0 \cdot a^{-1} = 0.
\]
The last equality follows from
Proposition 1
.  We have shown
that if \( ab = 0, \) then either \( a = 0 \) or \( b = 0.  \)
Therefore, if both \( a \ne 0 \) and \( b \ne 0, \) then it must be
that \( ab \ne 0.  \)  Th

data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 科学家在寻找假想的太阳系第九行星过程中，意外发现了一颗新的矮行星候选者，名为2017 OF201。这颗矮行星直径约700公里，位于海王星外的柯伊伯带，其轨道极其 elongated，远日点可达海王星距离的1,600倍，甚至可能曾接近其他恒星。其发现者认为，这颗矮行星的存在挑战了第九行星理论，因为它的轨道并不符合之前假设的行星集群轨道模式。尽管尚未找到第九行星存在的证据，但随着Vera Rubin天文台即将投入使用，这一谜团或将很快揭晓。

Does our solar system have a mysterious ninth planet? The discovery of a new dwarf world suggests not.
It's an evocative idea that has long bedeviled scientists: a huge and mysterious planet is lurking in the darkness at the edge of our solar system, evading all our efforts to spot it.
Some astronomers say the strange, clustered orbits of icy rocks beyond Neptune indicate that something big is out there, which they have dubbed Planet Nine.
Now, a US-based trio hunting this elusive world has instead stumbled on what appears to be a new dwarf planet in the solar system's outer reaches.
And the existence of this new kid on the block could challenge the Planet Nine theory, the researchers have calculated.
Named 2017 OF201, the new object is roughly 700 kilometers (430 miles) across, according to a
preprint study
, which has not been peer-reviewed, published online last week.
That makes it three times smaller than Pluto.
But it is still big enough to be considered a dwarf planet, lead study author Sihao Cheng of New Jersey's Institute for Advanced Study told AFP.
Distant traveler
The object is currently three times farther away from Earth than Neptune.
And its extremely elongated orbit swings out more than 1,600 times the distance between Earth and the sun, taking it into the ring of icy rocks around the solar system called the Oort cloud.
"It goes so far out, it could have passed by stars other than our sun in the past," Cheng said.
During its 25,000-year orbit, the object is only close enough to Earth to be observed around 0.5% of the time, which is roughly a century.
"It's already getting fainter and fainter," Cheng said.
The discovery suggests "there are many hundreds of similar things on similar orbits" in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune, Cheng said.
After taking a risk spending more than half a year sorting through a difficult dataset in search of Planet Nine, Cheng said he was "lucky" to have found anything at all.
The researchers are requesting time to point the James Webb, Hubble and ALMA telescopes at their discovery.
But Sam Deen, a 23-year-old amateur astronomer from California, has already been able to track the dwarf planet candidate through old datasets.
"OF201 is, in my opinion, probably one of the most interesting discoveries in the outer solar system in the last decade," Deen told AFP.
What about Planet Nine?
The icy rocks discovered in the Kuiper Belt tend to have a clustered orbit going in a particular direction.
Two decades ago, astronomers proposed this was due to the gravitational pull of a world up to 10 times larger than Earth, naming it Planet Nine and kicking off a debate that has rumbled since.
It is also sometimes called Planet X, a name proposed for a hypothetical world beyond Neptune more than a century ago.
Back in 1930, astronomers were searching for Planet X when they discovered Pluto, which became our solar system's ninth planet.
But Pluto turned out to be too tiny -- it is smaller than the moon -- and was demoted to
dwarf planet
status in 2006.
There are now four other officially recognized dwarf planets, and Cheng believes 2017 OF201 could join their ranks.
When the researchers modeled its
orbit
, they found it did not follow the clustered trend of similar objects.
This could pose a problem for the Planet Nine theory, but Cheng emphasized more data is needed.
Samantha Lawler of Canada's University of Regina told AFP that this "great discovery" and others like it mean that "the original argument for Planet Nine is getting weaker and weaker".
The Vera Rubin Observatory, which is scheduled to go online in Chile this year, is expected to shed light on this mystery, one way or another.
Deen said it was discouraging that no sign of Planet Nine has been found so far, but with Vera Rubin "on the horizon I don't think we'll have to wonder about its existence for much longer".
For Cheng, he still hopes that this huge planet is out there somewhere.
"We're in an era when big telescopes can see almost to the edge of the universe," he said.
But what is in our "backyard" still largely remains unknown, he added.

data.title: The Crafters of "Andor"
data.author: SLHamlet
data.article_summary: 《Andor》被誉为本世纪最出色的《星球大战》作品，甚至可能是史上最佳。该剧由托尼·吉尔罗伊主创，具有深刻的反法西斯主题，精致的制作设计，并关注供应链问题，极具个人特色。它与《星球大战》其他作品截然不同，预算庞大，挑战观众，实属难得。尽管网上分析众多，但许多过于表面，聚焦于粉丝考据，而忽视了其丰富的主题和独立于粉丝服务之外的艺术价值。该剧也带来了丰富的幕后访谈，创作者们深入探讨了他们的艺术选择和未被采纳的方向，提供了难得的创作洞见，令人想起DVD时代的幕后花絮。这些访谈展示了顶尖创作者如何重塑这个已有近半个世纪历史的宇宙，值得一看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：流媒体时代的内容丰富度与视觉体验的缺失，以及对特定影视作品的评价和比较。

不同观点：
• [gdubs] 认为流媒体服务（包括音乐和视频）相比DVD时代，丧失了许多额外的内容，如花絮、幕后纪录片、专辑艺术等。他特别指出，过去专辑的封面艺术和内页注释具有很高的艺术价值，而如今尽管有如Apple Music的动画和视觉效果，但整体视觉体验大不如前。他还提到Flash的消亡可能导致了这种互动内容和视觉艺术的缺失。

• [duxup] 专注于对《Andor》这一电视剧的评价，认为该剧即便脱离《星球大战》的背景也能独立成佳作。他强调了该剧在视觉细节和道具使用上的精心制作，显示出对剧集质量的赞赏。

• [InTheArena] 将《Andor》与《星战前传》、《The Expanse》、《Battlestar Galactica》以及《Babylon 5》等作品进行对比，认为《Andor》达到了他心目中《星球大战》系列应有的水准。他批评了《星战前传》的商业化倾向，并赞扬《Andor》在情节发展和历史隐喻上的深度和严谨，认为其为后续作品奠定了更好的基础。

补充讨论：
• 《Andor》作为一部科幻剧集，获得了观众的高度评价，尤其在与《星球大战》其他系列作品的对比中，被认为在剧情和制作质量上更为出色。
• 流媒体时代的内容创作中，互动性和视觉艺术的缺失成为一个讨论焦点，尤其在与过去的DVD内容和Flash互动内容对比时，这一点更为明显。
• 对《Andor》的讨论中，观众对其情节和细节处理的赞赏反映出对高质量剧集的需求和期待。

44111248.article_content:
It's hard for me to articulate just how much I love "Andor", the best Star Wars entertainment of at least this century, and maybe ever. Tony Gilroy's long been a favorite of mine (friends will know that I need
very
little prompting to wax rhapsodic about
Michael Clayton
, his greatest film) so it was no surprise that I would be inclined to like the show. But when it turned out to be a deeply ruminative, unabashedly anti-fascist show with lavish production design and a recurring fixation on supply chains, it's like it was crafted specifically to appeal to me personally.
There are lots of analyses of the show online, some fairly sophisticated, but too many suffer from being fairly facile as online fandoms have been trained to pursue "find the reference to the wiki lore!" rituals, and so they struggle to deal with a thematically rich work that is plainly indifferent to fan service. It also emphasizes just how
unlikely
it is that this series exists at all, striking such a different tone from anything else in the franchise, being given such an extravagant budget, and being allowed to challenge its audience in a way that no major studio has ever allowed a top-tier blockbuster cinematic universe to do.
If there's one thing Star Wars fans love, it's hating Star Wars, and so the only way we can ever truly praise a Star Wars work is by implicitly insulting all of them, usually in one of these two ways: This is Star Wars for adults! This is Star Wars for people who don't like Star Wars! Sure, it's those things, and it's genuinely good prestige TV (I say that as someone who generally despises prestige TV), but it's also
good
Star Wars) and I am not a person prone to "guilty pleasures"; I find no shame in enjoying a franchise that is enormously popular and that's been a fun form of entertainment in movies and shows and video games and toys since I was a kid.
Wither DVD Extras
But what has been a wonderful surprise is discovering that so many of the brilliantly talented artists behind "Andor" have participated in deep, thoughtful conversations about their work on the show. They've gone into deep detail about their artistic choices, and even discussed the directions that they
weren't
able to explore. On these kinds of streaming shows, there are always plenty of interviews with the cast that take the form of a typical press junket, and "Andor" has those, but they take the typical conventional form, and are not particularly interesting even though the actors are brilliant.
Fortunately, though, there are also a rich set of interviews with the creators responsible for aspects of production like the sound design, stunt choreography, set decoration, and writing — even Tony Gilroy himself talking about the combinations of writing and showrunning of the series. It is just an extraordinary glimpse at what it took to make the work. I grew up watching the "behind the scenes" documentaries that a generation of us pored over in the 80s and 90s as Star Wars fans before the DVD era. We felt like we'd won the lottery when DVDs arrived and suddenly studios felt like they had to expand their releases with an accompaniment of bonus material to entice fans to buy a copy of their favorite films. In the era before fan wikis and online fan culture in general, this was the only peek at how people made the creative work we were inspired by, in the same way that we would obsess over the liner notes on a favorite album.
Now it's as easy as a few clicks, and it is no surprise that the people who made "Andor" are also wonderfully articulate about how and why they made their choices while creating the series. If you enjoyed the show as much as I did, set aside some time and listen to how people who are operating at the very top of their game can make something amazing that reinvents a familiar universe after almost half a century.
(Spoilers) Creator Interview Videos
Tony Gilroy recaps the writing and structure of season two (and the overall story) of Andor.
The stunt coordinator and stunt doubles of Andor walk through the brutal climactic fistfight from the end of season two.
The cinematographer, production designer, and costume designer of Andor discuss season one of the show. (It's a long interview, here's a
brief excerpt about the minimalist design
in the show.) This is another good
audio-only interview
with Luke Hull and Michael Wilkinson, the production designer and costume designer.
The sound designer/sound editor and dialogue/ADR supervisor of Andor explain the sound design of season two.
The set decorator of Andor discusses the set decor of season one.

主要讨论点：人们对现实的认知与世界观的冲突，特别是关于mRNA疫苗的意识形态反感

不同观点：
• jleyank认为，大多数人很难让现实符合他们的世界观，但人们仍然会尝试去改变现实。他希望通过这些努力受到影响的人数能够最小化。
• matthewdgreen简洁地表达了对这种情况的负面评价，暗示这种情况可能带来不良后果。
• bediger4000详细分析了mRNA疫苗在意识形态上的反感现象。他指出，尽管mRNA疫苗是在特朗普政府期间开发的，而且特朗普本人曾为疫苗邀功，但在他的支持者中却引起了负面的反应。这种反感源于对疫苗的荒诞预测，比如接种疫苗的人会流血身亡，而这些预测都没有实现。

补充讨论：
• bediger4000进一步指出，尽管特朗普曾为疫苗开发邀功，但在疫苗问题上，他的支持者们实际上主导了立场，特朗普在这个问题上更像是在追随其支持者的意见。
• 争议的焦点在于mRNA疫苗的意识形态反感，以及这种反感情绪如何在特定政治群体中形成和传播。

data.title: A Song of “Full Self-Driving”
data.author: latexr
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论特斯拉和埃隆·马斯克在“完全自动驾驶”（FSD）技术上的承诺与现实差距。多年来，马斯克多次宣称特斯拉即将实现完全自动驾驶，但这些承诺一再落空，成为笑柄。尽管马斯克声称FSD即将推出，但具体细节模糊，且相关政府部门和公众并未得到充分沟通。相比之下，谷歌旗下的Waymo已经实现了真正的无人驾驶技术，特斯拉则明显落后。文章批评了将重大科技决策交给毫无头绪的巨富人士掌控的现象，并质疑特斯拉即将推出的“Robotaxi”是否只是噱头而非实际突破。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉的全自动驾驶（FSD）技术及其可行性、技术路线、以及与竞争对手（如Waymo）的比较。

不同观点：
• **ddalex**：认为FSD要么是一个需要先进传感器和算法的高难度问题，要么是一个通过摄像头和神经网络可以轻松解决的简单问题。如果属于前者，Waymo有不可逾越的优势；如果是后者，任何公司都可以轻松复制特斯拉的技术。同时质疑特斯拉是否具有战略护城河。

• **x187463**：虽然认为FSD在大多数情况下表现不错，但指出其存在许多问题，如无法正确处理交通信号和限速等，且仅依靠摄像头无法实现完全无监督的FSD。分享了自己使用FSD时遇到的多个实际问题，认为特斯拉需要引入LIDAR等更多传感器。同时，也承认FSD在某些复杂驾驶场景中表现良好。

• **Coeur**：纠正关于LIDAR在自动驾驶技术中应用的错误信息，指出许多现有功能（如车道偏离检测和自适应巡航控制）并不依赖LIDAR，而是使用雷达和摄像头。同时，认为LIDAR可能在未来全自动驾驶中发挥重要作用，但目前尚未广泛应用。

• **bhouston**：对Elon Musk的个人行为和宣传方式提出批评，认为他虽然有远见和执行力，但也有过度承诺和偏见的问题，且在个人生活方面存在争议。

• **walthamstow**：指出谷歌街景车频繁采集数据，质疑其是否仅采集图像，还是同时采集其他数据，认为这可能对自动驾驶技术的发展有帮助。

• **jp57**：质疑Waymo的FSD技术是否真正实现了完全自动驾驶，指出其可能依赖远程人工干预，但未公开具体细节。

• **amarcheschi**：提到一首关于Musk和特斯拉的歌曲，未深入讨论技术问题。

• **kklisura**：引用法律诉讼案例，指出Musk在FSD技术上的承诺被指夸大甚至误导，且法律团队成功辩护称这些承诺属于“企业乐观的模糊陈述”和“ mere puffing”。

• **cbeach**：认为许多文章对Musk和FSD的批评是基于个人和政治偏见，而非实质性技术评价，并指出FSD在现实世界中的进展显著，优于依赖地理围栏和安全驾驶员的Waymo。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于FSD技术是否能够仅依靠摄像头实现完全自动驾驶，以及特斯拉与Waymo等竞争对手的技术优劣对比。
• 部分评论者对Musk的个人行为和宣传方式提出批评，认为其承诺不可全信。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于LIDAR等传感器的必要性，一些评论者认为特斯拉需要引入更多传感器以提高FSD的安全性和可靠性。

Hey fam:
Supersized newsletter today. This Triad goes to
four
.
It’s about Tesla and Elon Musk and autonomous vehicles. It gets fairly technical at times. But it’s really about how we’ve turned over large portions of America to insanely rich people who have no idea what they’re doing.
It’s about oligarchy and technology. I hope you’ll take the ride with me—and share it if you are so inclined.
Join
P.S.: If this edition ends abruptly in your inbox, click the title to get to the full version on the site. Like I said—it’s a long one.
Cybercab! (Composite / GettyImages / Shutterstock)
1. “Full Self Driving”
For years, Elon Musk has been promising that Teslas will operate completely autonomously in “Full Self Driving” (FSD) mode. And when I say years, I mean
years
:
December 2015
: “We’re going to end up with complete autonomy, and I think we will have complete autonomy in approximately two years.”
January 2016
: “In ~2 years, summon should work anywhere connected by land & not blocked by borders, eg you’re in LA and the car is in NY.”
June 2016
: “I really would consider autonomous driving to be basically a solved problem. . . . I think we’re basically less than two years away from complete autonomy, complete—safer than a human. However regulators will take at least another year.”
October 2016
: By the end of 2017 Tesla will demonstrate a fully autonomous drive from “a home in L.A., to Times Square . . . without the need for a single touch, including the charging.”
March 2018
: “I think probably by end of next year [end of 2019] self-driving will encompass essentially all modes of driving”
February 2019
: “I think we will be feature complete—full self-driving—this year. Meaning the car will be able to find you in a parking lot, pick you up, take you all the way to your destination without an intervention, this year."
I’m going to stop the litany here, but it continued. For a decade Tesla’s “Full Self Driving” has been
a running joke

data.title: Derek Muller Confronts PFAS "Forever Chemicals"–In His Own Blood
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: YouTube科普明星德里克·穆勒（Derek Muller）以其频道Veritasium吸引了1800万订阅者，他通过挑战科学误解而广受欢迎。最近，他的一项血液检测发现体内存在被称为“永久化学品”的PFAS（全氟和多氟烷基物质）。这一发现正值美国环保署（EPA）突然撤销PFAS防护措施，使穆勒的工作显得尤为紧迫。在他的最新视频《一家公司如何秘密毒害地球》中，穆勒深入探讨了PFAS的危害，该视频时长近一小时，发布一天内就获得近300万观看。视频不仅揭露了企业不当行为，还详细解释了这些“永久化学品”对人类的危害。穆勒在科学教育和影视制作之间曾面临职业选择，最终通过Veritasium实现了将两者结合的独特价值。他的视频强调了困惑和挑战在学习中的重要性，并通过自己的例子警示公众关注PFAS污染这一紧迫健康问题。

不同观点：

• chiph的观点：
   - 支持避免食用微波炉爆米花，因为包装袋内的涂层会释放PFAS化学物质，这些化学物质会渗入爆米花的油中，最终被人体摄入。
   - 引用了视频中的数据，表明微波炉爆米花袋中的PFAS含量远高于其他涂层纸，如快餐汉堡包装纸。

• chiph的疑问引出了一个值得进一步探讨的问题：PFAS化学物质释放的具体条件（例如温度）是否会影响其健康风险。这表明尽管chiph已经决定避免食用微波炉爆米花，但仍对科学细节感兴趣，以更好地理解风险的来源和程度。

YouTube Science Star Derek Muller Confronts PFAS “Forever Chemicals”—In His Own Blood
YouTube star Derek Muller built an 18-million-subscriber YouTube empire by challenging misconceptions about science. Now his own blood test and a sudden EPA reversal give his work urgent relevance.
By
Deni Ellis Béchard
edited by
Dean Visser
Veritasium YouTube star Derek Muller discovered PFAS forever chemicals in his blood.
Simon Dawson/Bloomberg/Getty Images
As the creator of Veritasium, a science education YouTube channel with 18 million subscribers, Derek Muller has spent the past 15 years exploring a counterintuitive vision for learning: Clarity numbs the mind, but confusion can crack it open. His audience has grown because of how he challenges common misconceptions about the laws of nature, and his rise has paralleled YouTube’s, whose creator-focused approach has made it the world’s largest streaming service by almost every measure—from content library to audience size—recently surpassing Netflix in revenue. Amid this symbiosis, Veritasium evolved—from unpolished five-minute clips of Muller quizzing people on the street to technically sophisticated science explorations with the satisfying depth of feature films. Muller himself has appeared in many roles: trickster science teacher, experimenter with a mad-scientist flair, fearless investigator in the mold of Indiana Jones. And in Veritasium’s most recent video, one of the channel’s longest yet, he steps forward as an advocate for one of today’s most pressing health issues:
the toxic “forever chemicals”
that are now being found to contaminate almost every human being, animal and ecosystem on Earth. Entitled
How One Company Secretly Poisoned the Planet
, the video clocks in at nearly an hour and garnered almost three million views within a day. It is not only an exposé of corporate malfeasance but also a
scientific explainer of these forever chemicals (known as perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, or PFAS) and their harm to humans
. It debuted on the same day that the Environmental Protection Agency announced sweeping rollbacks of PFAS safeguards, supercharging the video’s impact. Leveraging his audience, resources and cinematic craft, Muller has now focused Veritasium on a crisis whose invisible poisons, as the film’s finale reveals, are already circulating in his own blood.
Learning from Wrong Answers
Teaching began early for Muller. Born in Traralgon, Australia, in 1982, he relocated to Vancouver as a toddler and so excelled in school that his teachers sometimes invited him to tutor the class. “There was a certain way in which science appeared like magic,” he recalls—invoking science-fiction giant Arthur C. Clarke’s adage that any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from sorcery. He remembers ordinary school experiments—the upside-down glass that keeps a tissue dry underwater and the soda-and-Mentos fountain. But what stuck was the sense that the universe kept secrets only curiosity could unlock. “Isn’t it everything?” he says when asked why science matters. “Isn’t it obvious that it’s the most important thing?”
On supporting science journalism

. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
When Muller graduated, he was torn between pursuing filmmaking and science. He wanted to be “uniquely useful,” he says. “I felt like if I went into science, maybe I would be a swappable cog in some sort of machine.” But he also feared that pursuing film might have him running coffees in Los Angeles in hopes of making the right connection and getting a break. He took a full scholarship in engineering physics at Queen’s University in Ontario and then decamped to Sydney, Australia, to pursue film—only to learn that the Australian Film, Television and Radio School admits just a handful of students per program each year. Lacking a portfolio, he wandered into the University of Sydney’s physics department in hopes of a tutoring gig and stayed to do a doctorate on how people learn—or fail to. In classes, he noticed that students often nodded appreciatively but retained almost nothing. “If you perform a demonstration and don’t force the class to make a prediction,” he says, “they’ll learn about as much as if they never saw the demonstration at all.”
Muller’s doctoral thesis compared two instructional video styles, which were viewed by undergraduates at the University of Sydney. The first featured an actor delivering a polished, textbook explanation of Newton’s laws. Participants described this version as easy to follow. The second portrayed a student repeatedly stumbling over the laws while a tutor tried to set him straight. Most viewers found this depiction confusing. data.title: Cory Doctorow on how we lost the internet
data.author: udev4096
data.article_summary: Cory Doctorow在PyCon US 2025上发表主题演讲，讨论当今互联网的衰退，即"enshittification"（腐化）过程。他将其分为三个阶段：首先，平台通过提升用户体验来吸引用户，同时设法锁定用户；接着，在用户难以离开时，平台开始牺牲用户体验以取悦商业客户，如增加广告；最后，平台价值被榨取到仅剩最低限度以维持用户和商业客户的依赖。他以Google为例，说明其通过锁定用户和操控广告市场来实现增长，甚至通过非法合作（如"Jedi Blue"项目）操控广告市场，最终导致搜索质量下降，用户和商业客户都受到负面影响。Doctorow强调，这种腐化也体现在其他行业，如护理工作通过类似"Uber for nursing"的应用程序剥削护士。他呼吁关注这种系统性问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Doctorow的演讲和其对互联网问题的分析的评价，以及进一步资源推荐。

不同观点：
• [freedomben] 认为Doctorow对问题的分析非常具有说服力，无论是否同意他提出的解决方案。该评论者赞赏演讲和相关文章，并提供了进一步观看演讲的链接。同时，他还推荐了Doctorow的书《The Internet Con: How to Seize the Means of Computation》作为深入理解的资源。

• [ChrisArchitect] 则指出该话题在之前已被讨论过，并提供了一个先前讨论的链接。这个评论似乎暗示可能没有必要再次讨论同一话题，或建议读者参考先前的讨论以获取更多信息。

补充讨论：
• 评论之间存在一定的讨论关系，[ChrisArchitect]通过提供先前讨论的链接，引导读者查看其他地方的相似话题，从而可能减少重复讨论。
• [freedomben]的评论更侧重于对Doctorow分析的个人评价和推荐，而[ChrisArchitect]则关注于避免话题的重复讨论。
• 争议的焦点可能在于是否有必要重复讨论相同的话题，还是应引导读者查阅之前的讨论以获取更多背景信息。

Cory Doctorow on how we lost the internet
[LWN subscriber-only content]
Welcome to LWN.net
The following subscription-only content has been made available to you
by an LWN subscriber.  Thousands of subscribers depend on LWN for the
best news from the Linux and free software communities.  If you enjoy this
article, please consider
subscribing to LWN
.  Thank you
for visiting LWN.net!
By
Jake Edge
May 27, 2025
PyCon US
Cory Doctorow
wears many hats
:
digital activist, science-fiction author, journalist, and more.  He has
also written many books, both fiction and non-fiction, runs the
Pluralistic blog
, is a visiting
professor, and is an advisor to the
Electronic
Frontier Foundation
(EFF); his
Chokepoint Capitalism
co-author, Rebecca Giblin, gave a
2023 keynote
in Australia
that we covered.  Doctorow gave a rousing keynote on
the state of the "enshitternet"—today's internet—to kick
off the recently held
PyCon US
2025
in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
He began by noting that he is known for coining the term
"
enshittification
" about the decay of tech platforms, so attendees were
probably expecting to hear about that; instead, he wanted to start by
talking about nursing.  A
recent
study
described how nurses are increasingly getting work through one of
three main apps that "
bill themselves out as 'Uber for nursing'
".
The nurses never know what they will be paid per hour prior to accepting a
shift and the three companies act as a cartel in order to "
play all
kinds of games with the way that labor is priced
".
In particular, the
companies purchase financial information from a data broker before offering
a nurse a shift; if the nurse is carrying a lot of credit-card debt,
especially if some of that is delinquent, the amount offered is
reduced. "
Because, the more desperate you are, the less you'll accept to
come into work and do that grunt work of caring for the sick, the elderly,
and the dying.
"  That is horrific on many levels, he said, but "
it
is emblematic of 'enshittification'
", which is one of the reasons he
highlighted it.
Platform decay
Enshittification is a three-stage process; he used Google to
illustrate the idea.  At first, Google minimized ads and maximized spending
on engineering to produce a great search engine; while it was doing that,
however, it was buying its way to dominance. "
They bribed every service,
every product
that had a search box to make sure that that was a Google search box.
"
No matter which browser, phone carrier, or operating system you were using,
Google ensured that you were using its search by default; by the early
2020s, it was spending the equivalent of buying a Twitter every 18 months
to do so, he said.  That is the first stage of the process: when the
provider is being good to its users, but is finding ways to lock them in.
The second phase occurs once the company recognizes that it has users
locked in, so it will be difficult for them to switch away, and it shifts
to making things worse for its users in order to enrich its business
customers.  For Google, those are the publishers and advertisers.  A
growing portion of the search results page is shifted over to ads
"
marked off with ever-subtler, ever-smaller, ever-grayer labels
distinguishing them from the organic search results
".  While the
platform is getting better for business customers—at the expense of the
users—those customers are also getting locked in.
Phase three of enshittification is when the value of the platform is
clawed back until all that is left is kind of a "
homeopathic residue—the
least value needed to keep both business customers and end users locked to
the platform
".  We have gained a view into this process from the three
monopoly cases that Google has lost over the last 18 months. In 2019, the
company had 90% of the world's search traffic and its users were loyal;
"
everyone who searched on Google, searched everything on Google
".
But that meant that Google's search growth had plateaued, so how was the
company going to be able to grow?  It could "
raise a billion humans to
adulthood and make them Google customers, which is
Google Classroom
, but that's a
slow process
".  From the internal memos that came to light from the
court cases, we can see what the company chose to do, he said: "
they
made search worse
".
The accuracy of the search results was reduced, which meant that users
needed to do two or three queries to the get the results they would have
seen on the first page.  That increased the number of ads that could be

44124360.article_summary: Cory Doctorow在PyCon US 2025上发表主题演讲，讨论当今互联网的衰退，即"enshittification"（腐化）过程。他将其分为三个阶段：首先，平台通过提升用户体验来吸引用户，同时设法锁定用户；接着，在用户难以离开时，平台开始牺牲用户体验以取悦商业客户，如增加广告；最后，平台价值被榨取到仅剩最低限度以维持用户和商业客户的依赖。他以Google为例，说明其通过锁定用户和操控广告市场来实现增长，甚至通过非法合作（如"Jedi Blue"项目）操控广告市场，最终导致搜索质量下降，用户和商业客户都受到负面影响。Doctorow强调，这种腐化也体现在其他行业，如护理工作通过类似"Uber for nursing"的应用程序剥削护士。他呼吁关注这种系统性问题。

data.title: Randomness Requirements for Security
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary:
RFC 4086 强调了安全系统中生成随机数的重要性，这些随机数用于密码、加密密钥等。尽管强加密算法能抵御模式分析，但如果使用伪随机过程生成秘密数值，可能导致伪安全。攻击者可能重现生成环境并搜索有限的可能性集合。

文档指出选择真正随机数生成方法的困难，建议使用硬件随机数生成器，并提供了在没有硬件解决方案时的替代方法。它还讨论了熵源、去偏技术、混合函数以及伪随机数生成器的优缺点，并提供了具体应用中随机数生成的示例和标准。最终，强调了在安全系统中生成高质量随机数的关键性。

June 2005
Randomness Requirements for Security
Status of This Memo
This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the
Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for
improvements.  Distribution of this memo is unlimited.
Copyright Notice
Copyright (C) The Internet Society (2005).
Abstract
Security systems are built on strong cryptographic algorithms that
foil pattern analysis attempts.  However, the security of these
systems is dependent on generating secret quantities for passwords,
cryptographic keys, and similar quantities.  The use of pseudo-random
processes to generate secret quantities can result in pseudo-
security.  A sophisticated attacker may find it easier to reproduce
the environment that produced the secret quantities and to search the
resulting small set of possibilities than to locate the quantities in
the whole of the potential number space.
Choosing random quantities to foil a resourceful and motivated
adversary is surprisingly difficult.  This document points out many
pitfalls in using poor entropy sources or traditional pseudo-random
number generation techniques for generating such quantities.  It
recommends the use of truly random hardware techniques and shows that
the existing hardware on many systems can be used for this purpose.
It provides suggestions to ameliorate the problem when a hardware
solution is not available, and it gives examples of how large such
quantities need to be for some applications.

data.title: Windows 11 Start Menu Revealed as Resource-Heavy React Native App
data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Windows 11开始菜单的性能问题。用户发现该菜单使用React Native构建，导致在点击开始按钮时，某些硬件配置下的CPU使用率会飙升30%到70%。虽然并非所有系统都受影响，但这一问题引发了对现代操作系统中软件优化和资源管理的关注。游戏开发传奇人物John Carmack也参与讨论，指出软件低效而非硬件限制是当前计算瓶颈，并建议若处理器发展停滞，市场将推动更优化的软件开发。这突显了对Windows核心组件开发框架选择的质疑以及对性能优化的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软Windows系统的技术实现及其变化引发的讨论

不同观点：
• [smileybarry] 认为有关Windows开始菜单使用React Native开发的说法并不准确。他指出，只有“推荐”部分使用了React Native，并且是微软为Windows定制的React Native，渲染的是真实的XAML组件，而不是简单的网页或WebView伪装。开始菜单本身仍然是用C++和XAML开发的，并不是完全基于JavaScript或React Native。

• [msgodel] 对Windows每个新版本都出现退步表示不满，认为尽管存在这些问题，Windows依然是一个可用且受欢迎的操作系统。这暗示了对微软在技术决策上的质疑，但同时承认其市场地位。

• [fredoralive] 通过对比1995年的微软（因硬件限制不显示秒数）和2025年的微软（使用React开发开始菜单而不考虑RAM、CPU或常识），讽刺微软在技术选择上的变化，质疑其对性能和资源消耗的考虑。

• [duxup] 开玩笑地问这是否是微软AI计划的一部分，暗示对微软选择新技术栈的困惑或不解。

• [benoau] 认为这可能是开发人员在追求“氛围编码”（vibe-coding），即盲目接受新潮流而不考虑其对系统的影响，暗示对技术决策过程的批评。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于微软在Windows系统中引入新技术的合理性，特别是使用React Native开发开始菜单部分是否合适。部分评论者担心这会影响系统性能和资源消耗。

• 评论中还反映出对微软技术决策过程的质疑，以及对新版本Windows出现退步现象的不满。

• 不同评论者对微软在技术选择上的态度各异，有的试图澄清技术细节，有的则通过讽刺和批评表达不满。

44124688.article_content:
