Recent observations from users on the social platform X have uncovered performance issues tied to the
Windows 11 Start Menu
, revealing that the component is built using
React Native
-  a framework known for its cross-platform flexibility but criticized for inefficiency in system-level applications.
Users
report
that clicking the Start button can spike CPU usage by
30% to 70%
on at least one core, depending on the hardware configuration. The issue doesn't occur consistently across all systems, with some users noting it happens in about
50% of clicks
.
This revelation has reignited discussions around software optimization and resource management in modern operating systems. Notably, legendary game developer
John Carmack
recently weighed in on a related topic during a discussion dubbed the "
CPU Apocalypse
" thought experiment.
Carmack, former CTO of Oculus and co-founder of id Software, argued that
software inefficiencies  -  not hardware limits  -  are the real bottleneck
in computing today. He suggested that if the development of new processors were to stall, market forces would push for significantly more optimized software, enabling older hardware to perform far better than currently expected.
The Start Menu issue highlights growing concerns over how modern UI components are built within Windows, raising questions about Microsoft’s choice of frameworks for core OS elements and whether performance considerations are being prioritized sufficiently.

data.author: admtal

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款名为"LAZY PUBLIC DOMAIN BLOCK GAME"的非传统俄罗斯方块游戏的改进建议、用户体验及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• [开发者admtal的观点] 开发者对玩家提出的建议表示感谢，并计划在周末进行一些更新，例如多袋系统、不自动清除游戏结束状态等。开发者提到自己为了个人喜好设计了这款游戏，但也承认有些功能虽然已经实现，但因为不直观而未被玩家发现。开发者还提到游戏设计中的技术实现和优化过程，特别是使用AI工具辅助开发。

• [玩家hnlmorg的观点] 玩家提到游戏中随机出现方块的问题，建议使用单袋系统来改善游戏体验，以避免某些方块出现过少的情况。

• [玩家lynx97的观点] 该玩家分享了一个为盲文显示器用户开发的俄罗斯方块克隆版，其中方块是水平下落并使用Unicode盲文进行渲染的。这显示了不同用户群体对游戏的需求和创新。

• [玩家freeone3000的观点] 该玩家赞赏游戏通过去除时间压力来探讨时间在游戏中的作用，但也指出过度去除压力会使游戏变得过于简单而失去乐趣。

• [玩家enahs-sf的观点] 该玩家将游戏过程与创业公司的工作相联系，指出即使在无时间压力和有撤销功能的情况下，玩家仍可能做出导致游戏失败的选择，这反映了人类心理学在决策中的作用。

补充讨论：
• [功能请求] 玩家tantalor建议增加一个预览功能，显示方块最终落地的位置（幽灵方块）。玩家heisenbit则希望在拖动方块到最低点时自动下落，而不是手动按下。

• [名称与法律问题] 玩家stevage认为“lazy”这个名称不太合适，建议改为“low stress”。而玩家jsheard和ggoo则警告开发者注意Tetris公司的商标保护，建议更改项目名称以避免法律风险。

• [其他游戏版本] 玩家cshimmin分享了一款低压力、多人玩的桌面游戏版本的俄罗斯方块，指出其不能实现某些 maneuver 的不足之处。

争议焦点：
• 名称问题：开发者最初将游戏命名为"LAZY PUBLIC DOMAIN BLOCK GAME"，但玩家建议更改名称以避免法律风险。
• 游戏随机性：玩家对游戏方块的随机性提出质疑，建议采用单袋系统以提高游戏公平性。

data.title: Show HN: PgDog – Shard Postgres without extensions
data.author: levkk
data.article_summary: PgDog 是一个用 Rust 编写的高性能事务池和逻辑复制管理器，专为 PostgreSQL 的自动分片和横向扩展设计。它支持管理数百个数据库和数十万个连接，具备负载均衡、健康检查、故障转移、事务池和分片等功能。PgDog 可以通过 Docker 和 Kubernetes Helm 快速部署，并支持使用 PgBouncer 风格的管理数据库和 OpenMetrics 进行监控。它还能够自动路由查询到不同的分片，处理跨分片查询，并支持逻辑复制以实现无停机扩展。PgDog 提供高度可配置的运行时选项，且大部分配置无需重启服务即可生效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PgDog工具的功能、应用及其在处理PostgreSQL数据库分片和高可用性方面的潜力

不同观点：
• jashmatthews（Jake）认为PgDog在处理如配置管理、分片分裂、跨分片事务等方面功能仍不足，并提出需要类似Vitess的解决方案。他还提到使用pg_query.rs重写查询时遇到AST不支持可变性和深度克隆的问题，并推荐了sqlparser crate作为替代方案。
• denysvitali强调了PgDog在读写分离（R/W split）方面的优势，认为这对许多不支持R/W分离的应用非常有帮助，能够显著提高速度。
• williamdclt对PgDog过度透明化处理分片表示担忧，认为在租户边界和跨分片查询的性能、内存及CPU影响上，应该更加明确和有控制，而不是完全抽象化。
• mijoharas和rco8786等人对PgDog表示赞赏，认为这是PostgreSQL扩展方面令人印象深刻的创新，并对项目的未来表示期待。
• PeterZaitsev指出，分片解决方案的挑战在于正确处理复杂查询和检测未正确处理的查询，以及隔离和一致性问题。
• Existenceblinks和aeyes提到PgDog目前不支持唯一索引和跨分片连接的问题，但仍对其未来发展表示乐观。
• jimmyl02关注PgDog在高可用性场景下的处理能力，特别是多前端代理和如何解决脑裂问题，并询问节点崩溃时的无停机重启方法。
• sroussey则关心PgDog的长期维护和更新计划，提到MySQLProxy和ProxySQL的历史。
• ewalk153询问PgDog在租户分片策略上的灵活性，特别是关于大租户的精细控制和热分片管理。

补充讨论：
• PgDog在透明化处理分片上的优缺点是讨论的焦点之一，部分人认为需要更多控制，部分人则赞赏其透明化特性。
• 高可用性和读写分离是用户关注的实际应用问题，尤其是多前端代理和无停机重启的能力。
• 关于PgDog未来发展的技术细节和长期维护计划也被多次提及，显示出用户对项目可持续性的关注。
• 具体技术实现如AST重写、唯一索引支持等也是技术用户关心的细节问题。

PgDog is a transaction pooler and logical replication manager that can shard PostgreSQL. Written in Rust, PgDog is fast, secure and can manage hundreds of databases and hundreds of thousands of connections.
Documentation
📘 PgDog documentation can be
found here
. Any questions? Join our
Discord
.
Quick start
Kubernetes
Helm chart is
here
. To install it, run:
git clone https://github.com/pgdogdev/helm
&&
\
cd
helm
&&
\
helm install -f values.yaml pgdog ./
Docker
You can try PgDog quickly using Docker. Install
Docker Compose
and run:
docker-compose up
It will take a few minutes to build PgDog from source and launch the containers. Once started, you can connect to PgDog with psql (or any other PostgreSQL client):
PGPASSWORD=postgres psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 6432 -U postgres
The demo comes with 3 shards and 2 sharded tables:
INSERT INTO
users (id, email)
VALUES
(
1
,
'
admin@acme.com
'
);
INSERT INTO
payments (id, user_id, amount)
VALUES
(
1
,
1
,
100
.
0
);
SELECT
*
FROM
users
WHERE
id
=
1
;
SELECT
*
FROM
payments
WHERE
user_id
=
1
;
Monitoring
PgDog exposes both the standard PgBouncer-style admin database and an OpenMetrics endpoint. The admin database isn't 100% compatible,
so we recommend you use OpenMetrics for monitoring. Example Datadog configuration and dashboard are
included
.
Features
Load balancer
PgDog is an application layer (OSI Level 7) load balancer for PostgreSQL. It can proxy multiple replicas (and primary) and distribute transactions evenly between databases. It supports multiple strategies, including round robin, random, least active connections, etc. PgDog can also inspect queries and send
SELECT
queries to replicas, and all others to the primary. This allows to proxy all databases behind a single PgDog deployment.
📘
Load balancer
Healthchecks and failover
PgDog maintains a real-time list of healthy hosts. When a host fails a healthcheck, it's removed from active rotation and queries are rerouted to other databases. This is similar to HTTP load balancing, except it's at the database layer.
Failover maximizes database availability and protects against bad network connections, temporary hardware failures or misconfiguration.
📘
Healthchecks
Transaction pooling
Like PgBouncer, PgDog supports transaction (and session) pooling, allowing
100,000s of clients to use just a few PostgreSQL server connections.
📘
Transactions
Sharding
PgDog is able to handle databases with multiple shards by routing queries automatically to one or more shards. Using the native PostgreSQL parser, PgDog understands queries, extracts sharding keys and determines the best routing strategy. For cross-shard queries, PgDog assembles results in memory and sends them all to the client transparently.
Using
COPY
PgDog comes with a CSV parser and can split COPY commands between all shards automatically. This allows clients to ingest data into sharded PostgreSQL without preprocessing.
Logical replication
PgDog understands the PostgreSQL logical replication protocol and can split data between databases in the background and without downtime. This allows to shard existing databases and add more shards to existing clusters in production, without impacting database operations.
📘
Sharding
Configuration
PgDog is highly configurable and many aspects of its operation can be tweaked at runtime, without having
to restart the process and break PostgreSQL connections. If you've used PgBouncer (or PgCat) before, the options
will be familiar. If not, they are documented with examples.
📘
Configuration
Running PgDog locally
Install the latest version of the Rust compiler from
rust-lang.org
.
Clone this repository and build the project in release mode:
cargo build --release
It's important to use the release profile if you're deploying to production or want to run
performance benchmarks.
Configuration
PgDog has two configuration files:
pgdog.toml
which contains general settings and PostgreSQL servers inform

data.title: Show HN: I wrote a modern Command Line Handbook
data.author: petr25102018
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一本关于Unix/Linux命令行使用的手册，适合软件开发者、系统管理员、技术工作者以及普通用户。无需阅读繁琐的指南，通过这本手册可以快速掌握常用概念和命令。手册涵盖终端、shell、命令行应用以及脚本编写，提供超过一百个带注释的shell操作示例，帮助读者自信运行命令。该书是作者四年学习的结晶，2025年更新后成为今年最佳指南，已有5700多名读者。手册以简洁方式展示命令行的核心功能，包含近100个语法高亮示例，旨在帮助用户充分利用命令行。手册定价14美元，读者可自行决定支付价格。
data.comments_summary:

data.title: Learning C3
data.author: lerno
data.article_summary: 本文记录了作者实时学习C3编程语言的体验。C3是一门基于C语言的现代系统编程语言，提供了诸如模块系统、运算符重载、泛型、编译时执行、语义宏等高级特性。作者从"Hello World"程序开始，逐步探索了C3的语法特性，包括`foreach`循环、`enum`与`switch`、`defer`关键字、结构体类型、错误处理、契约编程、宏、类型属性、Base64与Hex字面量等。C3通过要求使用完整命名空间来解决命名冲突，并支持格式化打印和C兼容的格式化符。作者认为C3对C程序员非常友好，同时提供了更现代化的编程体验，特别是在调试和代码组织方面。文章还简要介绍了如何安装C3和创建基本计算器项目。总体而言，C3结合了C语言的低级控制和现代语言的便捷特性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对编程语言C3的评价和比较

不同观点：
• **lerno**：分享了多个与C3相关的资源和项目链接，展示了C3在实际任务和项目中的应用，如Gameboy模拟器和RISCV的Hello World程序，表现出对C3的积极探索态度。

• **Defletter**：认为C3处理null值的方式不够理想，指出如果需要进行null检查，还不如使用Java。同时提到Java也在努力解决这个问题，表明对C3在这一方面的设计有所保留。

• **rdtsc**：提到另一种语言C2，提供了一个与C3相关的参考点，但没有深入比较两者的优劣。

• **throwawaymaths**：对C3的case语法提出批评，认为允许两个case执行相同操作的语法容易导致错误，建议修改语法以提高安全性。

• **plainOldText**：比较了C3和Hare，指出两者有相当多的重叠，询问社区对这两者的使用体验和看法。

• **tiniuclx**：对C3的优势提出疑问，特别是与Rust相比，强调社区支持对编程语言的重要性，但也承认C3在ABI兼容性和C互操作性方面的优点。

44125966.article_content:
2025-05-29 # Learning C3
In this article, I describe my experience learning the
C3
programming language.
I've always been an avid computer programmer. I would say that I am most familiar with low level systems
languages, though I have dipped into other programming languages from time to time. My journey here is
motivated by curiosity. I am always curious to try new programming languages, which has resulted in
learning a dozen or so within the past few years.
With each new programming language I learn, I encounter a never-before-seen paradigm. Each language has
it's own method of expressing ideas, and it's own status-quo for solving problems. I hope to learn what
this means for C3, and what projects I would be likely to use it for.
Here's the disclaimer: I'm writing this article in "real-time", which is to say I am typing it up as I
am learning C3. This means that I may have added insights about pain points and neat features that get
glossed over or forgotten in other aticles, yet it may also mean that my explanations and conceptual
grasp of the language is reduced or faulty compared to other sources.
Contents:
What is C3?
Language Overview
Hello World
foreach
loops
while
loops
enum
and
switch
defer
keyword
struct
types
Error handling
Contracts
struct
methods
macro
s
Type Properties
Base64 & Hex Literals
Primitives
Much More
First Steps
Installing C3
Creating a new project
Making a calculator with C3
What will this require?
Getting user input
The tokenizer
The parser
Conclusion
What is C3?
According to the C3 website, C3 aims to build on and with C. It offers ergonomics, optimizations, and
features. Some of these features may be difficult or impossible to express in standard C. These features
include a module system, operator overloading, generics, compile time execution, semantic macros,
an integrated build system, error handling,
defer
, value methods, associated enum data,
distinct types & subtypes, gradual contracts, built-in slices,
foreach
, dynamic calls &
types,
and more
.
Here are two other perspectives on what C3 is:
Thank you to FoxKiana and the C3 creator Christoffer Lernö for replying :)
Language Overview:
It's hard for me to picture what the language is like without clear examples. For this section I will
review the language reference online and share my thoughts on the language features C3 offers. I will
not cover each and every feature of C3, as this isn't meant to be an introduction to C3.
Hello World:
import std::io;
fn void main()
{
io::printn("Hello, World!");
}
Hello world seems pretty straightforward. I can immediately see this reminds me of C, although I
personally prefer having the opening brackets on the same line as the function declaration. In any case,
it's best to follow the status-quo here as it helps you understand other C3 code, and helps other C3
developers understand your code.
Something to note about importing modules - According to the
modules
page
, imports will recursively import submodules. C of course would do the same, and you might
end up needing to deal with name collisions by renaming things deep down the
#include
chain. C3 fixes the name collision issue by requiring you to use a more full case to resolve collisions.
For example, you would use
abc::Context
instead of
Context
if both imported
modules
abc
and
de
have a structure named
Context
.
I find it curious that the language requires the
fn
keyword to define the function here. I
would think that the language could get away with avoiding that keyword like C does. On further thought,
perhaps it is better to be more explicit that this is a function. Some reasons this may be is that the
function declaration syntax could be used elsewhere, or C3 could allow nested function declarations. The
first possibility seems more likely than the second, given that C3 is an evolution of C.
The
standard
print function
will print most types that are passed to it. That seems pretty nice! Definitely a
step-up from C here. I can imagine that
print
debugging works great in this language.
Taking a look at
formatted printing
, it seems that C3 resembles C quite a bit here. For the
printf
function,
%s
is still used for strings,
%d
is still used
for decimals,
%f
is still used for floats. Truly C3 is easing the transition for C
programmers. Something unique to note here - it seems that the string formatter (
%s
) can be
used to format certain non-string types as well - so an enum of type
Heat
with a value of
REALLY_WARM
would format itself as
REALLY_WARM
when you use the
%s
formatter.
foreach
loops:
// Prints the values in the slice.
fn void example_foreach(float[] values)
{
foreach (index, value : values)
{
io::printfn("%d: %f", index, value);
}
}
// Updates each value in the slice by multiplying it by 2.
fn void example_foreach_by_ref(float[] values)
{
foreach (&value : values)
{
*value *= 2;
}
}
Hold up, hold up.
C3 has foreach
? That is interesting. According to the docs,
break
and
continue
work as you would expect. Iteration by refere
44125966.article_summary: 本文记录了作者实时学习C3编程语言的体验。C3是一门基于C语言的现代系统编程语言，提供了诸如模块系统、运算符重载、泛型、编译时执行、语义宏等高级特性。作者从"Hello World"程序开始，逐步探索了C3的语法特性，包括`foreach`循环、`enum`与`switch`、`defer`关键字、结构体类型、错误处理、契约编程、宏、类型属性、Base64与Hex字面量等。C3通过要求使用完整命名空间来解决命名冲突，并支持格式化打印和C兼容的格式化符。作者认为C3对C程序员非常友好，同时提供了更现代化的编程体验，特别是在调试和代码组织方面。文章还简要介绍了如何安装C3和创建基本计算器项目。总体而言，C3结合了C语言的低级控制和现代语言的便捷特性。

44112686.article_content:
Eric Neyman
Prediction markets
,
Predictions
March 24, 2025
Thanks to Jesse Richardson for discussion.
Polymarket asks:
will Jesus Christ return in 2025?
In the three days since the market opened, traders have wagered over $100,000 on this question. The market traded as high as 5%, and is now stably trading at 3%. Right now, if you wanted to, you could place a bet that Jesus Christ will not return this year, and earn over $13,000 if you’re right.
There are two mysteries here: an easy one, and a harder one.
The easy mystery is: if people are willing to bet $13,000 on “Yes”, why isn’t anyone taking them up?
The answer is that, if you wanted to do that, you’d have to put down over $1 million of your own money, locking it up inside Polymarket through the end of the year. At the end of that year, you’d get 1% returns on your investment. And you can do
so much
better on the stock market, or even in U.S. treasury bonds.
So that’s why no one is buying the market down to 1%. But the real mystery is: why is anyone participating in the market on the “Yes” side? Like, who is betting that Jesus
will
return this year, and why?
Here are a few answers I came up with:
[True Believers] Maybe these people really believe that there’s a 3% chance that Christ will return this year!
[Incorrect Resolution] Maybe the “Yes” people are betting that the market will be resolved incorrectly (that there’s a 3% chance that the market will resolve “Yes” even though Christ will not return in 2025).
[The Memes] Maybe the “Yes” people are buying “Yes” for the lulz. It’s kinda fun to tell people that you bet that Jesus Christ would return this year!
But none of these hypotheses ring true to me:
The True Believers hypothesis rings false because that would be a frankly ridiculous belief to hold. Sometimes people profess ridiculous things, but very few of them put their money where their mouth is on prediction markets.
1
The Incorrect Resolution hypothesis rings false because, while there’s some chance of an incorrect resolution, it’s really unlikely to be as high as 3%. Polymarket has a lot of reputation to lose by incorrectly resolving this market, and would almost certainly override its
consensus-based resolution mechanism
if it came to that.
The Memes hypothesis is more plausible, but I think ultimately false. Several people have spent hundreds of dollars betting yes, which is a lot of money to spend for the memes.
So I asked my friend Jesse, who trades on Polymarket, and he had a pretty interesting theory:
[Time Value of Money] The Yes people are betting that, later this year, their counterparties (the No betters) will want cash (to bet on other markets), and so will sell out of their No positions at a higher price.
In other words: right now, there’s not much interesting stuff happening on Polymarket. People are spending a lot of money betting on sports, but not much else. But at some point in 2025, other markets will get a lot of attention. The
New York mayoral election
is happening this year. Pope Francis is in poor health, so there may be a
new pope
this year. God forbid
China invade Taiwan
, but such an invasion would result in many interesting markets. Right now, all these markets have mere single-digit millions of dollars in trading volume, but that could very easily change.
And if it changes, some of the people betting No on Christ’s return will want to unlock that money — that is, sell their “No” shares — so that they can use it to bet on other markets. If enough people want to sell their “No” shares, the “Yes” holders may be able to sell out at an elevated price, like 6%, potentially getting a 2x return on their investment!
The Time Value of Money hypothesis posits that the Yes bettors are more sophisticated than they look. In finance,
time value of money
is the idea that a dollar today is worth more than a dollar tomorrow, because you can do things with that dollar, such as making bets. The Yes traders are betting that the time value of Polymarket cash will go up unexpectedly: that other traders will be short on cash to place bets with, and will at some point be willing to pay a premium to free up the cash that they spent betting against Jesus.
Has this galaxy-brained trade ever gone well? Yes! In late October of last year — a week before the election — Kamala Harris was trading around 0.3% in safe red states like Kentucky, while Donald Trump was trading around 0.3% in safe blue states like Massachusetts. On election day, these prices
skyrocketed
to about 1.5%, because “No” bettors desperately needed cash to place other bets on the election. Traders who bought “Yes” for 0.3% in late October and sold at 1.5% on election day made a 5x profit! This means that even though Harris only had a 0.1% chance
2
of winning Kentucky, the “correct” price for the Kentucky market to trade at was more like 1.5%.
This means that the Jesus Christ market is quite interesting! You could make it even more interesting by replacing it with “This Market Wil

data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者妻子对编织的热情以及一个在编织社区迅速流行的现象——“情感支持鸡”。作者的妻子在短时间内掌握了复杂的编织技巧，并积极参与在线编织社区。社区中流行一种大小如抱枕的编织鸡，名为“情感支持鸡”，由Annette Corsino设计，灵感来自情感支持动物。自2023年该图案在Ravelry发布以来，已有近11,000人分享了他们编织的鸡照片。YouTube上的教程视频也获得了超过30万次观看。这种编织鸡不仅成为人们在家编织的热门项目，还被用于慈善活动，如为飓风幸存者编织。该趋势甚至被媒体报道，显示出其广泛的影响力。文章最后提到作者对这种小众艺术的兴趣，并附带了一些相关链接和个人近况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体和在线社区中的文化现象，特别是与心理健康、流行趋势以及特定物品（如鸡和编织图案）的关系。

不同观点：
• [alabastervlog] 对将一切归结为心理健康问题的趋势表示怀疑，认为这可能是一种社会玩笑，而非严肃的讨论。
• [LargeWu] 认为社交媒体和在线社区推动了文化的同质化。某个创意（如鸡）获得良好反应后，大家纷纷模仿，最终演变为追求流量的行为，随后这种趋势会被新的东西取代。
• [silisili] 提到鸡的流行可能与鸡蛋价格有关，但也指出其妻子的后院养鸡社区新成员激增，反映出实际供需问题，如孵化场缺货。
• [bentcorner] 将鸡的流行与Blender Donut（一个流行的初学者项目）类比，认为这是一种受欢迎的初学者项目。
• [munificent] 从编织爱好者的角度分析，认为鸡的流行是"幂律"作用的结果。特定物品因讨喜和恰逢心理健康潮流而变得更受欢迎，编织网站Ravelry上的热门图案即是例子。
• [stevetron] 以幽默方式建议可以编织鸡蛋并看它们变成编织鸡，或者编织粉红火烈鸟。
• [jsharpe] 提供了一个视频链接，暗示视频内容可能与讨论相关。
• [HocusLocus] 以幽默和阴谋论的方式暗示鸡的流行与FDA的记录发布有关。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于鸡的流行是否仅仅是社交媒体效应和追求流量的结果，还是与实际经济因素（如鸡蛋价格）相关。
• 编织社区中的流行趋势（如Emotional Support Chicken）被认为是幂律分布的实例，显示出特定物品如何通过网络效应变得极度流行。
• 讨论中还包含幽默和讽刺元素，如编织鸡蛋和FDA阴谋论，增加了讨论的趣味性和多样性。

44108139.article_content:
A couple years ago, my wife began knitting. And when she takes an interest in something, she goes all in. She’s a perfectionist about learning a new craft, so in a short amount of time, she’s gotten pretty damn good. I can’t even pretend to know anything more than the most basic idea behind knitting, but somehow she makes incredibly complex garments with skill and precision.
She’s also become active in the online knitting community, which is interesting for me to watch because she’s otherwise not really active online. But now she follows
r/knitting
and shares on
Ravelry
and watches knitting videos on YouTube.
The other day she told me about something that’s spread like wildfire through the knitting community: chickens. Knitted chickens. They’re roughly the size of a throw pillow and are stuffed with material to be soft and huggable. Everybody’s making them.
“Emotional Support Chicken” by Annette Corsino
Since
the knitting pattern
for this chicken was posted on Ravelry in 2023, nearly 11,000 people have posted photos of their own knitted chickens on the platform. The official
tutorial video
has more than 300,000 views on YouTube with comments like: “This pattern should come with a warning that it is HIGHLY ADDICTIVE! I have finished 4 so far and am working on 2 more.”
People give their knitted chickens names like Hennifer Lopez and Lindsey LoHEN, a punny habit shared by owners of actual backyard chickens,
who also like
to name their birds after celebrities. (Mine would be Henny Youngman.)
And there are knittable accessories, natch.
Accessories by Annette Corsino
I was fascinated by all this. I love little artsy niches and this one was completely new to me. I had to know where the knitted chicken came from. The answer turned out to be easy to find, it just never overlapped with my own interests so I never came across it before.
The knitted chicken is known as the Emotional Support Chicken and was designed by Annette Corsino at a fiber arts shop in Los Angeles called
The Knitting Tree
. She made the chicken as a sort of play on emotional comfort animals, but one that doesn’t require any sort of permit to own or need to feed it.
It was adapted from an earlier chicken design from the 90s called Henrietta (another “hen” name) by Bev Galeskas.
The original Henrietta by Bev Galeskas
The idea of a comforting stuffed animal for grownups (or anyone really) that you can make yourself was appealing to a lot of people in these hard times. During COVID lockdowns, people developed indoor hobbies like knitting which meant there were a lot of new knitters among the old-timers looking for things to knit. Knitting is a relaxing activity for many, and the Chicken knitting pattern wasn’t too difficult, so it made a good project for beginner-to-intermediate knitters.
In 2024, the LA Times
reported
(with great photos you should go look at) that people were gathering at The Knitting Tree for Emotional Support Chicken knit-along events. By then the store had already sold 25,000 copies of the knitting pattern and more than 3,000
kits
including everything you need except for needles and stuffing.
I admit that it does look kind of comforting to hug one of these chickens. And that comforting quality has prompted a
Facebook group
to knit Emotional Support Chickens for survivors of Hurricane Helene. The group description says, “There has been a request for chickens for those suffering from this historical tragedy. This is something I know we can do together! Let’s get together and make some chickens yall!!”
A couple weeks ago
someone in the group shared
this photo of an Emotional Support Chicken being delivered, noting “The need is real. I carry a few emergency chickens all the time now.”
Variations on the pattern include a crochet version, a mini-version, etc. And it’s a perfect feel-good story for TV news. Here are a couple stories I came across:
And the BBC reported on a yarn shop in Suffolk that displayed 67 olympic-themed chickens knitted by people around the world in its front window.
Olympic-themed knitted hens take over Long Melford shop front
Sixty-seven ‘Olympi’hens’ have been decorated to represent different nations in the Games.
BBC News
More fun photos await if you click through
This is obviously a trend that lots of people know about, and I have just been out of the loop (that’s a knitting pun). Have any of my readers ever made an emotional support chicken? What did you name it?
And that brings another newsletter to a close! So far, the move to Ghost seems to be going okay, right? No problems on your end? Only one person said they missed last issue so hopefully everyone else is getting it.
As long as you’re here, I have something for the font nerds among us. You know who you are. I directed a short documentary for Nebula about their new font and it’s now on YouTube:
Hope everyone has a great week. See you next time!
David

data.title: Show HN: Weather2Geo – Geolocate screenshots from weather widgets
data.author: Elliott-Diy
data.article_summary: Weather2Geo是一个开源OSINT工具，利用泄露的天气小部件数据（时间、温度、天气状况）进行地理定位。它使用与Windows天气小部件相同的API，通过匹配天气信息（时间、温度、天气状况）在真实城市中查找符合条件的地点。该工具具有时区感知、集群分析和可扩展性等特点，适合在截图发布后短时间内使用以获得最佳效果。安装和使用需要通过Git克隆项目并运行Python脚本，提供时间和天气细节以获取地理位置集群。该工具仅限于道德和教育用途，强调尊重隐私和法律界限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否计划抓取数据并建立历史数据库，以便能够使用旧的截图

不同观点：
• [支持建立历史数据库] @progbits 认为建立一个历史数据库是个很好的主意，可以让旧的截图也能够被使用。这表明了对数据长期保存和可访问性的重视，希望能够克服技术困难以实现这一目标。

• [对技术挑战的担忧] @progbits 同时意识到实现这一想法可能面临的技术困难，特别是突破速率限制（rate limits），这暗示了在数据抓取和存储过程中可能会遇到的实际问题。

补充讨论：
• [技术挑战的具体细节] 提到了速率限制是主要的潜在障碍，表明数据抓取工作可能需要应对网站对自动化访问的控制和限制。
• [潜在价值] 尽管存在技术挑战，建立历史数据库被认为是有价值的，因为它可以增强用户对历史数据的可访问性。

争议焦点：目前没有明显的争议，但存在理想功能（建立历史数据库）与实际技术限制（速率限制等）之间的张力。

Weather2Geo
Overview
Weather2Geo
is a focused OSINT tool that turns weather widget leaks into geolocation data.
People post screenshots with the Windows weather widget in their taskbar all the time, showing the exact temperature, weather condition, and local time. This tool uses the same API as the widget to find cities where those conditions are currently true.
⚠️
This tool works best if used shortly after the screenshot is posted. Conditions change fast.
Features
Geolocation from Widgets
: Match weather condition, temp, and time to a list of real cities
Timezone-Aware
: Localizes your input to each city’s timezone for accurate comparison
Clustering
: Groups nearby hits to reduce noise
Extensible
: Tweak tolerance, data sources, and clustering distance
Installation
git clone https://github.com/elliott-diy/Weather2Geo
cd
Weather2Geo
pip install -r requirements.txt
Usage
python main.py run --time
"
2025-05-22 14:00
"
--condition
"
Mostly cloudy
"
--temp 18 --tolerance 1.0
Options
Flag
Description
--time
Local time shown in the screenshot (
YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
)
--condition
Weather condition string (e.g., "Partly cloudy")
--temp
Temperature in Celsius
--tolerance
Temp wiggle room (default: 1.0°C)
--cluster-distance
Max distance in KM to group hits (default: 15)
--cities-file
Path to GeoNames cities file (default:
cities15000.txt
)
Example Use Case
You spot a screenshot that says:
Mostly clear | 13°C | 10:09 PM | May 22
Run:
python main.py run --time
"
2025-05-22 22:09
"
--condition
"
Mostly clear
"
--temp 13
And you'll get clusters of cities like:
Cluster 1 – 10 locations:
- US Seattle — 13°C, mostly clear
- US Bellevue — 13°C, mostly clear
...
Data Sources
City List
:
GeoNames
cities15000.txt
Weather
:
MSN Weather API
— same backend as the Windows widget
Disclaimer
This tool is for ethical, educational OSINT use only. Don’t be a creep. Respect privacy and legal boundaries.

data.title: The Maid Who Restored Charles II
data.author: samclemens
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了1659年英国复辟君主制过程中一位被遗忘的关键人物——乔治·蒙克将军的妻子安妮。乔治·蒙克手握重权，面临选择：是继续支持残缺议会，还是与流亡的查理二世联系。最终，他选择支持查理二世复辟，而这背后起到关键作用的是他的妻子安妮。安妮原是伦敦塔的洗衣女工，与被囚禁的乔治相识并秘密结婚，尽管她当时可能仍有婚姻在身。她的影响力帮助乔治做出了改变历史的决定，使查理二世顺利复位。安妮的故事长期被忽视，但她对英国历史的贡献不可忽视。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对英国内战的不同视角及其在历史教学和文章细节中的讨论

不同观点：
• [lordleft] 认为英国内战像是18世纪晚期动荡的预演，其中蕴含了美国和法国大革命的许多思想萌芽，例如平等主义和思想自由。他还指出，内战中从君主制到共和制再回到君主制的循环（美国除外）与后来的历史发展有相似之处。此外，他批评美国学校对这一段历史的教学不足，尽管它对理解美国建国背景非常重要。

• [gbolcer] 并没有对英国内战的宏观历史意义发表看法，而是关注文章中的一个具体用词，认为文章可能误用了"Stuart"一词，正确的用词应为"steward"。这属于对文章细节的技术性评论，而非对历史事件的分析。

补充讨论：
• [lordleft] 的评论引发了对历史教学的批评，指出英国内战在教育中被忽视的问题，并通过举例说明其对理解美国建国背景的重要性。
• [gbolcer] 的评论则聚焦于文章中的词汇使用，尽管这是一个较小的技术性问题，但也显示出读者对文章细节的关注。
• 争议的焦点在于历史事件的宏观分析与文章具体用词的技术性细节之间的差异，[lordleft] 关心历史事件的意义和教育，而 [gbolcer] 则关注文章的用词准确性。

44123486.article_content:
Feature
The Maid Who Restored Charles II
In 1659 the restoration of the exiled Charles II seemed impossible. It might not have occurred at all but for the forgotten intervention of a blacksmith’s daughter.
Anna Keay
| Published in
History Today
Volume 72 Issue 4 April 2022
I
n the early months of 1660 the taciturn West Country soldier George Monck held the fate of the British Isles in his hands. Oliver Cromwell was dead and the British republic had descended into chaos. The army and its leaders had ousted his son, Richard, and – once again – marched Members of Parliament out of their chamber in Westminster before bolting the door. Monck had been watching at a distance as army chief of Scotland. In the ensuing game of military and strategic chess, played for the future of the nation, he intervened as few had done before or since. Declaring his support for the expelled parliament, he marched south.
Monck enabled the MPs to return but, having done so, those parliamentarians then instructed him to arrest prominent London citizens and emasculate the city. He faced a stark choice. Would he carry out these orders, with which he bitterly disagreed, at the command of the ‘Rump’ Parliament? Would he reinstate Richard Cromwell as Lord Protector or take control by slipping into those shoes himself? Or would Monck do the unthinkable and make contact with the exiled Stuart, Charles II?
The question of how and why George Monck made the choices he did – resulting in the return of the monarchy on terms almost unchanged from those it enjoyed before its abolition in 1649 – has been long debated. That had certainly not been his original intention. How and when was his mind changed? Was it Charles Stuart and his agents or the Parliamentary leader Arthur Haselrige? Was it his disgust with fellow army officers or the intervention of the retired hero of the New Model Army, Thomas Fairfax?
In fact, the person who won George over was his wife, Anne. This remarkable woman has not been the subject of a biography and, unlike 60,000 other figures, she does not even have an entry in the
Dictionary of National Biography
. Yet without her influence the course of British history would have been entirely different.
Love in a hopeless place
Anne Monck met her future husband in the least promising circumstances: the dank chambers of the Tower of London in the mid-1640s. George Monck was a prisoner, she the laundry maid or seamstress who washed and repaired the inmates’ clothing. Though George was a detainee, Anne was still many rungs below him on the social ladder. He was the 37-year-old son of a Devon knight. She was the daughter of a Soho blacksmith in her mid-20s. Their characters were also different. He was serious and uncommunicative, ‘the most reserved man alive’. She had a lively forthright manner that displeased many but captivated him.
As a soldier of the royal army George had been captured by the parliamentary forces at the Battle of Nantwich in 1644. He was thought worth retaining and so was sent to the Tower, where he whiled away long hours writing a manual of military discipline. What relief Anne’s visits gave him and exactly what transpired between them is lost to history. But from that time on he ‘never cast an amorous glance upon any other woman’.
General George Monck, duke of Albemarle, after Michael van der Gucht. Yale Center for British Art, Paul Mellon Collection. Public Domain.
George Monck was released from the Tower on the condition that he join his former opponents. He did so without hesitation, having fought for the king as a career soldier rather than from any ideological fervour. When he left London, Anne went with him. In the remaining years of the Civil War George’s abilities saw him promoted, rising up the ranks as the New Model Army fought on to victory. When moderate MPs were purged from Parliament and Charles I was tried and executed by an army-backed minority, the Moncks voiced no protest.
In 1653 Anne gave birth to a son named Christopher. A furtive wedding took place in the early months of the pregnancy in St George’s Church, Southwark, at which only the couple’s Christian names were entered in the parish register. There was a good reason for such secrecy: Anne Clarges was already married, betrothed in her teens to haberdasher Thomas Radford. He was from Derbyshire but had been apprenticed in London and kept a shop at the New Exchange. From here, Anne had plied her trade as a seamstress, which had taken her to the Tower of London. As the Moncks’ relationship was sealed, the Radfords’ disintegrated. It was later claimed that Thomas had died, though when evidence was sought in the burial registers none could be found. Instead, Radford had, it seems, been induced to leave London.
Bigamy was a serious crime, punishable by death, so the risk George and Anne ran was colossal. Monck would later remark of his intervention in national politics that it was better to chance death in the jaws of a lion than to be slowly

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了开发自主大型语言模型（LLM）游戏大师的两种方法：快速代理方法和慢速深入理解方法。作者原本计划使用快速方法，通过搭建MCP服务器并利用前端模型快速实现目标，但最终选择从基础模型开始，逐步构建，以更好地理解模型能力的全栈开发过程。由于计算资源有限，作者将选择能够在小预算内训练的较小模型，如Qwen3系列，并通过继续训练这些模型来嵌入特定于桌面角色扮演游戏（TTRPG）的知识，尤其是Shadowdark RPG的规则。作者的目标是先开发一个可以辅助游戏大师或玩家的模型，再逐步过渡到更具代理性的游戏大师模型。文章还提到继续预训练模型以嵌入特定领域知识的重要性，并强调理解规则和在游戏中灵活应用这些规则的能力。

44126214.article_content:
There’s a fast way and a slow way to go about developing an autonomous LLM Game Master. The fast way - the
agentic
way - would probably be to build some MCP servers to act as a harness, providing access to maps and rulesets, plugging the results into a frontier model and seeing what happened.
I was intending to go that way, developing some environments I could do
GRPO
on immediately. The thought was, provide an MCP server that allowed rule search, and then come up with some combat scenarios that had verifiable outcomes
1
. Those would work both as eval for frontier models and external rewards for any model being trained, and would certainly go a lot further a lot faster to getting to the final desired result.
However, that would only make sense if my goal was primarily or exclusively to get to the end product: an LLM that can run TTRPGs. It’s not. The goal is to get a better understanding of the front-to-back development of model capabilities and get as much painful hands on experience as possible with every part of the stack. Besides, with the research suggesting RL may just be focusing skills/knowledge a pretrained model
already has
. At any rate, it makes sense to bake in priors specific to TTRPGs - their rulesets are particular, and a baseline understanding of their structure would make any tool-assisted lookups easier to do, and the results of that search easier to interpret for that model. So, we’ll start with base models and work our way up from scratch.
Before we have an LLM GM, we’ll create a model that can act as an assistant to a GM or player playing a TTRPG, and see how such a system can make a transition to a more agentic GM.
Getting Started
#
The additional constraint is around compute. This project is GPU poor. Due to those constraints, we’ll only choose models we can reasonably train without blowing our budget. We’ll be seeking to make this model as
small as possible
while still being useful. I’m an admirer of
Alexander Doria’s
work, which inspired me to work with small models and synthetic datasets. The new Qwen3 series appears to have been pre-trained
really well
. In addition, it has quite a few different sizes of dense base models, starting at a minute 0.6B up to a respectable 14B. If my compute situation were to change
2
, these different size models would let us experiment with scaling laws on these tasks/datsets.
Also, crucially, it appears to know nothing about
Shadowdark RPG
whatsoever, the TTRPG I’ll be focused on for these experiments.
Asking Qwen3-8B:
“What do you know about Shadowdark RPG?”
Results in:
“Shadowdark RPG is a horror-themed tabletop role-playing game (RPG) created by James Raggi, the same designer behind the Dungeons & Dragons 3.5 edition. It is designed to immerse players in a grim, survival-focused setting where the goal is not to defeat monsters but to survive the horrors of the world.”
Qwen goes on to explain the game is out of print from a now defunct publisher, but still has an active scene of reprints and fan-made modules. This sounds nice and plausible but is totally hallucinated. The designer is in fact the wonderful Kelsey Dionne
3
, who runs the very much thriving company “The Arcane Library”. Shadowdark does have a somewhat darker tone, but is at its base a heroic fantasy RPG that trims a lot of the fat of modern 5th edition DND. It’s a fun game, and has been something of an indie darling for those moving away from DND who aren’t ready to get an associate’s degree in
Pathfinder
.
Initially I was considering diving right into an LLM for 5e DND, but decided against it for a few reasons. For starters, it’s
big
. Positive from availability of training data, but less forgiving on the wallet to acquire all those materials. There have also been so many versions of DND at so many different points in the ruleset that there are going to be tons of priors even in base models I can get my hands on that I would know nothing about. Pretraining from scratch is infeasible, but having some assurance that I’m starting from close-to-nothing in terms of introducing knowledge during pretraining makes me feel a little more scientific. Finally, simple laziness. To verify a game of DND is being run “according to the rules” is hilariously complicated, and I would spend more time doing personal rules lawyering than working on model development.
So our interest here is seeing how continued training of a small base model with tokens associated with a new domain can bake in knowledge we want. Particularly, knowledge about how the game broadly functions, and specifically knowledge recall of particular rulesets. This maps to how GMs work in real life: they go to the rulebook if there’s something obscure to recall, but they understand most of the rules intuitively and can simply focus on running the game, using that knowledge on the fly to adjudicate a game in flight.
Continuing Pretraining
#

data.article_summary: ClickHouse,一家实时分析、数据仓库、可观察性和人工智能/机器学习领域的公司，宣布完成3.5亿美元的C轮融资，由Khosla Ventures领投。此轮融资将用于扩展产品开发、支持全球扩张以及深化与客户和技术供应商的合作，以构建下一代AI原生应用。ClickHouse在过去一年中增长超过300%，目前拥有2000多家客户，包括Anthropic、Tesla和Mercado Libre等新客户，以及Sony、Meta和Lyft等现有客户。公司CEO Aaron Katz表示，ClickHouse旨在支持广泛的实时数据应用，满足企业和AI代理对实时分析的需求。传统数据库难以满足这些需求，而ClickHouse的高性能、列式存储引擎专为大规模实时分析和AI/ML应用设计，具有低延迟和高吞吐量优势。

ClickHouse raises $350 million Series C to power analytics for the AI era
ClickHouse Team
May 29, 2025

SAN FRANCISCO, CA — May 29, 2025
— ClickHouse, Inc., a leader in real-time analytics, data warehousing, observability, and AI/ML, today announced it has raised $350 million in Series C financing. The round was led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from new investors BOND, IVP, Battery Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, as well as existing investors including Index Ventures, Lightspeed, GIC, Benchmark, Coatue, FirstMark, and Nebius. Today’s round follows earlier investments of over $300 million, bringing total funding to over $650 million.
This combined funding will be used to scale product development, support global expansion, and deepen partnerships with customers and technology providers building the next wave of AI-native applications. In addition to this financing, ClickHouse has secured a $100 million credit facility led by Stifel and Goldman Sachs.
The momentum behind ClickHouse is accelerating: the company grew over 300% during the past year and now serves over 2,000 customers across a range of industries from fintech and transportation to consumer and healthcare. New customers include Anthropic, Tesla, and Argentina’s Mercado Libre, among others. They join companies such as Sony, Meta, Memorial Sloan Kettering, Lyft, and Instacart, as well as AI innovators Sierra, Poolside, Weights & Bases, Langchain, and more.
Today’s announcement was made at ClickHouse’s inaugural user conference, showcasing how enterprises are building data products to meet the demands of the agentic era.
“As AI agents proliferate across data-driven applications, observability, data infrastructure, and beyond, the demand for agent-facing databases like ClickHouse has reached an inflection point. The future of analytics isn’t just dashboards. It’s intelligent agents that interpret data, trigger workflows, and power real-time decisions,” said Aaron Katz, CEO of ClickHouse. “But AI is just one driver. We designed and built ClickHouse from day one to support a broad spectrum of real-time data applications across industries, and our momentum reflects that enterprises are hungry for a platform that can keep up with their scaling ambitions.”
“We invested in ClickHouse because they’re solving one of the most important infrastructure challenges of this era of AI and agents: enabling real-time data platforms that can support both traditional analytics and the growing demands of AI-native workloads,” said Ethan Choi, Partner at Khosla Ventures. “As AI reshapes every industry, the ability to deliver fast, scalable, and cost-efficient analytics is becoming foundational, ClickHouse is poised to become the default engine for next-generation intelligent data products.”
The next frontier: real-time analytics for agentic workloads
#
The market traction around ClickHouse is rooted in a fundamental shift: enterprises are no longer just building dashboards or batch reports—they are building real-time, intelligent data platforms that must serve both human and AI agents. Since AI agents can generate queries much faster and at a higher rate than human analysts, agent-facing databases must support low-latency, interactive analytical queries at an increasingly high throughput.
ClickHouse was designed from the ground up to meet this demand. Its high-performance, columnar storage engine enables interactive, analytical queries across massive datasets with minimal latency—perfect for powering AI and ML applications, real-time analytics, cloud data warehousing, and observability workloads.
Built for speed at scale: high-performance analytics across industries
#
Traditional databases and warehouses are struggling to keep up with this demand. Transactional databases don’t scale for analytical workloads. Meanwhile, traditional data warehouses are optimized for internal, batch-heavy use cases with limited concurrency and slow performance. Finally, search-oriented technologies become prohibitively expensive for structured analytics—using 10x more in storage and compute and limiting the practical range of applications due to cost.
By contrast, ClickHouse offers a purpose-built solution that bridges the gap—combining high-performance analytics with the scalability and concurrency that today’s intelligent, data-driven applications require.
About ClickHouse
#
ClickHouse is a fast, open-source columnar database management system built for real-time data processing and analytics at scale. Engineered for high performance, ClickHouse Cloud delivers exceptional query speed and concurrency, making it ideal for applications that demand instant insight from massive volumes of data. As AI agents become increasingly embedded in software and are generating far more frequent and complex queries, ClickHouse brings a high-throughput, low-latency engine, purpose-built to meet this challenge. • amazingamazing：关注自托管ClickHouse集群的难度以及与托管服务之间的功能对等性，表明用户对自建和使用托管服务的选择有所顾虑。

• devops000：对ClickHouse的商业模式表示怀疑，认为以200美元/月的价格可以获得一个良好的数据库，而ClickHouse的收入与其用户数量不匹配。这暗示了对ClickHouse商业可行性的质疑。

• whiskeytwolima：对ClickHouse团队在公开场合的形象表示关注，特别是衬衫没有熨烫的小细节，属于非技术性评论。

不同观点：
• [cjs_ac] 认为法律并非像算法一样机械执行，而是需要法院根据具体案例进行解释。他通过文章提醒大家，法律是一种启发式规则，而不是固定的程序。
• [sph] 通过McVities的Jaffa Cake案例类比，指出类似法律争议往往依赖于特定的产品特性（如Jaffa Cake变硬而不是变软），从而影响其法律分类。
• [masfuerte] 引用了Walkers在法庭上的辩论，指出他们最初认为某些产品（Sensations）不属于薯片，因为这些产品需要进一步准备才能食用，但后来放弃了这一论点。
• [comrade1234] 质疑英国对薯片征收20%关税的动机，并开玩笑地暗示这可能是为了防止爱尔兰薯片占据市场。
• [normie3000] 对文章中将Discos不视为薯片表示困惑和反对。

补充讨论：
• [TheOtherHobbes] 对零食的口味进行了个人评价，表达了对某一口味的喜爱，但没有参与法律或分类讨论。
• [ChrisMarshallNY] 提到了Walker’s Poppadom Chips与文化现象（Poppadom Elvis）的关联，将讨论引向娱乐和文化层面。
• [comrade1234]（另一个评论）对poppadoms的材料进行了探讨，指出其可以由多种材料制成，包括土豆。
• [petesergeant] 引用了一个幽默的法庭陈述，强调某些食物是否为薯片的问题有时很难定义，但法官通过视觉和经验判断。
• [AStonesThrow] 提到了Walkers品牌与Walker’s Shortbread的区别，并讨论了不同文化中零食的多样性，以及这些零食如何受到外来文化的影响。

争议的焦点：
• 主要集中在食品的法律分类和定义问题上，例如薯片与非薯片的区分标准，以及这些标准在实际案例中的应用。
• 对某些食品征收高关税的动机也存在一定的质疑和调侃。

总体来看，讨论围绕着食品分类、法律解释以及文化背景对食品认知的影响展开，其中夹杂了一些幽默和个人口味的评价。

data.title: The Art of the Critic
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了亨利·詹姆斯（Henry James）作为文学评论家的角色及其对批评的见解。詹姆斯对同时代英国小说的评价苛刻，认为大多平庸无奇，但他赞赏美国作家威廉·迪恩·豪威尔斯（William Dean Howells）的自然主义写作。他批评查尔斯·狄更斯（Charles Dickens）的作品缺乏深度和对人性理解的贡献，尽管承认狄更斯是出色的观察者和幽默家。詹姆斯强调，批评需要才华和敏感性，而他在年轻时已展现出这些特质。文章还提到，詹姆斯深受法国作家巴尔扎克（Honoré de Balzac）影响，认为其对细节的过度追求既是缺点也是其叙事风格的核心。詹姆斯作为评论家，能够从小处着眼，思考大局，展现出独特的批评艺术。

Claude Monet,
Le Parc Monceau
, 1876, Oil on canvas
“The floods of tepid soap and water which under the name of novels are being vomited forth in England, seem to me,” Henry James wrote, “to do little honour to our race.” In February 1884, 40-year-old James dismissed contemporary British novels in a letter to American novelist and editor William Dean Howells. James then went on to laud Howells as “the great American naturalist” before tempering his praise: “I don't think you go far enough, and you are haunted with romantic phantoms and a tendency to factitious glosses; but you are in the right path, and I wish you repeated triumphs there.”
James had opinions. He also had the language — and the critical sensibility — with which to effectively, and lyrically, express those opinions. Criticism without flair is dull, and criticism without sensibility is useless. James had plied his critical trade for years; a notable early work was a terrible gift for Charles Dickens a few days before Christmas in 1865. Writing of
Our Mutual Friend
for
The Nation
, James dismissed the novel as “poor with the poverty not of momentary embarrassment, but of permanent exhaustion.”
Bleak House
was “forced,”
Little Dorrit
“labored,” and
Our Mutual Friend
“dug out as with a spade and a pickaxe.” “Seldom,” James affirms, “had we read a book so intensely written, so little seen, known, or felt.”
James’ criticism was especially sharp because he identifies Dickens’ literary failings as inextricable from the novelist’s method and sense.
Our Mutual Friend
was not merely a bad book, a misfire. Dickens was perhaps incapable of better. He seems to only create “figure[s],” and in doing so “added nothing to our understanding of human character.” Dickens was “a great observer and a great humorist,” but those are skills of attention and entertainment. James is clear: Dickens “is nothing of a philosopher.” And that is a grave sin, for “a novelist very soon has need of a little philosophy.”
Dickens was 53: a celebrated, prolific writer. James was 22; he’d left Harvard Law after a year, and had only published a few, forgettable stories. Yet James was ambitious, and he could write well, and — perhaps most importantly — there was a space for critics to practice their craft.
“Most people don’t read criticism, not beyond the length of a review,” Michael Gorra acknowledges in
Portrait of a Novel: Henry James and the Making of an American Masterpiece
. Yet they do “read narrative,” and his 2012 biography of the novelist manages to embed criticism within story. Gorra is the ideal curator of James’ essays; he has a deft sense of the novelist’s life and language, and his curation of
On Writers and Writing: Selected Essays
collects a healthy range of work. Here we see classic James, as in the essential essay “The Art of Fiction,” as well as his reviews of contemporary novels, expansive memorials and valedictions, and examinations of the forms of fiction.
In 1905, James spoke to the Contemporary Club of Philadelphia, a literary and artistic group (Walt Whitman and Woodrow Wilson had been previous guests). His subject was the French writer Honoré de Balzac. James had been writing about Balzac for thirty years. Balzac was James’ lodestar: James had “learned from him more of the lessons of the engaging mystery of fiction than from anyone else.”
James owed much to Balzac, and his debt is revealed through the care of his engagement rather than mere deference. Balzac’s “inordinate passion for detail” is “also his great fault,” yet such saturation is “essentially prescribed by the terms of his plan.” A critic needs to see small and think big, and James was able to perceive Balzac’s narrative method as being “characteristic and constructive.” Although Balzac’s details “multiplied almost to madness,” the style revealed “the measure of his hallucination.” Balzac wished to animate “the palpable, provable world before him,” yet his singular vision meant that he “collected his experience within himself.”
James proceeds to introduce an ambitious analogy, likening Balzac to “a Benedictine monk leading his life within the four walls of his convent.” A libertine Catholic with an especial penchant for Jesuits, the image of Balzac as a coffee-fueled ascetic is a plausible one. James, though, had a gift for teasing out the complexity of his analogical thinking. Balzac embraced a hyperbolic image of himself; “he was most at ease, while he wrought, in the white gown and cowl.” Despite his monkish tendencies toward art, Balzac’s “subject of illumination was the legends not merely of the saints, but of the much more numerous uncanonized strug

data.title: I started a little math club in Bangalore
data.author: viveknathani_
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Vivek Nathani在班加罗尔发起的一个数学俱乐部。由于毕业后缺乏合作学习的机会，Vivek希望重现学生时代与朋友们一起讨论和解决数学问题的社区氛围。俱乐部的第一次聚会于2025年3月15日在Kormangala的Dialogues Cafe举行，有7人参加。第二次聚会于2025年5月4日举行，有8人参加。每次聚会都包括共同解决数学问题，并分享心得。Vivek对发起这个俱乐部感到非常满意，并欢迎更多人加入。感兴趣的人可以通过邮件或Twitter与他联系。

• [seanhunter] 作为数学学习者，对该数学学习社区表示赞赏，认为这是一个很好的想法。他的观点侧重于对数学学习的热情和学习社区的价值。

I started a little math club in Bangalore.
Why
Since finishing college a few years ago, studying math has been a mostly solitary pursuit for me.
While I enjoy exploring new concepts and solving problems on my own, I often miss the collaborative spirit of my
academic days.
Back then, my friends and I would gather to discuss homework problems, share insights, and learn from each other.
There was a unique joy in exploring ideas together, something that’s hard to replicate alone.
I’d love to bring back that sense of community, where math isn’t just an isolated exercise but a shared
experience.

44126518.article_content:
Making History
Medieval Fogge: In Defence of the Middle Ages
The medieval era did not wallow in savage, ignorant darkness, despite what some would have us believe.
George Garnett
| Published in
History Today
Volume 75 Issue 6 June 2025
I
n a recent tweet, Robert Jenrick, shadow justice secretary, denounced immigrants from ‘alien cultures, who possess medieval attitudes towards women’. He claimed that these ‘medieval attitudes’ were responsible for the widespread sexual abuse of white girls in Britain. Interviewed on the
Today
programme, it became clear that for him ‘medieval’ was synonymous with ‘backward’ – ‘alien’, that is, to progressive, modern Britain. Professor Kathleen Stock, whose expression of her views on gender aroused great hostility at the University of Sussex, has characterised that hostility as ‘medieval’. By this she appears to mean backward, in the sense of prejudiced and irrational. The equation of ‘medieval’ with reprehensibly primitive is never questioned, but increasingly parroted, in the media.
What humanists in the 15th century came to term the
medium aevum
– hence ‘medieval’ – was the gap between the collapse of classical antiquity and its renaissance, over which they presented themselves as officiating. In origin, therefore, the term was a retrospective humanist slur on the preceding millennium.

data.title: Asus router backdoors affect 9K devices, persist after firmware updates
data.author: Bender
data.article_summary: 截至2025年5月，研究报告显示数千台华硕路由器被植入了无恶意软件后门，可能用于未来构建僵尸网络。这些后门通过利用安全漏洞和合法路由器功能建立持久访问，即使重启或更新固件也无法清除。攻击者利用暴力破解和认证绕过漏洞获取初始访问权限，然后通过TCP/53282端口建立SSH连接，使用攻击者控制的公钥进行远程控制。特别影响的型号包括ASUS RT-AC3200、RT-AC3100和RT-AX55。由于后门配置存储在非易失性内存（NVRAM）中，建议用户对受感染设备进行出厂重置，并手动重新配置。同时，应阻止报告中提到的恶意IP地址并确保设备已更新以修补安全漏洞。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ASUS路由器存在的安全漏洞及相关问题

不同观点：
• [ctippett] 认为ASUS路由器的漏洞问题并不令人意外，并引用了2017年Darknet Diaries播客中的一集，讨论了ASUS路由器的广泛漏洞问题。这表明ASUS路由器的安全问题早已存在，且可能一直没有得到有效解决。
• [Saris] 具体指出了ASUS路由器的管理界面和SSH通过WAN端口访问的问题，认为这是一个重大的安全隐患。同时提到关闭所谓的“后门”似乎只需要禁用SSH，暗示问题可能没有想象中复杂。
• [jwilk] 对“无恶意软件的后门”这一表述表示疑惑，质疑其具体含义，表明对相关术语和概念的不确定性，可能反映出公众对安全漏洞描述的困惑。
• [lotharcable] 分享了使用Banana Pi BPI-R3与OpenWRT组合来解决消费级WiFi路由器问题的经验，认为这是一种经济有效的替代方案，暗示对传统消费级路由器的不信任。

ASUS router backdoors affect 9K devices, persist after firmware updates
May 28, 2025
Share
By
Laura
French
(Credit: Tada Images – stock.adobe.com)
Thousands of ASUS routers have been compromised with malware-free backdoors in an ongoing campaign to potentially build a future botnet,
GreyNoise reported Wednesday
.
The threat actors abuse security vulnerabilities and legitimate router features to establish persistent access without the use of malware, and these backdoors survive both reboots and firmware updates, making them difficult to remove.
The attacks, which researchers suspect are conducted by highly sophisticated threat actors, were first detected by GreyNoise’s AI-powered Sift tool in mid-March and disclosed Thursday after coordination with government officials and industry partners.
Sekoia.io also reported the compromise of thousands of ASUS routers in their
investigation of a broader campaign
, dubbed ViciousTrap, in which edge devices from other brands were also compromised to create a honeypot network.
Sekoia.io found that the ASUS routers were not used to create honeypots, and that the threat actors gained SSH access using the same port, TCP/53282, identified by GreyNoise in their report.
Attackers gain access, execute commands via known vulnerabilities
The backdoor campaign targets multiple ASUS router models, with GreyNoise initially detecting attack attempts against their emulated ASUS RT-AC3200 and RT-AC3100 firmware profiles, both with “out-of-the-box” configuration settings.
Initial access is gained through a combination of credential brute-forcing and exploitation of authentication bypass flaws, which are patched but have not been assigned CVEs, according to GreyNoise.
Authentication bypass techniques used include impersonation of the ASUS user-agent “asusrouter--” and the use of an “asus_token=” cookie followed by a null byte, which may prematurely terminate string parsing during the authentication process and lead to authentication bypass on vulnerable systems,
according to GreyNoise’s technical analysis
.
Sekoia.io also noted the exploitation of
CVE-2021-32030
in
their observations
, an authentication bypass flaw specifically affecting ASUS GT-AC2900 and Lyra Mini devices.
Once the attacker gains authenticated access, they exploit built-in settings and security flaws to establish an SSH connection at TCP/53282 along with an attacker-controlled public key for persistent, remote access.
On ASUS RT-AX55 models that have not received a patch for the vulnerability tracked as
CVE-2023-39780
, the attackers exploit this command injection vulnerability to activate an embedded logging feature called Bandwidth SQLite Logging (BWSQL). Code used by this logging feature allows for the execution of user-controlled data, expanding the attacker’s ability to inject malicious commands.
Factory reset recommended for compromised devices
The backdoor configuration in these attacks is stored in non-volatile random access memory (NVRAM) rather than the disk, making it resistant to removal via reboots or firmware upgrades.
“If a router was compromised before updating, the backdoor will still be present unless SSH access is explicitly reviewed and removed,” GreyNoise stated.
GreyNoise recommends users perform a full factory reset and manual reconfiguration on any device suspected to be compromised. Users can check if their device was compromised by checking for SSH access on TCP/53282 and for unauthorized entries in the authorized_keys file.
Organizations should also block the known malicious IP addresses identified in GreyNoise’s and Sekoia.io’s reports and ensure their devices are fully updated to patch any security vulnerabilities that may be used by the attackers.

data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 数千台华硕家用和小型办公室路由器正遭受隐秘后门攻击，攻击者利用已修复的漏洞获得设备管理权限，安装公共加密密钥以通过SSH访问设备。该后门即使在设备重启或固件更新后仍能存留，使攻击者能够长期控制受感染设备。研究人员发现全球约9,000台设备被感染，受感染设备通过特定端口和数字证书登录。用户可通过检查SSH设置和系统日志来判断是否被感染，并通过删除相关密钥和端口设置来移除后门。攻击者可能与某国有关，目前尚未利用这些设备进行活动。

Thousands of home and small office routers manufactured by Asus are being infected with a stealthy backdoor that can survive reboots and firmware updates in an attack by a nation-state or another well-resourced threat actor, researchers said.
The unknown attackers gain access to the devices by exploiting now-patched vulnerabilities, some of which have never been tracked through the internationally recognized CVE system. After gaining unauthorized administrative control of the devices, the threat actor installs a public encryption key for access to the device through SSH. From then on, anyone with the private key can automatically log in to the device with administrative system rights.
Durable control
“‍The attacker’s access survives both reboots and firmware updates, giving them durable control over affected devices,” researchers from security firm GreyNoise
reported Wednesday
. “The attacker maintains long-term access without dropping malware or leaving obvious traces by chaining authentication bypasses, exploiting a known vulnerability, and abusing legitimate configuration features.”
GreyNoise said it has tracked roughly 9,000 devices around the world that have been backdoored in the ongoing campaign. That number continues to grow. Company researchers said they have no indication that the threat actor has deployed the infected devices in any activity. Rather, the hacks appear to be the beginning stages of the threat actor amassing a large number of compromised devices for future use.
GreyNoise said it detected the campaign in mid-March and held off reporting on it until after the company notified unnamed government agencies. That detail further suggests that the threat actor may have some connection to a nation-state.
The company researchers went on to say that the activity they observed was part of a larger campaign
reported last week
by fellow security company Sekoia. Researchers at Sekoia said that Internet scanning by network intelligence firm Censys suggested as many as
9,500 Asus routers
may have been compromised by ViciousTrap, the name used to track the unknown threat actor.
The attackers are backdooring the devices by exploiting multiple vulnerabilities. One is CVE-2023-39780, a command-injection flaw that allows for the execution of system commands, which Asus patched in a recent firmware update, GreyNoise said. The remaining vulnerabilities have also been patched but, for unknown reasons, have not received CVE tracking designations.
The only way for router users to determine whether their devices are infected is by checking the SSH settings in the configuration panel. Infected routers will show that the device can be logged in to by SSH over port 53282 using a digital certificate with a truncated key of: ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAABIwAAAQEAo41nBoVFfj4HlVMGV+YPsxMDrMlbdDZ...
To remove the backdoor, infected users should remove the key and the port setting.
People can also determine if they’ve been targeted if system logs indicate that they have been accessed through the IP addresses 101.99.91[.]151, 101.99.94[.]173, 79.141.163[.]179, or 111.90.146[.]237. Users of any router brand should always ensure their devices receive security updates in a timely manner.

data.title: I taught my 3-year-old to read like a 9-year-old
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者如何通过辅导，使自己三岁的孩子达到九岁孩子的阅读水平。作者通过系统教学，使孩子能够阅读如《霍比特人》这样的书籍片段，但仍有限制，如对某些词汇和暴力情节的处理。作者采用SDQA测试评估孩子的阅读水平，结果显示其阅读能力相当于三四年级学生。文章强调，真正值得关注的阅读里程碑是孩子是否能从中获得乐趣，因为早期自主阅读与认知能力提升和心理健康改善密切相关。研究显示，早期阅读还能促进大脑发育。此外，作者提到早期阅读不仅能替代屏幕时间，还具有显著的育儿优势，如提高孩子自我娱乐能力和情绪调节能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：早期儿童教育，特别是阅读能力的培养及其利弊

不同观点：
• **bitshiftfaced**：认为过早让孩子进行学术学习（如阅读）可能剥夺他们进行创造性、社交和情感调节等方面学习的机会。这些非学术性的学习对孩子同样重要，有助于他们的全面发展。
• **randunel**：孩子的学习能力和进度主要取决于孩子自身，而非家长的教学能力。即使是同一家庭、教学方式相同，不同孩子的发育和学习速度也可能大不相同。家长只需提供足够的关注和陪伴。
• **j2kun**：每个孩子感兴趣的领域不同，家长应该尝试不同的方法来激发孩子的兴趣。阅读并不是激活孩子大脑的唯一方式，现代的娱乐方式多样化，使得阅读的吸引力降低。
• **flkiwi**：通过自家孩子的例子说明，孩子可以通过自我驱动学习阅读，且早期阅读能力强可以带来一定的育儿便利。同时强调，孩子的个体差异和复杂思维能力在很早就会显现出来。
• **WillAdams**：讨论如何维持孩子的学习轨迹，提出按能力分班是一种有效的解决方案，但在实际操作中受到学校规模和预算的限制。
• **sixtram**：分享了自己教五岁孩子在三个月内学会阅读的经验，并指出语言的音素正字特性（如匈牙利语）使得阅读教学更加容易。
• **xkriva11**：引用Alan Kay的例子，说明过早学会阅读可能导致孩子对学校教育产生质疑和抵触。
• **acquisitionsilk**：对在互联网上展示孩子成就的行为持批评态度，强调学校教育系统的不足，推荐Grace Llewellyn和John Holt的教育理论。
• **explorigin**：认为孩子之间的差异是自然存在的，不能用统一的标准来衡量。家长应根据孩子的实际情况来爱护和培养他们。
• **nathell**：通过自身经验说明，早期学会阅读是可能的，且对成年后的生活没有明显的负面影响。
• **schnitzelstoat**：认为阅读是最重要的儿童技能，因为阅读能力不足会影响孩子其他学科的学习。
• **jacknews**：质疑早期阅读能力的实际理解效果，认为阅读的意义在于理解内容，而非仅仅发出声音。
• **toolslive**：认为过早让孩子学会阅读可能导致他们在小学阶段感到无聊，建议将精力转向学校不教授的技能（如棋类、音乐等）。
• **wat10000**：批评那些自认为在教育上有卓越成就的家长，认为孩子的成就更多是由于自身能力，而非家长的教学技巧，家长不应自视过高。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于早期学术教育（特别是阅读）的利弊，以及家长在孩子学习过程中所起的作用。一些评论认为早期阅读能够带来长远的好处，而另一些评论则担心这可能剥夺孩子其他方面的发展机会，且可能导致孩子在学校的无聊和不适应。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是孩子个体差异的重要性，强调不能用统一的标准来衡量所有孩子的发展和学习能力。

Art for
The Intrinsic Perspective
is by
Alexander Naughton
Over a year has passed since I began teaching my toddler—then two years old—how to read (a process
chronicled here
).
Now, I’m prepared to answer a burning scientific question that has kept absolutely zero researchers up at night: Can a three-year-old read
The Hobbit
?
Turns out: yeah, pretty much. Here’s Roman reading from Chapter 1:
In a hole, in the ground, there lived a hobbit. Not a nasty, dirty, wet hole, filled with the ends of worms and an oozy smell, nor yet a dry bare, sandy, hole, with nothing in it to sit down on or to eat: it was a hobbit-hole, and that means comfort.
Of course, there are still plenty of words he can’t read! While he could handle a lot of
The Hobbit
, I haven’t let him read the whole book himself (there’s too much violence, and the small font size, confusing names, and enough unknown words would likely wear him down). But for the class of books that he has any business reading alone, like early readers and chapter books, he can do so. He reads by himself for pleasure every day now, quickly and silently plowing through his growing library, and his decoding abilities have met the limits of his comprehension.
As you can tell, I’m quite proud of how well he’s done, to the degree I risk coming across as supercilious about the whole thing (now there’s a word he probably can’t read). A few months ago, I gave him the
SDQA test
, a simple way of determining reading level, and he got all the 3rd-grade-level words correct (so somewhere around eight or nine-year-olds).
Estimating reading level isn’t very meaningful from a practical perspective, however. Goodhart’s law of measures becoming targets has made vicious work of education. For example,
in a study
wherein researchers had college students read the first few paragraphs of Charles Dickens’
Bleak House
, only 5% of English majors could passably describe what was going on.
Instead, I think the only literacy milestone worth caring about is whether a child reads for pleasure, because…
Read for pleasure, make brain big.
In the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD) project, a cohort of over 10,000 children in the US was tracked longitudinally. A 2023
analysis of the data
revealed that the earlier a child was reading for pleasure, the more this correlated with higher scores on cognitive tests
and
lower numbers of mental health issues, even after controlling for things like socio-economic status, such that…
…cognitive performance was better and the mental problems were lower in young adolescents with higher levels of early RfP [reading for pleasure].
Here is years of reading for pleasure plotted against a number of such outcomes.
Sun et al. (2023)
In fact, the researchers found that reading for pleasure—and the more years spent doing so—may literally lead to larger brain volumes in adolescence.
Sun et al. (2023)
(note how the effects are non-localized)
The positive effects showed up after controlling for genetics (as best one can, using genome-wide analyses in the full cohort). ABCD also had a participating set of 711 twins and, interestingly, estimations from the twin data revealed that, while early reading-for-pleasure does have a genetic component, the majority of the trait’s variance appears environmental.
Put it all together, and early reading for pleasure stands out in the scientific literature, in that it has (a) very broad cognitive benefits, (b) good empirical support for this class of thing, (c) has a large environmental component, and (d) actively replaces and competes with screen time, which is usually neutral or negative in the literature (in the ABCD cohort, screen time had an inverse correlation with reading for pleasure).
Subscribe
This last point, that reading for pleasure fills a certain time in the day, means I daily…
Thank god for this new independent activity.
When I look back on my official reasons for teaching reading so early, oh, how naive I was! All pale in comparison to the true benefit.
Holy smokes, does early reading make parenting easier sometimes!
It’s all the advantages of an iPad, none of the guilt. You’ve unlocked
infinite self-entertainment
. Long drive? Bring a book. Or five. Roman toddles into restaurants clutching a book as a backup activity, and reads while waiting in boring lines. It’s also calming, and so helps with emotional regulation. Toddler energy descending rapidly into deviance? Go read a book! It’s a parenting cheat code. I don’t know if this alone justifies the hours spent, but it sure is one heck of a benefit.

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust编程中错误消息的处理，强调了错误信息应提供更多细节以帮助用户解决问题，而不仅仅是简单地返回“错误”或“失败”。文章通过一个计数程序的例子，展示了如何改进错误处理，使用`Result`和`?`运算符捕获并返回错误。此外，文章还讲解了如何以更友好的方式向用户展示错误信息，避免直接显示给程序员的调试信息。最后，提出了将错误信息输出到标准错误流，并根据程序状态设置退出代码的最佳实践，以提高命令行程序的健壮性和用户友好性。

“It doesn’t work” is the least helpful bug report you could ever get,

what

say more than just something like “error” or ”failed”.
Oddly enough, though, most programmers don’t give a great deal of
thought to error messages, or how they’re presented to users. Worse,
they often don’t even anticipate that an error
could
happen,
and so the program does something even worse than printing a meaningless
error: it prints nothing at all.

realised that our line-counting program doesn’t cope well with errors

hang

function returns it immediately. Otherwise, this statement has no
effect, and we move on to increment the counter and continue the
loop.
This passes the test that simulates a read error, so let’s see if the
real program now also behaves correctly. We’ll need to update
main
for the new signature of
count_lines
,
because right now we have a compile error:
`std::result::Result<usize, std::io::Error>` doesn't implement
`std::fmt::Display`
In other words, we tried to print the return value of
count_lines
using the
println!
macro, which
uses the
Display
trait to ask the value how it should be
formatted as a string.
Result
doesn’t implement
Display
, because there
isn’t
really a sensible
default way to print a
Result
, so Rust requires us to
implement the trait manually if that’s what we want to do.

That seems like overkill for this simple program, so let’s just use
the
?
formatting parameter for now, which will give us the
“programmer’s view” of the value, using the
Debug
trait:
fn
main()
{
let
lines
=
count_lines(stdin()
.
lock())

println!
(
"{lines:?} lines"
)
;
}

interested in what users see when an error happens, so let’s trigger

cargo run <.
Err(Os { code: 21, kind: IsADirectory, message: "Is a directory" })
A bit wonky, but this is the
debug
format, which is intended
for the programmer’s eyes only, so that’s fine.
A slightly nicer
presentation
Let’s go ahead and spare the user the more excruciating details:

main()
{
let
res
=
count_lines(stdin()

lock())
;
match
res
{
Ok
(lines)
=>
println!
(
"{lines} lines"
)
,
Err
(e)
=>
println!
(
"{e}"
)
,
}
}
Unlike
Result

Err
is
Display
, meaning it knows how to format itself in a
(relatively) user-friendly way. Here’s the output:
Is a directory (os error 21)
That’s good enough. It tells the user what’s wrong, without too much
wonky syntax or detail: “Hey, it looks like you’re trying to count lines
in a directory, and that doesn’t really make sense. Try something
else.”

useful, and flexible. The first step in that direction is knowing when
to expect errors, and the second is figuring out what to do when they
happen.

status
Let’s add one more refinement before we move on. It’s a useful
convention for command-line programs to print their error messages to
the
standard error
stream, not the standard output. That way,
if the normal output is being redirected to some file, error messages
will still go to the user’s terminal, not the file.

exit status

program is being used in a shell script, for example, the abnormal exit

44125606.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust编程中错误消息的处理，强调了错误信息应提供更多细节以帮助用户解决问题，而不仅仅是简单地返回“错误”或“失败”。文章通过一个计数程序的例子，展示了如何改进错误处理，使用`Result`和`?`运算符捕获并返回错误。此外，文章还讲解了如何以更友好的方式向用户展示错误信息，避免直接显示给程序员的调试信息。最后，提出了将错误信息输出到标准错误流，并根据程序状态设置退出代码的最佳实践，以提高命令行程序的健壮性和用户友好性。

主要讨论点：欧盟创业环境中的官僚主义和资金申请问题

不同观点：
• RugnirViking认为当前的创业环境非常糟糕，充斥着层层的欺诈行为，许多公司试图依赖政府资金生存。他指出，欧盟通过增加官僚程序来应对问题，但这反而助长了欺诈公司的行为，使得真正想创业的人更难获得支持。
• 他还提到，申请欧盟资助往往需要找一个专门处理文件的合作伙伴，而这些人通常要求从资助中分得一大笔费用。

补充讨论：
• RugnirViking强调了创业环境中存在的系统性问题，尤其是与政府和欧盟资金相关的复杂程序，使得创业变得更加困难。
• 他指出了具体的问题：申请程序的繁琐和外部合作伙伴在资助申请过程中的角色，这增加了创业成本和复杂性。
• 争议的焦点在于如何简化资助申请程序，减少欺诈行为，并为真正的创业者提供更好的支持。RugnirViking似乎认为增加官僚程序并不是解决问题的有效方法。

data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 文章作者Juha-Matti Santala分享了作为一名软件开发者，他认为最重要的工具是笔和笔记本。虽然编写代码是开发的核心部分，但更重要的是思考如何解决问题和设计方案。作者发现，在电脑前工作时很难进行深度思考，因此他常通过笔记本手写和画图来理清思路、设计UI或解决代码问题。写作帮助他将抽象想法具体化，并发现知识盲点和代码错误。此外，这种方法还留下思考过程的记录，便于日后回顾。作者鼓励通过写作促进思维，并希望与更多人展开深入讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：笔记本与数字工具在开发、设计和日常工作中的应用与效果

不同观点：
• **ednite**：认为工具本身（笔记本或数字工具）不是关键，重要的是改变工具或方式可以刺激大脑以不同的方式集中注意力、激发创造力和增强记忆。他通过改变晚间活动（从编码到写作）获得了大脑的"重启"效果，并认为计划时从数字工具切换到纸笔也能带来类似的效果。

• **sky2224**：指出一些高智商的数学、物理和计算机科学家只用打印纸和笔，且用完即弃，认为笔记对个人长期作用不大。如果需要分享，会将重要内容记录到文档中。他强调这种方式并不适合所有人，并认为讨论不应局限于字面意义，而是分享一种哲学，不应强迫别人接受。

• **js4ever**：反对将笔记本称为开发者“最重要的工具”，认为这是浪漫化。他认为笔记本对某些人有用，但不能与调试器、版本控制或CI等工具的重要性相比，强调软件工程的实际需求。

• **kstenerud**：认为讨论过度集中在纸笔的物理层面，而忽略了作者提出的核心原则，即避免在设计时陷入“执行模式”。他强调保持设计与执行的平衡才是关键，具体工具取决于个人选择。

• **adampwells**：作为有多年经验的软件工程师，他因患有无法视觉化事物的心盲症（aphantasia），依赖纸笔或白板进行ERD、思维导图和序列图的绘制。他认为纸笔对他的成功至关重要，反驳了认为纸笔是“浪漫化”的观点。

• **voilavilla**：支持在编码前进行思考，并分享了自己作为高级软件架构师的经验。在高层次设计中，使用的工具如Visio、Word、PowerPoint和PlantUML比具体的代码实现更为重要，强调抽象层次越高，工具越简单。

补充讨论：
• **bufferoverflow**：质疑纸笔的效率，认为书写慢、搜索困难，且难以复制和分享内容。

• **unsungNovelty**：结合数字和纸质笔记的优点，长期笔记保存在数字应用中，短期思考过程记录在笔记本中，认为这种方式有助于记忆和回顾。

• **Brajeshwar**：偏爱书写，尤其喜欢使用特定品牌的笔记本和钢笔，享受书写过程中的触感和体验。

• **jandrewrogers**：习惯使用工程纸和铅笔解决复杂的软件设计问题，认为纸笔在非线性和任意访问模式上更有效，而计算机UI则限制了这种灵活性。

• **CommenterPerson**：作为SQL数据分析师，认为笔记在处理未记录或记录不良的数据库和业务流程时至关重要，虽然以前使用纸张，但现在依赖OneNote，尽管不喜欢。在商务会议中，共享屏幕和简要的数字笔记能有效聚焦需求。

争议焦点：
• 纸笔与数字工具的效率和适用场景。
• 笔记本是否应被视为开发者最重要的工具，或只是浪漫化的看法。
• 个人经验和习惯对工具选择的影响，以及是否应推广某种工具或方法。

44113210.article_content:
As a developer, my most important tools are a pen and a notebook
May 28th, 2025
by
Juha-Matti Santala
(
Mastodon
@hamatti@hamatti.org
)
This was published in categories:
notes
dev
After I signed my contract to join my new job a month ago, I was so excited.
Not only that I would join the company but also because I got to buy a new
notebook. The weekend before my first day I headed to the local bookstore and
spent a good amount of time browsing through the notebooks available and ended
up with this happy orange one.
Why am I so excited about a notebook then?
Because it’s the most important tool I have as a software developer.
When it comes to building software or solving problems, writing code is the
necessary bit at the end where we tell the computer what to do but way more
important than writing that code is figuring out what code to write.
I learned very early on in my career that I’m not very good at thinking when
I’m at a computer. When I have my code editor open, I’m in a “function mode”
where I write stuff that does something. When my brain hits that mode, there’s
not much creative energies flowing around.
So I often step away from the computer. Sometimes it’s for walks (I tend to
work at companies near water features so I’ve used to go for strolls near San
Francisco Bay, Spree or the best of them all, Aurajoki) but often I take my
notebook and sit on a couch or outside at the patio and ponder.
I might be thinking of initial solutions to new problems (ie. designing how to
approach it, drawing UI sketches or flowcharts) or I’m helping myself
understand the flow of data and interactions in the current code base to
figure out how to fix a bug or add new functionality.
Writing (and sketching) is such a powerful tool for thinking in that. It helps
me turn my vague abstract ideas into tangible artefacts through words and
drawings. It helps me expose the gaps in my knowledge or understanding because
I can’t skip them as easily when writing as I can when just thinking about
them.
When I’ve written code, I like to write about it as if I would be explaining
it to someone else. Whenever possible, I like to publish them as blog posts as
well but even when it’s not possible, writing it that way helps me find
inconsistencies, bad designs and even mistakes in my code. I’ve written about
how writing is my favourite refactoring tool
.
A lovely side benefit of thinking through writing is that it leaves behind a
copy of my thoughts and the process of how I reached them. I don’t have to
separately go and write notes because my thinking process already created most
of them and I usually just reorganise and polish them a bit to make them more
useful in the future as well.
That way, if someone asks what I was thinking about when I did X two weeks,
six months or two years ago, I can go back to my notes and tell them exactly
that. (Spoilers: quite often that someone is me in the future.)
I also have a longer post about
how I take work notes as a developer
that focuses more on the content of my notes.
If something above resonated with you, let's start a discussion about it!
Email me at juhamattisantala at gmail dot com and share your thoughts
. In 2025, I want to have more deeper discussions with people from around the world and I'd love if you'd be part of that.

data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为"Space Selfie"的免费活动，参与者可以通过上传自拍，由名为SAT GUS的卫星将自拍与地球合影，并传回地球。该活动由Mark Rober发起，SAT GUS卫星得名于CrunchLabs的松鼠 mascot Phat Gus。文章还解答了常见问题，如卫星如何升空、自拍安全性、照片格式、活动免费性及参与者范围、照片返回时间、卫星追踪方法、相机类型，以及为何自拍中不见星星和云层差异等。活动旨在让更多人体验太空主题的夏季活动。

data.title: WeatherStar 4000+: Weather Channel Simulator
data.author: adam_gyroscope
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了WeatherStar 4000+系统（v5.21.2）的天气预报界面。用户可输入位置查看当前天气情况和每小时预报，包括温度、风力、云量和降水概率等信息。还提供旅行预报、区域观测、日出日落时间、风暴预测等功能。用户可以复制链接分享天气信息，并根据需要调整显示设置。当前系统版本为5.21.2，提供详细的气象数据和图表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：复刻90年代Weather Channel天气预报图形设备（WeatherStar 4000）及相关技术、文化讨论

不同观点：
• [ndiddy] 介绍了一个通过重写固件来复刻90年代天气预报图形的项目，解释了由于原版固件丢失，通过新固件在真实硬件上模拟出90年代天气预报的实现。该项目在YouTube上有直播流。
• [gasgiant] 提到自己曾认为Pat Metheny Group的音乐优于Weather Channel的背景音乐，但在酒店房间偶然听到"Last Train Home"后改变了看法，显示出对Weather Channel音乐的认可。
• [socalgal2] 原本期待"Weather Channel Simulator"是通过AI生成天气主播视频，而不是复刻90年代的图形，暗示了对未来技术发展的期望。
• [post_break] 分享了自己使用树莓派和3D打印显示器模拟CRT显示器的经验，并提供了相关资源链接，但由于频率问题放弃了使用真实CRT显示器。
• [jader201] 调侃只有当背景播放The Rippingtons的音乐时，才是真正的90年代Weather Channel体验，强调了音乐在氛围中的重要性。

补充讨论：
• [jasonpeacock] 提出在URL中存储选项（尤其是自助服务终端模式）的建议，并希望通过<esc>键退出自助服务终端模式，关注用户体验的改进。
• [volleygman180] 对背景音乐表示关注，并认为添加声音开关按钮是完美的设计。
• [doawoo] 提到自己拥有在SGI O2上运行的类似软件，并计划将其上传到存档位置，提供了软件资源的另一种可能。
• [Vitamin_Sushi] 表达了对WS4000的喜爱，并计划将其作为一个侧项目在Firestick上实现，显示出对技术学习的热情。
• [barbazoo] 以调侃的语气表示对该项目的喜爱，体现出对复古技术的欣赏。
• [noduerme] 报告了在Android手机上浏览该页面时出现的崩溃问题，指出了技术实现中的潜在缺陷。
• [crims0n] 分享了自己在自助服务终端模式下的体验，并联想到CRT显示器的氛围，表达了对复古体验的满意。
• [lordfrito] 感叹该项目让他回想起过去网络的乐趣，表现出对过去网络文化的怀念。
• [kylehotchkiss] 以幽默的方式询问"赞助内容在哪里？"，暗示对现代广告渗透的不满。

争议焦点：
- 对复刻90年代天气预报图形的真实性和完整性存在不同期待，例如对背景音乐的讨论和AI生成视频的设想。
- 技术实现中的用户体验问题，如Android手机上的崩溃问题和自助服务终端模式的改进建议。

data.title: The flip phone web: browsing with the original Opera Mini
data.author: protonbob
data.article_summary: Opera Mini是2005年发布的一款移动浏览器，最初通过将网页加载任务交由外部服务器处理，使得功能较弱的手机也能浏览完整网站。在智能手机普及前，它非常受欢迎，但随着智能手机的普及，其独特性逐渐减弱。如今，Opera Mini仍适用于iPhone和Android，但已不再是必需品。最初的Java ME版本仍可运行，甚至能在现代电脑上使用。Opera Mini通过云服务器渲染网页并压缩数据，以减少流量消耗。尽管其用户数量在2012年达到1.69亿，但随着手机性能提升，使用需求下降。用户可通过修改浏览器用户代理字符串下载旧版Opera Mini，并在桌面使用Java运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Opera Mini的历史、功能、影响以及与现代浏览器的比较

不同观点：
• **怀旧与历史价值**：
  - iamjackg和nfriedly回忆早期使用Opera Mini的经历，强调其在限制数据流量和无WiFi年代的革命性作用。
  - fidotron提到Opera Mini出现的时代背景，包括WAP/WML的失败和iMode在日本的成功。
  - jbverschoor回忆在日本移动市场的见闻，尤其是对QR码和日本手机的兴趣。

• **技术演进与挑战**：
  - fidotron详细描述了Opera Mini的技术演进，尤其是在2005年和2007年的重要更新。
  - lysace补充了Opera Mini服务的技术细节，并提到其参与开发的经历。

• **现代应用与局限性**：
  - FridayoLeary分享了最近使用Opera Mini的体验，认为尽管其技术过时，但在某些方面（如无广告浏览）仍优于现代浏览器。
  - 强调了Opera Mini只能加载静态元素，无法处理现代网页的复杂功能。

• **经济与市场因素**：
  - BlueTemplar讨论了数据费用和设备兼容性问题，提到2005年数据费用可能很高，并分享了自己在Nokia N75/N95上的使用体验。
  - 提及Razr手机和数据速度的提升对浏览体验的影响。
